packets.implementation: 1. rules/Cargo.toml: `[package] name = "glia-rules"`, `version.workspace = true`, `edition = "2024"`, `publish = false`, description 'Domain-free Datalog rule evaluator: a string-named rule IR, one lexer shared by the Datalog surface and the GQL read subset, analysis, a planner, levelled semi-naive evaluation over sorted batches, reaches / scc builtins over activation::algo, provenance and explain, grouped aggregates and magic sets; its fact seam is FactSource: GraphSource. Query-time: no stored derived edges.' (never the text toy-domain); `[dependencies] glia-core = { path = "../core" }` and `glia-activation = { path = "../activation" }`, each with a one-line comment; no other table. 2. rules/src/lib.rs: a `//!` crate doc (the paragraph above plus 'The API is reached by module path: glia_rules::eval::evaluate, glia_rules::parser::parse_program, glia_rules::source::FactSource. Every hash map is value::Lookup (no iteration API); evaluation is single-threaded; output rows sort by rendered values.'), then `pub mod` lines for analysis, diag, eval, explain, ir, lexer, parser, source, testkit, value, gql and `mod` lines for aggregate, closure, exec, magic, plan, relation, strata, each preceded by a one-line `///` naming its purpose and owner; no `use`, no re-export, no item. 3. One doc-only file per module, each exactly one `//!` paragraph ending 'Filled by <owner>.' and no item: `analysis` (DA.5b: name and type resolution against the Catalog, safety / range restriction, arity, negation and aggregate checks, the diagnostic message table); `diag` (DA.2: spans, diagnostics and RulesError); `eval` (DA.14b: evaluate / run: lazy EDB loading, the magic rewrite, levelled semi-naive evaluation per stratum, the row budget); `explain` (DA.15: Evaluation::explain: the minimal-height derivation at a row's tier as a Witness); `ir` (DA.2: the string-named rule IR (Program / Rule / Atom / Term / Aggregate / Comparison) and the Catalog); `lexer` (DA.4: the one tokenizer for the Datalog surface and the GQL read subset); `parser` (DA.9: the Datalog surface parser into the IR, with spans and diagnostics); `source` (DA.6: the FactSource: GraphSource trait, the Builtin trait and MemSource); `testkit` (DA.13: deterministic MemSource graph builders for the crate's tests and gates); `value` (DA.3: the Tier lattice, Value / ValueRef, the per-evaluation ValueTable and Lookup); `aggregate` (DA.8: grouped count / min / max / sum as a stratum operator); `closure` (DA.11: the reaches / scc builtins over activation::algo); `exec` (DA.14a: the step interpreter behind evaluation, aggregates and explain); `magic` (DA.12: the magic-sets / demand rewrite for unseeded recursion); `plan` (DA.10: per-stratum rule plans: semi-naive variants, bound-first order, index choice); `relation` (DA.7: sorted, deduplicated batch storage with permuted key indexes); `strata` (DA.5a: stratification of the predicate dependency graph over activation::algo::cycles); and rules/src/gql/mod.rs ('The GQL read subset (MATCH .. WHERE .. RETURN, aggregates, ORDER BY, LIMIT) parsed over the shared lexer and lowered to the rule IR (Q4: set semantics, edge homomorphism). DB.7a declares ast.rs and parser.rs here, DB.7b lower.rs; there is no second lexer. Filled by DB.7a (+DB.7b).'). Doc-only private modules compile with 0 warnings (no item, so no dead_code; the 0.5.0 / 0.5.1 slots were the same shape). 4. Cargo.toml: the member line as in entry_points (the `[workspace.package] version` stays 0.5.1 - the bump is the release step, after DZ). 5. engine/Cargo.toml: `# 0.5.2 (D0.2): engine::rules (DB) evaluates rules over glia-rules. A path dependency with no external crate; engine/Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are hashed, so PARSER_STAMP moves once, here.` + `glia-rules = { path = "../rules" }` after glia-activation. Nothing in the engine uses it until DB.2a (an unused path dependency is not a warning: unused_crate_dependencies is allow-by-default). 6. `cargo check --workspace` writes Cargo.lock (glia-rules 0.5.1 with glia-core / glia-activation; glia-engine's list gains glia-rules); no existing package version may move. 7. `bash scripts/check-engram-export.sh --update-lock` copies the re-resolved engram-export/Cargo.lock over the tracked one. 8. stamp/build.rs is NOT edited (rules/ stays out of HASHED_ROOTS: R1 section 2.2, Q8). packets.title: activation::algo::reach::bfs_levels - the levelled multi-source BFS (per-edge and per-seed levels, a membership mask, rank-ordered frontiers) behind the rules layer's 3-level tier closure
packets.area: DA reaches / scc builtins - levelled BFS substrate
packets.rationale: R1 section 4.3 defines a reached node's tier as the first of three passes (FACT edges only, then +DERIVED, then all) that reaches it, exact and O(3(V+E)). The algorithm is generic (levels are small integers the caller assigns), so by the standing rule it lives in activation::algo over Adjacency, not in rules/ or engine. VERIFIED at HEAD 22c65ee: activation/src/algo/reach.rs has `bfs`, `reachable`, `reachable_by` only (`grep -n 'fn bfs_levels\|LevelReached' -r activation/src` prints nothing); `bfs` walks every kept edge of the index, and the per-edge position the rules layer needs to tier a hop (`Inc.edge`, activation/src/algo/mod.rs) is private, so a caller outside activation cannot filter a walk by edge tier. The workaround without this packet is one Adjacency per level per category set: at glia x10 the carry index alone holds 424,465 kept edges (verifier, HEAD 22c65ee: the R1 spike binary over a `glia analyze --format json` dump of a git-archive copy of HEAD, scaled x10 = 257,680 nodes / 826,755 edges, carry/2 = 424,465 rows; R1's 0.5.0-era figure was 301,773), about 20 MB per Adjacency (two 12-byte incidences per kept edge, the id vector, the id map and the CSR starts), so three levels x three category sets (carry, IMPORTS, CALLS) is ~180 MB - more than the whole RSS gate of 150 MB at glia x10 (R1 section 9 spike 1). One Adjacency per category set plus a `[u8]` level per kept edge costs one byte per kept edge instead. Two more needs fold into the same walk: scc levels (DA.11) walk forward and backward from a component's representative WITHOUT leaving the component (a membership mask keeps it O(component)), and checkout-stable witnesses (R1 section 10) need a node's parent to be the lowest-RANKED node one layer up, not the first discovered, because discovery follows edge order and edge order follows path-derived NodeIds. impact(activation::src::algo::reach::bfs, backward, depth 1) lists 24 callers (engine trace / effects / implementors / why, graph traversal / blast): this packet adds a function and two structs and changes none of them.

The plan puts the GQL parser in DB, so this lexer is a published API DB's GQL parser consumes: it must tokenize `MATCH (a:ROUTE)-[:CALLS|USES*1..3]->(b) WHERE a.qname STARTS WITH 'x' RETURN a, count(b)` and `->{1,3}` / `<-[` as well as `p(x) :- q(x, "A"), !r(x).`. packets.implementation:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum TokenKind {
    Ident(String), Str(String), Int(i64),
    LParen, RParen, LBracket, RBracket, LBrace, RBrace,
    Comma, Dot, DotDot, Colon, ColonDash /* :- */, Semicolon, Pipe, Star, Plus, Minus, Question,
    Arrow /* -> */, LeftArrow /* <- */, Bang, Eq, Ne /* != or <> */, Lt, Le, Gt, Ge, Dollar /* GQL parameters: lexed so DB's GQL parser can refuse them by name */, Eof,
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct Token { pub kind: TokenKind, pub span: Span }
pub fn lex(source: SourceId, source_name: &str, text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Token>, RulesError>;   // RulesError::Parse on any lexical error; the Vec ends with Eof
```
Rules: identifiers [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* (keywords are idents; DB's GQL parser compares them case-insensitively, the Datalog parser reads `not` / `count` / `min` / `max` / `sum` by position); a lone `_` is Ident("_") (the parser makes it Term::Wild). Integers are decimal digits only (no floats, so `1..3` lexes Int DotDot Int); overflow past i64::MAX is an error. A leading minus is a separate Minus token (the parser folds `-` Int into a negative literal); `<-` lexes greedily as LeftArrow, so a Datalog comparison with a negative constant needs a space (`a < -1`), documented in the module doc. Strings take '...' or "..." with escapes \\ \" \' \n \t; any other escape, a raw newline inside a string, or end of input inside one is an error at the opening quote. Comments: `//` to end of line and `/* ... */` (unterminated block comment = error at its start). Spans: byte offsets from char_indices (never slicing mid-char), line 1-based, col = 1 + chars since the line start (UTF-8 safe); Windows CRLF counts as one line break. Errors: up to 20 Diagnostics (each "unexpected character `@`", "unterminated string", "integer out of range") are collected before returning Parse(diags), so one bad char does not hide the next. No HashMap, no allocation per token beyond the Ident / Str payload.
packets.acceptance: Unit tests in rules/src/lexer.rs: (1) datalog_rule_tokens - `p(x) :- q(x, "A"), !r(x), x != 3.` lexes to the exact TokenKind sequence [Ident p, LParen, Ident x, RParen, ColonDash, Ident q, LParen, Ident x, Comma, Str A, RParen, Comma, Bang, Ident r, LParen, Ident x, RParen, Comma, Ident x, Ne, Int 3, Dot, Eof]; (2) gql_pattern_tokens - `MATCH (a:ROUTE)-[:CALLS|USES*1..3]->(b) WHERE a.qname STARTS WITH 'x' RETURN a, count(b)` lexes to the exact sequence (Minus LBracket Colon Ident Pipe Ident Star Int DotDot Int RBracket Arrow ...), and `(a)<-[:T]-(b)` and `->{1,3}` produce LeftArrow / Arrow LBrace Int Comma Int RBrace; (3) spans_count_chars - in `"é" x` on line 2 the token x has line 2, col 5 and byte start 6 (the é is two bytes); CRLF input reports the same line numbers as LF; (4) comments_and_escapes - `// c\n/* b */ "a\\\"b"` yields Str(`a\"b`); (5) lexical_errors_are_located - an unterminated string opened at line 2 col 5 gives Parse with one Diagnostic whose Display is `rules:2:5: error: unterminated string`; `99999999999999999999` gives "integer out of range"; two bad characters give two diagnostics; (6) ne_spellings - `!=` and `<>` both lex to Ne; `<=` / `>=` / `->` / `<-` / `:-` / `..` are single tokens; `$p` lexes to Dollar, Ident p. RE-MEASURED today (R1 spike binary, /usr/bin/time -v): glia x10 whole program peak RSS 886,912 kB with 7,252,713 rows in its largest relation; the spike's Relation is exactly that HashSet + HashMap<Vec<usize>, HashMap<Box<[u32]>, Vec<u32>>> design. R1 section 4.4: two provenance columns (rule, height) per derived tuple (Souffle). The tier lattice (section 4.3) is evaluated as LEVELLED semi-naive in DA.14b (a tuple's tier = the first level whose fixpoint derives it, which equals min over derivations of max over inputs), so a tuple is inserted once into the partition of its level and never updated; storing partitions per level makes 'visible at level <= L' a slice choice instead of a per-tuple filter. R1 section 3: parse at CHECK time, not at overlay load (the loader drops an invalid stanza, glia_config.rs, which would make graph contents depend on the parser and drag rules/ into PARSER_STAMP); a bad rule is an errors row, exit 2. The rule text authors are agents (R1 section 1.3), so recovery matters: one bad rule must not hide the next. Syntax follows R1's own examples (`handled(r) :- edge(r, _, "HANDLED_BY"). violation(r) :- node(r, "ROUTE"), !handled(r).`): bare identifiers in argument position are variables, constants are quoted strings or integers - no Prolog case convention for agents to trip on. packets.implementation:
`pub fn parse_program(source_name: &str, text: &str) -> Result<Program, RulesError>` (Program has one source, `source_name`; RulesError::Parse(diags) on any error). Recursive descent over DA.4's tokens:
```
program  := clause*
clause   := head ( ':-' body )? '.'
head     := ident ( '(' [ harg (',' harg)* ] ')' )?      // `ok.`, `ok() :- ...` and `ok :- ...` are arity 0
harg     := aggop '(' ident (',' ident)* ')' | term      // aggop = count|min|max|sum, only in a head
body     := literal (',' literal)*
literal  := ('!' | 'not') atom | atom | term cmpop term
atom     := ident '(' [ term (',' term)* ] ')'               // `p()` is a 0-arity atom
term     := ident | '_' | string | int | '-' int         // ident = variable
cmpop    := '=' | '!=' | '<>' | '<' | '<=' | '>' | '>='
```
A literal starting `ident (` is an atom; otherwise term cmpop term. Every IR node carries its Span. Diagnostics (Error, source_name, line / col of the offending token, predicate = the clause's head `name/arity` once the head is parsed): `expected `.` after the rule for `v/1`, found `edge``; `expected a term, found `)``; `an aggregate (count) may appear only in a head`; ``<-` here reads as an arrow; write `a < -1``; `unknown aggregate `avg``; `a fact may not contain `_``. Recovery: on an error skip to the next `.` at bracket depth 0, record the diagnostic, continue; stop after 20 diagnostics. Integer literal after `-` negates with overflow check (i64::MIN is reachable). A 0-arity atom is written `p()` in a body (a bare identifier there starts a comparison, so `!p` alone is a parse error naming `write p()`); a 0-arity head may be written `ok` or `ok()`. The module doc states the grammar above verbatim (DZ links it from the rules reference).

packets.title: glia-rules plan: per-stratum rule plans - levelled semi-naive variants, bound-first atom order with known sizes, index choice, the reaches source hoist (one multi-source BFS when the source is dead after the call), aggregate body plans and explain plans
packets.rationale: R1 section 1.3: binary joins with body atoms reordered bound-first by a deterministic greedy planner (Angle leaves ordering to the author; glia's rules are written by agents, so the planner does it), one semi-naive variant per recursive atom (stable before, recent at, stable + recent after). R1 section 1.4 (re-measured today with the spike): the seeded unary forbid-transitive shape costs 1.1-1.7 ms on glia vs 8.5-12.5 ms pairwise, and 31 ms vs 441 ms at x10 - so when a `reaches` source variable is used by nothing after the call, the planner must run ONE multi-source BFS from all sources (R1 section 3: 'reaches = multi-source BFS'), not one BFS per source. Index choice: each lookup's bound columns name a permutation the relation keeps sorted (DA.7). The tier lattice is evaluated level by level (DA.14b), so lower-stratum and EDB atoms also get variants: in the first round of level L their level-L partition is the delta that can create new derivations. VERIFIED at HEAD 22c65ee: no planner exists (`ls rules` fails).

packets.title: glia-rules magic: the magic-sets / demand rewrite for unseeded user recursion - adorned copies per binding pattern, magic seed and propagation rules over the shared SIPS order, applied only to non-output recursive predicates and dropped when it would break stratification
packets.rationale: R1 section 7 lists a magic-sets / demand rewrite for unseeded user recursion (R2, pulled into 0.5.2 by the plan) and section 6 lesson 4: recursion bottom-up with magic sets, one demand predicate per binding pattern (lazamar's Glean fork: counting to 80,000 went from 141 s to 111 ms). RE-MEASURED today with the R1 spike: an UNSEEDED closure over CALLS on glia is 242,467 rows / 138-153 ms and 3,819,603 rows / 3.53 s at x10, while the seeded form of the same question is 1.1 ms / 31 ms - agents will write the unseeded `tc` and then call it with a bound first argument, and the rewrite turns the first into the second without the author doing it. packets.implementation:
```rust pub(crate) struct MagicReport { pub rewritten: Vec<(String /* name/arity */, String /* adornment, e.g. "bf" */, usize /* call sites */)>, pub skipped: Vec<(String, &'static str /* reason */)> } pub(crate) fn rewrite(program: &Program, an: &Analysis, catalog: &Catalog, outputs: &[PredId]) -> Option<(Program, MagicReport)>; // None when nothing qualifies ``` Candidates (in PredId order): recursive IDB predicates that are not outputs, not synthetic and have no aggregate. Call sites = body occurrences of the candidate in rules OUTSIDE its SCC; each site's adornment (b / f per argument) is read from sips_order (DA.5b) over that rule with nothing bound at start - an argument is b when it is a constant or a variable bound by the literals before the site. Skip reasons (each printed): `output` (the caller reads it whole), `no-bound-site` (every site is all-f), `aggregate`, `unstratifiable` (below). Rewrite (generalised magic sets, Bancilhon-Ramakrishnan; Raqlet applies it on its Datalog IR, R1 section 5): for each needed adornment a of p, an adorned copy `__a_p__a` of every rule of p's SCC whose SCC body atoms are renamed to their own adorned copies (adornments propagate through the SCC by the same SIPS with the head's b-arguments bound; a fixpoint over (pred, adornment) pairs, at most 2^arity per predicate, arity <= 8 enforced or the predicate is skipped as `arity`); each adorned rule gains the first body atom `__m_p__a()`; for each SCC atom __a_q__c at body position i, a propagation rule `__m_q__c() :- __m_p__a(), `; for each external site of p with adornment a (a has at least one b), a seed rule `__m_p__a() :- ` and the site renamed to `__a_p__a`. An external all-f site keeps the original, unrewritten p (both forms coexist). Negated, comparison and builtin literals before a site enter the seed / propagation rule only when fully bound there. Names: `__a_

__` for an adorned copy and `__m_

__` for a magic predicate (the draft's `p__bf` / `__magic_p__bf` could collide with a user predicate named `tc__bf`, and a user predicate `magic_tc` would collide with tc's magic name). Both start with the reserved `__` prefix no user rule may use (DA.5b), and `__a_` / `__m_` cannot collide with each other. They are synthetic: analysis accepts them only through analyse_with(.., allow_synthetic = true) and marks them, rows() refuses them, explain drops magic atoms and splices adorned copies (DA.15), and the `[rules] magic` lines print the ORIGINAL name. The rewritten program is re-analysed by the caller (DA.14b) with analyse_with(.., true); if analysis now fails (a magic rule closed a negation cycle), the caller keeps the original program and the predicate is reported skipped `unstratifiable`. Determinism: candidates, adornments and generated rules in PredId / source order; no HashMap iteration. Each rewrite prints `[rules] magic pred=/ adornment= sites=`; each skip prints `[rules] magic skipped pred=/ reason=`.

packets.risks: Correctness: magic sets preserve the answers of the predicates that READ the rewritten one, never the rewritten predicate's full extension - so outputs are never rewritten (a test pins it) and rows() refuses synthetic names. Tiers: a magic atom's tier is at most the tier of the prefix that bound it, so a row's min-over-derivations-of-max tier is unchanged (DA.18 compares tiers with magic on and off). Stratification can break when a negation precedes a site: re-analysis catches it and the original program is kept. Blow-up of adornments is capped by arity <= 8. Names use the reserved `__a_` / `__m_` prefixes so no user predicate can collide with a generated one. No HashMap iteration.

packets.rationale: Five DA test packets (DA.14b's unit tests, DA.18 oracle, DA.19 determinism + budget, DA.16 errors, DA.17 cost) need the same graphs; landing the builders once, before them, keeps those packets file-disjoint so they share a wave. As a public module (`glia_rules::testkit`, a D0 slot) the builders are never dead code in any one test target, so no test helper needs a dead_code allow, and DB's engine-side tests can reuse them. The determinism gate (plan section 2 DA: ties broken by rendered values) needs the same graph under DIFFERENT NodeIds: a re-salted RepoId stands in for a checkout at another path, since code NodeIds hash a path-derived RepoId (R1 section 1.3 / section 10). The x10 scaler restates the R1 spike's `scaled()` exactly - k copies with ids offset per copy, plus edges x k / 100 random CALLS edges from an LCG with seed 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15, multiplier 6364136223846793005, increment 1442695040888963407, value = (state >> 33) as u32, endpoints = value % (n x k) - so DA.17's numbers compare with R1 section 1.4. The spike's code lives only in a 0.5.1 spec-run scratch directory and is not a dependency. packets.implementation:
```rust
pub struct Lcg(pub u64);   // next_u32() = { state = state * 6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407 (wrapping); (state >> 33) as u32 }
pub const KINDS: [(&str, u32); 4];       // FUNCTION 1, MODULE 2, ROUTE 3, OBJECT 4 (test-local ids)
pub const CATEGORIES: [(&str, u32); 6];  // CALLS 1, IMPORTS 2, USES 3, HANDLED_BY 4, TESTS 5, NEXT 6
pub fn tables() -> DomainTables;         // those registries; carry_edges [CALLS, USES]; empty entry / sinks / weights
#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct GraphSpec { pub nodes: u32, pub edges: u32, pub categories: Vec<&'static str>, pub tier_mix: [u8; 3] /* percent FACT / DERIVED / HEURISTIC */, pub seed: u64, pub salt: u64 }
pub fn lcg_graph(spec: &GraphSpec) -> MemSource;      // node i: NodeId::from_parts("rules-test", RepoId(salt), kind, "n<i>"), kind KINDS[i % 4], render "n<i:05>", attribute `index` = i
pub fn chain(n: u32, category: &str, tiers: &[Tier]) -> MemSource;   // 0 -> 1 -> .. -> n-1, hop i at tiers[i % len]
pub fn clique_ring(n: u32, chords: u32, category: &str, seed: u64) -> MemSource;   // a ring plus LCG chords: strongly connected, unseeded TC = n^2 rows
pub fn resalted(g: &MemSource, salt: u64) -> MemSource;  // same rendered graph, new NodeIds, node order and edge order reversed
pub fn scaled(g: &MemSource, k: u32) -> MemSource;       // the spike's x k: copy c of node v is NodeId::from_parts("rules-scaled", RepoId(c as u64), NodeKindId(0), &format!("{:016x}", v.0)) with v's kind, attributes, cells and render unchanged (scopes span copies, as in the spike); nodes copy 0..k in node order, then edges copy 0..k in edge order (tiers kept), then the cross CALLS edges between dense node indexes (value % (n x k)), tier FACT
```
Every builder gives node i the render `n<i:05>`, kind KINDS[i % 4] and the Int attribute `index` = i, so rules can seed by `index(x, 0)`. MemSource gains no method here (only its public builder API from DA.6 is called). The module doc states it is a test and benchmark kit, not a domain.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DD.3 cross-group): DD.3 (a dependency of this packet) adds the required field `identity_rules: &'static [IdentityRule]` to activation's DomainTables (exhaustive on purpose), so tables() builds the literal with `identity_rules: &[]` beside its other fields (and every DomainTables field DD.3 / CD.1c added: registries, carry_edges, entry, effect_sinks, activation_weights, community_weights, ...).

packets.title: glia-rules eval: evaluate / run - lazy EDB loading, the magic rewrite with an unstratifiable fallback, levelled semi-naive per stratum (FACT, then +DERIVED, then +HEURISTIC) over exec (DA.14a), aggregate strata, the row budget with an actionable error, absence caveats, rows sorted by rendered values, and the `[rules] eval` marker
packets.rationale: The evaluator is the R1 bet's core (R1 section 1.3; R1 section 0: hand-rolled, datafrog-style storage, stratified negation, closure builtin, provenance, 3-level tier lattice). The tier rule (plan section 2: a row's tier = min over derivations of max over inputs) is evaluated exactly and without per-tuple tier updates by running each stratum's fixpoint three times incrementally: first with only FACT inputs visible, then adding DERIVED, then HEURISTIC; a tuple's level is the first fixpoint that derives it, which is the min over derivations of the max input tier, and a tuple is inserted once. Q5 (binding): negated atoms read the complete relation and contribute no tier, the row carrying absence caveats instead; aggregates take the weakest contributing row. The budget (plan gate: the measured blow-up stopped by the budget) is DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 5,000,000. The draft's justification used R1's 0.5.0-era dump; the verifier re-ran the spike on a HEAD 22c65ee dump (25,768 nodes / 81,857 edges): at x10 (257,680 / 826,755) the unseeded carry closure is 13,551,390 rows (10.06 s, whole-process peak RSS 1,654,172 kB) and the unseeded CALLS closure 7,840,842 rows - both stopped by 5 M; at x1 the same unseeded closures are 611,464 and 456,041 rows and run; the largest seeded, check-shaped relation measured at x10 is the pairwise forbid at 704,796 rows (7x headroom), with the error naming the predicate and advising a seed (R1 section 1.3, the posture of Adjacency::over_limit). R1 section 1.3: output rows sorted by RENDERED values. VERIFIED at HEAD 22c65ee: `ls rules` fails; check lists `invariant` unchecked (engine/src/check.rs). The interpreter itself is DA.14a (split from the draft's DA.14: ~700 LOC counted, over the 600 cap).

packets.title: glia-rules explain: Evaluation::explain - the minimal-height derivation at the row's tier as a Witness tree (Souffle-style search over (rule, height), no re-evaluation), checkout-stable candidate choice by rendered values, edge / path / node / attribute leaves with global edge ordinals, aggregate and negation nodes, synthetic atoms elided, and a leaf cap
packets.rationale: R1 section 4.4: adopt Souffle's provenance exactly - (rule, height) per derived tuple, minimal-height proof trees built lazily by search, with no re-evaluation (Zhao, Subotic, Scholz, TOPLAS 2020); each leaf edge is located through its EVIDENCE cell and rendered as check's ViolationEdge, capped at MAX_EVIDENCE (engine/src/check.rs `pub const MAX_EVIDENCE: usize = 100`, verified at HEAD 22c65ee); the witness is the minimal-height derivation, for forbid-transitive a shortest path, ties broken by rendered qname for checkout-stable output. With the levelled evaluation (DA.14b) a tuple's recorded (rule, height) belong to the first derivation at its level and never change, so the search invariant holds by construction: some instantiation of the recorded rule uses body tuples of level <= the row's level and height < its height. The leaf names the GLOBAL edge ordinal so DB maps it back to its &Edge and reads Evidence::of (the rules crate never parses evidence: domain-free).

packets.title: glia-rules cost gates (R1 spike 1): 20 check-shaped rules on glia's own graph under 200 ms, peak RSS under 150 MB at glia x10, and the measured 7.25 M-row unseeded closure at x10 stopped by the default budget - an ignored release test target over a `glia analyze --format json` dump
packets.rationale: Plan gates (section 2 DA): the spike's cost targets - 20 check rules < 200 ms on glia; RSS < 150 MB at glia x10 (R1 section 9 spike 1) - and the measured blow-up stopped by the budget. MEASURED BY THE VERIFIER AT HEAD 22c65ee (the draft re-ran the spike on the 0.5.0-era dumps, 18,387 nodes / 56,738 edges, which no longer describe glia): `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia analyze <git-archive copy of HEAD> --format json` = 26,008 node rows for 25,768 distinct ids (one id in several language graphs) and 81,857 edges, 0 dangling endpoints; converted to the spike's TSV and run with the spike's release binary (`/usr/bin/time -v`): x1 - carry/2 41,628 rows 10.5-11.4 ms, unseeded TC over CALLS 456,041 rows 223-238 ms, unseeded TC over carry 611,464 rows 364-384 ms, seeded forbid-transitive cli->store 3.7 ms / py->graph 1.9 ms, pairwise 14.7-17.3 ms, negation 9.6-9.7 ms, count 2.0-2.6 ms, 3-atom forbid 3.4-3.6 ms, whole program 0.65-0.69 s; x10 (257,680 nodes / 826,755 edges) - carry/2 424,465 rows, unseeded TC over CALLS 7,840,842 rows in 6.24 s, over carry 13,551,390 rows in 10.06 s (R1's 7.25 M case at 0.5.0 size), seeded forbid-transitive 47 ms, pairwise 704,796 rows 518 ms, whole program 17.5 s, peak RSS 1,654,172 kB. So the gates run on a fresh dump of HEAD, not on R1's numbers, and the blow-up case is the unseeded carry closure at x10 (13.55 M rows at HEAD). RSS reading: R1's spike held its graph as three compact vectors, so its whole-process RSS was the evaluator's; here the graph is a MemSource of core::Edge values (48 bytes each, ~40 MB of edges at x10) plus the parsed dump, which the engine already holds in memory before any rule runs. The gate therefore measures the evaluator's own peak (VmHWM reset through /proc/self/clear_refs after the graph is built, verified on this machine: writing `5` drops VmHWM to the current VmRSS) and reports the whole-process figure beside it; open question for James. The rules crate cannot depend on the engine, so the gate reads glia's graph from `glia analyze --format json` (verified at HEAD: top-level keys [edges, nodes], edge keys [category, from, intra, to], node keys [id, kind, kind_name, name, qname, repo, roles]); the dump carries no evidence, so tiers are assigned by a fixed category table (below) to exercise all three levels. Timing gates are meaningless in a debug build, so the target is #[ignore]d and run in release, one test per process (VmHWM is per process).

Oracles: tc(x, y) at tier <= L iff y in reachable(adj_L, successors_L(x)) (the >= 1-hop closure; x itself iff on a cycle), a row's tier the smallest such L; scc membership = strongly_connected(adj_all), member tier = smallest L where x and rep share a component of strongly_connected(adj_L); negation = set difference; aggregates = folds over the rows. VERSION: `validate` accepts `SUPPORTED_VERSIONS`; version 0 -> "`version` is missing (1, or 2 to use rule / transitive / via / min_tier); the whole file is ignored"; any other -> "version = <v> is not supported (this glia reads versions 1 and 2); the whole file is ignored". A version-1 file keeps loading exactly as today (Q7). #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct QueryOptions { pub outputs: Vec<String>, pub limit: Option<usize>, pub explain: bool,
    pub row_budget: Option<usize>, pub source_name: String, pub surface: &'static str /* Default: "engine" */ }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)]
pub struct QueryAnswer { pub language: &'static str /* datalog | gql */, pub outputs: Vec<QueryOutput>,
    pub results: Vec<QueryRow>, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)]
pub struct QueryOutput { pub predicate: String, pub arity: usize, pub columns: Vec<String>, pub total: usize, pub shown: usize }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)]
pub struct QueryRow { pub predicate: String, pub values: Vec<QueryValue>, pub tier: &'static str,
    pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub caveats: Vec<CoverageNote>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] pub witness: Vec<ViolationEdge> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum QueryValue { Node { qname: String, kind: &'static str, file: Option<String>, line: Option<i64> }, Str(String), Int(i64) }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RuleDiagnostic { pub line: u32, pub column: u32, pub message: String } // 1-based, within the program text
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RuleError { pub kind: &'static str /* parse | analysis | budget | evaluation */, pub diagnostics: Vec<RuleDiagnostic>, pub rendered: String }

PIPELINE (`query`): parse (DA, spans tagged with `source_name`, default `<query>`) -> reserved names (a user rule whose head is a core predicate node / edge / cell, a CODE_ATTRIBUTES name or a builtin is an analysis error naming it) -> analysis against the CODE schema (DA's checker given CODE_TABLES.registries, CODE_ATTRIBUTES and the builtin signatures: unknown node kind / edge category / cell type constant in node/2, edge/3, cell/3 -> "unknown node kind `ROUTEE` (a registered kind name; `glia inspect` lists them)"; unknown predicate / arity / safety / unstratifiable negation as DA words them) -> outputs: `opts.outputs`, else every predicate the text defines, in first-definition order; an output no rule defines is an analysis error -> evaluation over CodeFacts::new(merged) with `row_budget` (DA's default when None; DA's budget error, naming the predicate and advising a seed, becomes kind `budget`; DA's parse errors kind `parse`, its analysis errors kind `analysis`, its runtime builtin / type / unknown-output errors kind `evaluation`) and explain = opts.explain. RENDERING: a Node value -> QueryValue::Node through the one Locator; Str / Int as is. A row's `file` / `line` are its first Node value's. COLUMNS: the head variable names of the predicate's first rule in source order; a constant head position is `c<i>`. ORDER: per output, rows sorted by their rendered value tuples (Int < Str < Node; Node by qname, then file, then line; ties keep DA's order, which is deterministic), then cut to `limit` (QueryOutput.total keeps the count). TIER: tier_name(DA's row tier). CAVEATS (Q5): a static walk of the program's IR from each output: every predicate reached under a negated literal contributes the edge categories its rules read - an `edge(_, _, "C")` constant names C; an edge atom whose category is a variable, or any core / attribute atom over edges with an unbound category, means every category - and the output's rows carry caveats_for(merged, <those names>, None) (positive atoms tier the row; negation only adds caveats). WITNESS (explain): DA's minimal-height derivation leaves; each leaf edge(a, b, c) is located at the FIRST edge in all_edges order with that key (the why / implementors convention), its tier and note from why::tier_of, through located_edge; capped at check::MAX_EVIDENCE. ABSENCE: when results is empty, absence::empty(merged, "query", <the first 120 chars of the text>, "no_match", "no row of <pred>/<n> in this graph" (several outputs: each named), <every category the program reads, positive or negated>, None). MARKER, once per query: `[query] lang=<datalog|gql> outputs=<o> rows=<r> fact=<f> derived=<d> heuristic=<h> caveated=<c> surface=<cli|py|engine>`. `validate(text)`: parse + reserved names + analysis with no graph (the schema is static), returning the diagnostics (empty = valid); `glia gaps` (DB.4) and check (DB.3a) use it. `evaluate_rule` (pub(crate)): the same pipeline with outputs ["violation"] and explain on, over a caller's CodeFacts; a program without a `violation` predicate -> Err("rule defines no `violation` predicate"); returns the rows with their NodeIds kept (check renders subject and location); it prints no `[query]` line (check prints `[rules] check`, DB.3a). docs/rules.md: core predicates (node/2, edge/3, cell/3 as DA defines them), the code attributes and builtins of DB.2a, output selection, rendering and ordering, tiers and the Q5 caveats, the row budget, determinism, and that the evaluator reads structure only (SECURITY.md).
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DA.2 / DA.5b / DA.9 / DA.14b / DA.15 cross-group): (a) analysis diagnostics are DA.5b's message table verbatim (pinned by DA.16): the unknown-constant case reads `unknown node kind `ROUTEE`; did you mean `ROUTE`?` - the engine wraps DA's Diagnostic (source name, 1-based line:col) and adds no second wording, so the draft's `(a registered kind name; `glia inspect` lists them)` suffix is dropped; acceptance (3)'s `contains` assertions stand. (b) eval::Options is #[non_exhaustive]: build it with Options::default() and assign outputs / max_rows / magic, never a struct literal. packets.implementation:
PRELUDE TEXT (DA's surface syntax; one rule per concept, a comment line above each):
```
carry(A, B) :- edge(A, B, C), carry_category(C).
depends(A, B) :- edge(A, B, C), dependency_category(C).
calls(A, B) :- edge(A, B, "CALLS").
uses(A, B) :- edge(A, B, "USES").
imports(A, B) :- edge(A, B, "IMPORTS").
defines(P, C) :- edge(P, C, "DEFINES").
contains(P, C) :- edge(P, C, "CONTAINS").
implements(A, B) :- edge(A, B, "IMPLEMENTS").
inherits(A, B) :- edge(A, B, "INHERITS_FROM").
handles(R, H) :- edge(R, H, "HANDLED_BY").
handled(R) :- handles(R, _).
unhandled_route(R) :- node(R, "ROUTE"), !handled(R).
tested(N) :- edge(_, N, "TESTS").
unreached(N) :- node(N, K), symbol_kind(K), !live(N).
effect(F, S, Class) :- edge(F, S, C), node(S, K), effect_sink(K, C, Class).
cross_repo(A, B, C) :- edge(A, B, C), repo(A, R1), repo(B, R2), R1 != R2.
module_dep(A, B) :- module_import(A, B).
```
`carry_category/1` is DA's core relation (its Catalog declares it from FactSource::tables().carry_edges, which CodeFacts answers with CODE_TABLES), so the prelude reads it and does not redefine it. ENGINE RELATIONS (prelude.rs; extra EDB handed to DA's evaluator, each built only when the merged program references it, each row tiered and each declaring `reads: &[&str]` for the Q5 walk): dependency_category/1 = check::default_forbid_categories names (FACT); symbol_kind/1 = CLASS, FUNCTION, METHOD (gaps' dead_symbol kinds; FACT); effect_sink/3 = for every (kind, category) pair named in CODE_TABLES.effect_sinks, CODE_TABLES.effect_sink(kind, category)'s class, so the first match classifies (FACT); live/1 = entrypoint_reachable(merged) (DERIVED: a computed walk; reads the carry categories); module_import/2 = module_import_graph's lifted MODULE -> MODULE edges, tier = why::tier_of(imports.evidence(a, b), edge) (reads IMPORTS). `unreached` is NOT gaps' dead_symbol (no dispatch or test-fixture exclusions): docs/rules.md says so. MERGE: PRELUDE is parsed once (OnceLock) with source name `prelude`; run_program and validate append it to the user program; DA evaluates only the strata the outputs need (an unreferenced prelude rule costs nothing, `live` is never computed unless used); a user rule defining a prelude predicate or engine relation name is an analysis error "`carry` is a prelude predicate (docs/rules.md); name yours differently"; default outputs never include prelude predicates. GUARD (prelude.rs unit test `prelude_is_structural_only`): every predicate PRELUDE defines and every engine relation name contains none of DENY = [auth, login, passw, secret, credential, token, permission, privilege, taint, sanitiz, vuln, cve, exploit, bypass, attack, unauthenticated] (case-insensitive), and no engine relation reads a CODE / SCHEMA text cell; a comment at the top of prelude.dl states the rule. SECURITY.md, new section after `What glia does not build`: "## The query language reads structure only" - `glia query`, `PyGraph.query` / `query_gql` and `[[constraint]] rule` evaluate Datalog (or a GQL read subset) over the structural graph only: nodes, their kinds and locations, edges and their categories, and cells; no value- or data-flow relation exists to query, the shipped prelude defines no authentication, authorization or security predicate (a test enforces it), and glia ships no rule that classifies routes by authentication. A repo owner can ask structural reachability questions of their own code; glia does not provide or curate security rules, and the gated list above is unchanged. docs/rules.md `## The prelude`: the table of predicates with their rules and the engine relations with their sources and tiers.

SCOPES: from_set = ctx.scope(from, "from")? (the existing empty-scope error), to_set = ctx.scope(to, "to")?, via_sets = each via scope through ctx.scope(v, "via")? (a facade no node sits in is a rule error: "via scope `x` matches no located node"). seeds = from_set minus to_set minus every via node, sorted by rendered qname (ctx.qname) then id, so the BFS order is checkout-stable; stop = to_set union via nodes. CHAINS (Q3): cats = the rule's categories or default_forbid_categories(); if cats contains both IMPORTS and CALLS AND the rule named its categories -> ONE mixed chain over the raw edges of cats; else an `imports` chain when cats contains IMPORTS (over module_import_graph(merged): seeds / stop / hits are the MODULEs in those sets - a module is in a scope by its file, as no_cycle's import rules place it) and a `symbols` chain over cats minus IMPORTS when non-empty (the raw node graph). WALK: for each chain, `Barred { inner, stop }` (GraphSource: node_ids as inner; edges = inner.edges().filter(|e| !stop.contains(&e.from))) and DA's levelled multi-source BFS (activation::algo::reach, the function the `reaches` builtin runs: three passes over the edges of `keep = CategorySet::of(chain cats)` whose tier <= Fact, <= Derived, any; per reached node the first pass's tier, depth, parent and category; path_to(node)) - a domain-free walk, so the engine adds no graph algorithm (CLAUDE.md: generic algorithms live in activation::algo) with tier fn: symbols / mixed chains `edge_tier_of(e)` (DB.2a, why::tier_of), imports chain `tier_of(imports.evidence(e.from, e.to), e)`. HITS: reached nodes in to_set, not in a via set, not a seed. A node hit by two chains keeps one violation: the stronger tier, then fewer hops, then imports first. VIOLATION per hit: rule_kind FORBID_PATH, tier = the hit's pass tier (the weakest hop on its best path), blocking per min_tier (DB.3a), subject [hit qname], file / line = the hit's location, count = hop count, evidence = the path's hops IN PATH ORDER (not tier-sorted: it is a witness), each located at the first edge in all_edges order with key (parent, category, child) whose own tier is no weaker than the hit's tier (imports chain: imports.evidence(a, b)), through located_edge; that lookup is one index per rule, built in the same pass that tiers the chain's edges (key -> the first ordinal at each of the three tiers), never a scan of the edge list per hop. Violations of one rule sorted by subject; an evaluated transitive rule counts in CheckReport.checked. `[rules] check ... transitive=<T> hits=<H> (imports=<a> symbols=<b> mixed=<c>)` counts the transitive rules evaluated and the hits per chain. Module doc: a `# Transitive forbid_edge (Q3)` section with the fx1 example; direct forbid_edge keeps its function and output unchanged.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DA.1 cross-group): call activation::algo::reach::bfs_levels directly over the Barred GraphSource (glia_rules::closure is crate-private): pass edge_level per KEPT edge (Adjacency::build order = global edge order filtered by the CategorySet) and levels = 3; a hit's tier is Tier::from_level(level). LevelReached.parent is the node's FIRST-pass parent, so the shortest witness at the hit's level takes a second walk at that level alone (edge levels <= L mapped to 0, others to u8::MAX) with parent_rank = rank by rendered qname; hops between parallel edges are chosen by (tier, category name), as DA.11 does.

packets.title: The GQL read subset, parsed: glia_rules::gql AST + recursive-descent parser (Pratt WHERE) over DA's shared lexer, for MATCH ... [WHERE] RETURN [DISTINCT] ... [ORDER BY] [LIMIT], both quantifier spellings, with span diagnostics and an explicit refusal for everything outside the subset
packets.research: R1-datalog §5 (construct table, grammar: hand-rolled, one lexer per surface, Pratt for WHERE)
packets.rationale: Plan §2 DB item 5 (Q1: GQL is the ad-hoc read surface; Q4: set semantics + edge homomorphism, documented as unlike openCypher). R1 §5 fixes the subset (patterns with labels / properties / typed and quantified relationships, WHERE with AND / OR / NOT / comparisons / STARTS WITH / CONTAINS / IN / NOT pattern / function calls, RETURN with aggregates, ORDER BY, LIMIT, ANY SHORTEST path variables) and the grammar choice: hand-rolled for span control and no version coupling (winnow 0.7 is in the lock only through toml_edit; the rules crate takes no external dependency). R1 §10: scope creep into a general graph database is the risk, so the subset list is the contract and every other clause is refused by name. The crate is domain-free: labels, relationship types and property names are plain identifiers here; DB.7b maps them onto core predicates and attributes. VERIFIER: R1 §5 says ONE shared lexer for both surfaces, and DA's lexer packet is specced to be that lexer (its TokenKind covers `->`, `<-`, `..`, `{`, `}`, `|`, `*`, `+`, `<>` and its tests tokenize `MATCH (a:ROUTE)-[:CALLS|USES*1..3]->(b) WHERE a.qname STARTS WITH 'x' RETURN a, count(b)`). A second tokenizer in rules/src/gql/lexer.rs would duplicate it (two string-escape and column rules to keep equal), so this packet parses DA's tokens and writes no lexer.
entry_points: rules/src/gql/mod.rs (D0 slot) - `pub mod ast; mod parser; pub use parser::parse;`
rules/src/lexer.rs (DA, read) - lex / Token / TokenKind: the shared tokenizer; keywords arrive as Ident and are compared case-insensitively here
rules/src/gql/ast.rs (new) - Query, PathPattern, NodePat, RelPat, Dir, Quant, Expr, Operand, Lit, ReturnItem, RetExpr, Agg, OrderKey
rules/src/gql/parser.rs (new) - pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<ast::Query, Vec<Diagnostic>>
rules/tests/gql_parse.rs (new)
packets.implementation:
TOKENS: DA's `lexer::lex(source, "<gql>", text)` (one tokenizer for both surfaces, R1 §5); a lexical error comes back as DA's Diagnostic unchanged. Token mapping the grammar uses: `-[` = Minus LBracket, `]->` = RBracket Arrow, `<-[` = LeftArrow LBracket, `]-` = RBracket Minus, `-->` = Minus Arrow, `<--` = LeftArrow Minus, `--` = Minus Minus, `*1..3` = Star Int DotDot Int, `{1,}` = LBrace Int Comma RBrace, `<>` / `!=` = Ne; keywords (MATCH, WHERE, RETURN, ...) are Ident tokens compared case-insensitively. GRAMMAR (keywords case-insensitive, identifiers case-sensitive):
```
query    := match+ [WHERE expr] RETURN [DISTINCT] item (',' item)* [ORDER BY key (',' key)*] [LIMIT int] [';']
match    := MATCH pattern (',' pattern)*
pattern  := [ident '=' [ANY SHORTEST]] node (rel node)*
node     := '(' [ident] [':' ident ('|' ident)*] [props] ')'
props    := '{' ident ':' lit (',' ident ':' lit)* '}'
rel      := '-[' relbody ']->' [gquant] | '<-[' relbody ']-' [gquant] | '-[' relbody ']-' [gquant] | '-->' | '<--' | '--'
relbody  := [ident] [':' ident ('|' ident)*] [ '*' [int] ['..' [int]] ]
gquant   := '+' | '*' | '{' int ',' [int] '}' | '{' int '}'
expr     := Pratt: OR < AND < NOT < cmp; cmp := operand (('=' | '<>' | '!=' | '<' | '<=' | '>' | '>=') operand
            | STARTS WITH operand | ENDS WITH operand | CONTAINS operand | IN '[' lit (',' lit)* ']')
            | pattern | EXISTS '{' pattern '}' | ident '(' [operand (',' operand)*] ')' | '(' expr ')'
operand  := ident | ident '.' ident | lit | TYPE '(' ident ')'
item     := (operand | agg | ident) [AS ident];  agg := (COUNT | MIN | MAX | SUM) '(' ('*' | [DISTINCT] operand) ')'
key      := (ident | ident '.' ident) [ASC | DESC]
lit      := string ('..' or "..", backslash escapes) | int | TRUE | FALSE
```
Quantifier normalisation in the AST: Cypher `*` -> {1, None}; `*n` -> {n, n}; `*m..` -> {m, None}; `*..n` -> {1, n}; `*m..n` -> {m, n}; GQL `+` -> {1, None}, `*` (after the rel) -> {0, None}, `{m,n}` / `{m,}` / `{m}` the same shapes; min > max, or a max of 0 with min 0 on a typed rel, is a diagnostic. A rel may carry one quantifier form, not both. REFUSED, each with a diagnostic at its keyword: "`<KW>` is not in the GQL read subset (docs/rules.md)" for OPTIONAL MATCH, WITH (as a clause), UNWIND, UNION, CALL, CREATE, MERGE, SET, DELETE, DETACH, REMOVE, FOREACH, LOAD, SKIP, CASE, `$` parameters, shortestPath() / allShortestPaths(), ALL SHORTEST, and the restrictors TRAIL / ACYCLIC / SIMPLE (the message adds "glia returns endpoint pairs under walk semantics (Q4)"). Diagnostics reuse DA's Diagnostic / Span types (1-based line:column rendering identical to Datalog's); the parser recovers to the next clause keyword so one query reports every error, at most 20. AST nodes carry spans for DB.7b's diagnostics. No evaluation, no IR here.

packets.title: The GQL read subset, lowered to the rules IR: patterns to core node / edge atoms and attributes, quantifiers to the `reaches` builtin or bounded unrolling, WHERE to DNF with negated helper predicates, RETURN to a `result` head with grouped aggregates; set semantics and edge homomorphism (Q4)
packets.research: R1-datalog §5 (lowering table, deliberate deviations), §8 Q4 / Q5
packets.rationale: Plan §2 DB item 5: the GQL read subset lowered to DA's IR so one evaluator, one tier lattice and one budget serve both surfaces (R1 §0.5: GQL is R2 on the same IR). R1 §5's table is the mapping; Q4 (resolved): rows are DISTINCT (set semantics) and two relationship patterns may bind the same edge (homomorphism), unlike openCypher's relationship isomorphism; GQL's restrictors are not needed because glia returns endpoint pairs, so `->{1,}` is plain reachability and only a path variable needs ANY SHORTEST. Prior art R1 cites: Raqlet (Cypher -> Datalog IR), openCypher in relational algebra. The lowering lives in the rules crate beside the parser (domain-free: labels and types are names the analysis resolves against the FactSource registries, properties are attributes).
entry_points: rules/src/gql/mod.rs - `mod lower;` + `pub use lower::{compile, Compiled, OrderKey};`
rules/src/gql/lower.rs (new) - pub fn compile(text) -> Result<Compiled, Vec<Diagnostic>> (parse + lower); the lowering
rules/tests/gql_lower.rs (new) - lowering checked by evaluation over an inline FactSource
packets.implementation:
```rust
pub struct Compiled { pub program: Program, pub output: String /* "result" */, pub columns: Vec<String>,
    pub order_by: Vec<OrderKey>, pub limit: Option<u64>, pub path_column: Option<usize> }
pub struct OrderKey { pub column: usize, pub descending: bool }
```
LOWERING (IR constructors are crate-internal; names are DA's): every pattern / expression variable -> an IR variable; an anonymous node -> a fresh `_g<n>` variable. NODE: one label L -> `node(v, "L")`; labels L1|L2 -> one alternative per label (DNF); no label and the variable bound nowhere else -> `node(v, _)` (range restriction); `{k: lit}` -> attribute atom `k(v, lit)`. REL (unquantified): type T -> `edge(a, b, "T")` (direction In swaps a / b; undirected -> two alternatives a->b, b->a); several types -> a helper `gql_hop<n>(a, b) :- edge(a, b, "T1").` one rule per type, used as one atom (no combinatorial DNF); no type -> `edge(a, b, _)`; a rel variable r binds the category variable (for `type(r)`). QUANTIFIED: {1, None} -> `reaches(a, b, "T1|T2")` (DA's reaches/3, whose category-set argument is a constant `"A|B"`; no type = `"*"`, every category); {0, None} -> two alternatives (`a = b` with node(a, _), and reaches); {m, None}, m > 1 -> m - 1 hop atoms then reaches; {m, n} with n <= 8 -> one alternative per length k in m..=n unrolled through the hop helper with fresh intermediates (walk semantics, homomorphic); n > 8 -> diagnostic "bounded repetition above 8 hops: use * (any length)". WHERE: NOT pushed inward (De Morgan); NOT over a comparison flips it; NOT over a pattern, EXISTS, STARTS WITH / ENDS WITH / CONTAINS or a function call -> a helper predicate whose head is the variables it shares with the enclosing pattern, negated (`!gql_not<n>(..)`); the whole condition in DNF, each conjunct becoming one rule body with the MATCH atoms; more than 64 alternatives -> diagnostic "the query expands to <n> alternatives (limit 64): split it". IN [..] -> a helper fact table `gql_in<n>(lit).` per list. Comparisons and string tests -> DA's comparison literals and its starts_with / ends_with / contains builtins; a function call -> the builtin of that name (a domain builtin such as in_scope; an unknown one is an analysis error later, with the call's span). RETURN: head `result(<one variable per item>)`; `a.k` -> attribute atom `k(a, X)` binding a fresh variable (a node without that attribute drops the row: no nulls, documented); `type(r)` -> the category variable; aggregates -> DA's grouped aggregate head (count over one or more variables; count(*) counts distinct bindings of every MATCH variable; DISTINCT is accepted and changes nothing under set semantics) grouped by the non-aggregate items; a path variable p is returned as a column whose value is the row's witness (path_column; it requires exactly one quantified relationship in its pattern, else a diagnostic). columns = alias, else the item's source text (`a.qname`, `count(b)`). ORDER BY keys resolve to columns (an alias or an item's text; anything else -> diagnostic), LIMIT kept for post-processing (the engine sorts rendered values, DB.7c). Every helper predicate starts `gql_`; numbering is by visit order, so the same text lowers to the same program. Prints `[gql] lower rules=<r> helpers=<h> alternatives=<a> output=result` once per compile.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DA.5b / DA.12 cross-group): helper predicates are named `gql_hop<n>`, `gql_not<n>` and `gql_in<n>` (prefix `gql_`, NOT `__gql_`): DA.5b's analysis rejects every user predicate name starting `__` (reserved for DA.12's magic copies `__a_` / `__m_`; allowed only under the crate-private analyse_with(.., true) that the magic rewrite uses), and DB.7c runs the lowered program through the public pipeline, so a `__gql_` helper would fail analysis. A GQL text defines no predicates and no prelude predicate starts `gql_` (DB.2c's guard lists them), so the prefix cannot collide. The verifier's text spelled the prefix `__gql_`; the integrator replaced it with `gql_` throughout this packet (acceptance (3) asserts one `gql_not0` rule). Also DA.19's source guard covers rules/src/gql (no HashMap / HashSet, no threads).

PROGRAM (reflexion.dl; components are Int indices of ModelEdb.components, so every relation keys like the native BTreeMaps):
```
project_placed(N) :- project_path(N, _).
place(N, P) :- project_path(N, P).
place(N, F) :- located(N, F), !project_placed(N).
owns(N, C, P) :- place(N, F), component_path(C, P), under(F, P).
shadowed(N, P) :- owns(N, _, P), owns(N, _, P2), under(P2, P), P2 != P.
in_component(N, C) :- owns(N, C, P), !shadowed(N, P).
mapped(N) :- in_component(N, _).
unmapped(N, F) :- located(N, F), !mapped(N).
dep(C1, C2, E) :- edge_site(E, A, B), in_component(A, C1), in_component(B, C2), C1 != C2.
dependent(C1, C2) :- dep(C1, C2, _).
allowed(C1, C2) :- allow(C1, C2, _).
allowed(C1, C2) :- layer_of(C1, R1, "lax"), layer_of(C2, R2, _), R1 < R2.
allowed(C1, C2) :- layer_of(C1, R1, "strict"), layer_of(C2, R2, _), next_rank(R1, R2).
closed(1) :- allow(_, _, _).
closed(1) :- layer_of(_, _, _).
convergence(C1, C2) :- dependent(C1, C2), allowed(C1, C2).
divergence(C1, C2) :- closed(1), dependent(C1, C2), !allowed(C1, C2).
absence(C1, C2) :- allow(C1, C2, _), !dependent(C1, C2).
unmapped_edge(E) :- edge_site(E, A, B), mapped(A), unmapped(B, _).
unmapped_edge(E) :- edge_site(E, A, B), unmapped(A, _), mapped(B).
```
EDB (reflexion.rs, extra relations with tiers; FACT unless said): component_path(C, P) from ModelEdb.component_path (normalised paths; the equal-path errors stay ModelEdb's); layer_of(C, Rank, "strict" | "lax"); next_rank(R, R + 1) for each rank R a layer holds (R + 1 through checked_add; a rank at u32::MAX has no row - the native `checked_add(1) == Some(r2)`), so the rule body needs no arithmetic; allow(C1, C2, Id) from ModelEdb.allow; located(N, F) from CodeFacts.files() (raw file strings, so unmapped samples match); project_path(N, P) from CodeFacts.projects(); edge_site(E, A, B): E = the index of each distinct EdgeSite (check's dedup key: from, category, to, evidence file, evidence line) among all_edges of the checked categories, in all_edges order, its tier = why::tier_of of that first edge; a parallel Vec<(edge, evidence, tier, note)> keeps E -> the edge for rendering. `under` is DB.2a's builtin (same normalisation as check's norm_path / owner: `.` holds everything, segment boundaries). READ BACK -> ReflexionFacts: in_component (N -> C), unmapped (N -> F), dep (pair -> its DepEdges from E), allowed (pair -> allowed_by label: the smallest allow id when allow(C1, C2, _) exists, else `layer:<upper>><lower>` from the layer facts - naming is rendering, unchanged), closed, convergence, divergence, absence, unmapped_edges = |unmapped_edge|. packets.rationale:
Plan §0.1 Q9 (binding): rule text is overlay-only and LLM-proposed rules go through `overlay propose / try / accept`. DB.1 closes the cell API to `rule` text (validate_entry refuses it whatever the source), so after DB.1 the overlay file is the only way in, and its only writer is overlay_loop::accept (CE.3d). The integrator's uncovered list names this hole. Verified at HEAD 22c65ee (docs-only past 84e2e71): engine/src/overlay_loop/writer.rs `CANDIDATE_SECTIONS` is [route_prefix, wrapper, edge, constants, entrypoints] and `TABLE_SECTIONS` [route_prefix, wrapper, edge]; `scan`'s catch-all arm refuses any other section, and engine/tests/overlay_loop.rs `candidate_sections_are_limited` pins `parse_candidate("[[constraint]]
id = "r"
kind = "invariant"
text = "t"

The id check reads the base text only: a rule with the same id written through the cell API is not visible to merge (DB.1 closes the cell API to `rule` text; DB.9b's try marks such a stanza duplicate). Refusing `allow` and prose invariants is deliberate (a waiver and an unjudgeable stanza are a person's), and both still load from a hand-written file. PARSER_STAMP moves (engine/src is hashed): one parse-cache invalidation, no format change. DB.4 edits GUIDE, accept.rs, cli overlay.rs, py overlay_loop.rs, engine/tests/overlay_loop.rs and docs/overlay.md first (depends_on); DF.11 also edits docs/overlay.md (the `[walk] tests` paragraph, another section): the integrator orders the two. Determinism: scan / merge iterate document order only. The rule guard runs DB.2b's static validate (no graph, no build) on each chosen rule, so accept stays build-free for a candidate. It must not move into parse_candidate: try has to judge a broken rule (status error) instead of refusing the whole candidate. validate and DB.4's rotted_rule share one reader, so a rule accept admits is never a rotted_rule row on the same glia. The version-raise guard compares section counts only. A base whose raise changes an error text without changing a count does not exist under DB.1's rules: every version-1 error that version 2 lifts drops a stanza. docs/rules.md is DB.2b / DB.2c / DB.7c's file before this packet: one sentence, no other line moves.

packets.title: overlay try judges rules by the check delta: each build's declared rules are checked and their violations compared by identity (an evidence row, a rule / forbid_path subject, a cycle), a [[constraint]] stanza is judged on WITH alone (holds / violated / error / orphaned / duplicate, and the scopes its rule names that hold no node) with no leave-one-out build, a graph stanza that adds or hides a declared rule's violation is review instead of keep, and the candidate's verdict combines its graph and rule parts; `[overlay] try-rules` marker

packets.research: R1-datalog §3, §7 (check / review as the rule consumers), §8 Q2 / Q9
packets.rationale: Plan §0.1 Q9 sends LLM-proposed rules through `overlay try`, whose verdict today measures graph counts only: engine/src/overlay_loop/trial.rs `measure` keeps `graph_counts(merged)` and the graph-category gap ids, and `stanza_trial` / `try_candidate` judge by `gaps::verdict` (a gap category fell or a node kind / edge category rose). A [[constraint]] stanza adds only a CONSTRAINT cell on its anchor (engine/src/external/declared.rs; no node, edge or gap moves), so after DB.9a every rule reads `drop` ("no gap category fell and the graph did not grow") whatever it finds, and its leave-one-out build is a full rebuild that cannot differ in counts. The reverse hole is live at HEAD: a graph stanza that breaks a declared rule is judged `keep`. Probe (probe/DB9 (scratchpad spec052), the python tree with forbid_edge `scripts-no-store` scripts -> store in a version-1 overlay, anchored on the scripts PROJECT): `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia overlay try py --candidate cand_edge.toml` (one [[edge]] scripts::tool::run -> store::db::save) reports `| edge#1 | keep | — | — | CALLS +1 | dead_symbol -1 |`, verdict keep, `gaps 4→3`; with that stanza accepted, `glia check` exits 1: `[check] rules=1 checked=1 violations=1 ... [check] tiers fact=0 derived=0 heuristic=1`, `scripts::tool::run -> store::db::save` at .glia/overlay.toml:12 by overlay:edge. A second silent case the trial must name: a [[constraint]] with no `anchor` whose scope has no PROJECT is orphaned at build and never reaches check - probe: forbid_edge from "web/view.py" and from "webs" in the same tree print `[declared] ... anchored=1 orphaned=2` and `[declared] orphaned constraint id=view-no-store ... (no PROJECT)`, then `[check] rules=1`. And a rule invariant whose `in_scope` literal names a scope with no node passes vacuously: DB.2a's in_scope "yields nothing" for such a scope, and check pre-validates only forbid_edge / no_cycle / via scopes (check.rs module doc "A scope no node sits in is a rule error"; DB.3b's via error), so `violation(a) :- edge(a, b, \"CALLS\"), in_scope(a, \"webs\"), ...` holds forever. Check stays as it is (an empty in_scope literal may be intended: "nothing may live under legacy/" holds once legacy/ is gone); the trial reports it for review. Everything the delta needs exists after DB.3a / DB.3b: check::check_rules over declared_constraints, Violation.blocking / subject / file / line, check::is_blocking / min_tier_of / DEFAULT_MIN_TIER, the RULE and FORBID_PATH kinds; CodeFacts::members (DB.2a), answers::resolve_scope, and glia_rules' parser (DA.9) for the rule's literals. VERIFIER: every claim above was re-checked at HEAD (probe/DB9v), and the expected values of acceptance (1) were re-derived from that probe and from the specs of DB.2a, DB.3a and DB.3b. A scope-less invariant anchors to the root PROJECT (`[declared] ... anchor_project=3`), so c1-c4 are anchored. The rule hit's subject location web/app.py:4 is the node, not the call site at :5. DB.3a's `rotten` message contains "unknown node kind `ROUTEE`". Two identity holes were patched. no_cycle is keyed by its witness plus the member count, because review keys it by member set and a witness-only key misses a grown cycle. A forbid_edge / divergence past check::MAX_EVIDENCE gets an overflow key, because the heuristic overlay edge a stanza adds sorts past check's list and would read as no move.

packets.risks: The no-extra-build claim rests on a CONSTRAINT stanza moving no count or gap id: (1) asserts every rule stanza's marginal is empty with leave-one-out skipped, and if a later packet makes a declared rule mint a node the skip must go (the test fails first). Check runs once per rule-bearing build (2 + graph stanzas at most), with DB.3a's one CodeFacts each; a transitive rule's BFS is the costliest piece and runs per build as `glia check` would. Hit identity is textual (qnames): two repos with one qname collapse into one hit, as review's row identity does. A forbid_edge rule with more than MAX_EVIDENCE rows is compared on its listed rows plus one overflow key. A stanza that swaps one hidden row for another of the same count reads as no move, the only miss the overflow key leaves. The no_cycle key (witness + member count) can read a re-chosen witness as a move, which errs toward review. The vacuity probe reads only literal scopes in the rule's own text: a scope held in a helper predicate's variable is not probed. Determinism: BTreeMap / BTreeSet everywhere, check's output order, no HashMap iteration; byte_identical is untouched (no build output changes). PARSER_STAMP moves (engine/src): one parse-cache invalidation. If DB.3a / DB.3b rename is_blocking / min_tier_of / RULE / FORBID_PATH, this packet follows them.

packets.title: Walk reuse: split walk_source_files into a descent plan (plan_walk: gating, regions, roots, every entered directory with its mtime, every .gitignore) and the reads (read_walk) with an injectable per-file reuse and optional stat stamps; walk_source_files becomes their composition, byte-identical
packets.rationale: A watch session must not re-read every file on every update: R2-watch section 2 measured the walk + read as a fixed per-update cost, and at HEAD 22c65ee (engine/graph/parsers sources as at the v0.5.1 release; HEAD differs only in docs) the release glia warm build spends walk=124-156 ms of a 910-1095 ms build total (S1 table in DC.7a) re-reading 3,150 files of which one changed. engine/src/walk.rs walk_source_files is one function: the sequential descent (walk_dir: gitignore layers via IgnoreStack::push_dir, walk_gating::gate_dir region collapse, project_roots::detect_root reading manifest CONTENT, the migration size cap via metadata, Pending queueing by PendingClass) and the pooled reads (read_pending -> read_one: Markdown cap with source fallback, JsonSniff admission by content, Source) are welded together and return only (files, regions, md, roots). Nothing records which directories were walked (needed to detect an added / removed file by a directory mtime change, Q11), which .gitignore files gated the walk (a HIGH-durability input), or a stat per file (the session's file table). Callers at HEAD: engine/src/build/mod.rs generate_one_inner and assemble_many_with, engine/src/shared_cache/export.rs and import.rs, and 13 walk.rs unit tests; their signature stays. PRE-FIX: `grep -c 'fn plan_walk\|fn read_walk' engine/src/walk.rs` -> 0.
entry_points: engine/src/walk.rs - walk_source_files - becomes `read_walk(root, &plan_walk(root), None, false).0`; same output, same stderr lines in the same order

engine/src/walk.rs - plan_walk (new) - the descent: config load, IgnoreStack, walk_dir; returns WalkPlan; prints only the inline descent lines it prints today (`[walk] skipped engine output`, `[migrations] skipped`)

engine/src/walk.rs - read_walk (new) - read_pending generalised: per Pending an optional reuse (prior Read) and an optional FileStamp taken BEFORE the read; then merge_declared_roots, the root sort and every marker read_pending and walk_source_files print today, in today's order
engine/src/walk.rs - walk_dir - records each entered directory (rel path, mtime), each collapsed region root (rel path, mtime) and each `.gitignore` among its non-dir entry names into the plan

engine/src/walk.rs - WalkPlan, WalkedDir, FileStamp, ReadRecord (new, pub(crate))
packets.implementation:
Shapes (all pub(crate), engine-internal, glia_engine's public API is unchanged: walk is a private module):
- `struct WalkPlan { pending: Vec<Pending>, regions: Vec<RegionAnchor>, roots: Vec<ProjectRoot> /* detected, pre-merge */, declared: DeclaredDirs, projects: Vec<Spanned<ProjectDecl>> /* the config's [[project]] */, counts: GateCounts, ignore_lines: Vec<String> /* the IgnoreStack marker / config_marker strings rendered after the descent, printed by read_walk */, dirs: Vec<WalkedDir>, region_dirs: Vec<WalkedDir>, gitignores: Vec<String> }`; `struct WalkedDir { rel: String /* "" = root */, mtime: Option<SystemTime> }` (walk_dir pushes one per entered directory, from `std::fs::metadata(dir).modified()`; regions and hard-skipped dirs are not entered, so not listed); `region_dirs` = each collapsed region root (rel + mtime), pushed where walk_dir records its RegionAnchor: walk_gating::gate_dir decides a region from that directory's own direct entries (nested_repo reads `<dir>/.git`, dir_is_build_bundle its file names), so a watcher must see those entries change even though the walk never enters the dir; `gitignores` = repo-relative paths of every `.gitignore` present in an entered directory (from the `names` list walk_dir already builds), whether or not IgnoreStack pushed a layer for it.
- `struct FileStamp { len: u64, mtime: Option<SystemTime> }`; `struct ReadRecord { rel: String, class: PendingClass, read: Read, stamp: Option<FileStamp> }`, one per plan.pending entry, in plan order.
- `fn plan_walk(root: &Path) -> WalkPlan`: the first half of today's walk_source_files (config load, IgnoreStack::with_config, DeclaredDirs::new, push_dir(root), walk_dir, pop).
- `fn read_walk(root: &Path, plan: &WalkPlan, reuse: Option<&(dyn Fn(&Pending) -> Option<Read> + Sync)>, stamps: bool) -> (WalkResult, Vec<ReadRecord>)`: `par_map_ordered(&plan.pending, |p| { let stamp = stamps.then(|| stat(p)); let read = reuse.and_then(|f| f(p)).unwrap_or_else(|| read_one(p)); (stamp, read, reused) })` (the caller's reuse closure answers Some only for a prior ReadRecord with the same rel AND the same PendingClass: a re-gated path can change class), then the sequential fold read_pending does today (files / md / JsonAdmission counts in plan order), merge_declared_roots(&plan.projects, &plan.declared, &plan.regions, &mut roots), the explicit roots sort, and the markers in today's order: `[parallel] walk`, `[contract] json sniffed=`, `[contract] json over_cap=`, `[roots]`, `[walk] <counts>`, the ignore lines. With `reuse` given it also prints `[walk] reuse root=<root> reused=<r> read=<k> of <n>`. The stamp is taken before the read so a write racing the read leaves a stamp older than the content and the next stat sees the change (DC.7c adds the same-tick racy rule).
- `walk_source_files(root)` = `read_walk(root, &plan_walk(root), None, false).0`: clean builds take no stat and print exactly today's lines, so stderr-reading tests and the byte gates are untouched.
Why not cache WalkResult and patch one entry: a content edit can move a file between `files` and `md` or in / out of `files` (a .json becoming an OpenAPI contract is admitted by content; an .md over MARKDOWN_CAP falls back to source), and the fold computes the json counters; re-running the fold over reused Reads is exact by construction and costs no I/O.
Tests (walk.rs mod walk_tests): `plan_then_read_is_walk_source_files` - a temp tree with a doc .md, an OpenAPI .json, a tsconfig.json (sniffed, not admitted), .py / .go sources, a gitignored file, a node_modules region, a package.json root and a `.glia/overlay.toml` `[walk] skip` - read_walk(plan_walk) equals walk_source_files on files, md, roots (rel_path) and region rel paths; `reuse_rereads_only_changed` - read_walk with stamps, edit one file, read_walk with reuse returning the prior Read for every other rel: the reuse closure hit n-1 times, the result equals a fresh walk_source_files, only the edited file's stamp differs; `plan_records_dirs_and_gitignores` - dirs list "" and every entered subdir but no region dir, region_dirs lists the node_modules region root, gitignores lists `.gitignore` and `sub/.gitignore`, and a dir's mtime changes after a file is created in it.

AFTER: (1) `cargo test -p glia-engine --lib -- walk::walk_tests::plan_then_read_is_walk_source_files walk::walk_tests::reuse_rereads_only_changed walk::walk_tests::plan_records_dirs_and_gitignores` green (all three fail to compile on HEAD: no plan_walk / read_walk); (2) every existing walk.rs test and `cargo test -p glia-engine --test byte_identical --test parallel_build --test user_config_walk --test glia_control_dir` green; (3) the L0.6 instrument (`GLIA_PARITY_REPOS=<glia copy>:<grpc-go copy>:<Kina copy> GLIA_PARITY_OUT=<out> cargo test -p glia-engine --test build_parity -- --ignored`) run before and after the change gives `diff -r -x manifest.json` empty and identical `[parity]` lines; (4) a `glia build` of the Kina copy prints the same `[parallel] walk`, `[contract] json`, `[roots]` and `[walk]` lines before and after (diff of the grep).

MEASURED in release (timestamped GLIA_THREADS=1 glia warm build, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec052/probe/DC/ts-glia-t1.log): `[nav-pages]` 426.3 -> `[queue-const]` 431.6 = 5.3 ms, -> `[event-const]` 435.6 = 4.0 ms. packets.title: Build memos held by ParseCache (in memory, never in the sidecar): per-file const-table scans, RPC needle outputs keyed by (content hash, module id, proto service set, twirp flag), and non-code route outputs keyed by content hash; every in-process cache holder (watch, neuropil hot reload, delta / review / contract-breaks rev builds, timeline, the overlay-loop trial) stops recomputing them
packets.rationale: R2-watch section 14: RPC needles re-run on every text-gated file on every build, and nothing caches them; section 5 A1 step 4 asks for per-file memos so the grafts cost about the changed file. At HEAD 22c65ee (engine/graph/parsers sources as at the v0.5.1 release; HEAD differs only in docs): the needles are already on the pool (LG.1b: engine/src/build/rpc_needles.rs apply_rpc_needles maps needle_one with par_map_ordered) - so 'pooled' is done - but not memoised; build_const_table rescans every source file every build; route_one (engine/src/route.rs) re-runs every non-code branch every build because ParseCache only holds code parses (Routed::NonCode is never cached). MEASURED release, GLIA_THREADS=1, one-file warm builds (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec052/probe/DC/ts-*.log): grpc-go RPC needles 382 ms over 703 files (`[const]` 196.2 -> `[grpc-client]` 578.6), the whole grafts phase 408 ms; glia RPC needles 70 ms, const scan 44 ms, route 100 ms of which the 297 synthetic (yaml / json / proto / manifest / ...) parses are nearly all (1 code file reparsed). At default threads grafts is 69-112 ms. Each of these is a pure function of one file plus a small repo-wide key (needle_one reads only the file's CLASS / STRUCT / METHOD / FUNCTION nodes, which no earlier graft touches - its own doc comment; the yaml / dockerfile / manifest / dotenv / migration / json / proto / graphql / avro branches read only (path, source, repo)). DESIGN CHOICE, measured: the memo is NOT persisted in parse_cache.bin - a persisted memo would add its serialisation to every save (the no-change glia save already costs 170 ms) and widen the CE.2 shared-cache payload contract for a one-shot saving of ~60 ms at default threads; in memory it serves every caller that holds a ParseCache across builds: the watch session, generate_one_with_cache holders (neuropil does not hold one today: /home/ivy/Code/neuropil/crates/neuropil-app/src/state.rs:443 calls generate_one), graph_delta_vs_rev / review / contract-breaks (after-build then rev-build on one cache), timeline (one build per rev on one cache) and the overlay-loop trial (base + candidate + every leave-one-out on one cache).

memo.rs: `#[derive(Default)] pub(crate) struct BuildMemo { pub(crate) consts: ConstMemo, pub(crate) needles: NeedleMemo, pub(crate) noncode: NonCodeMemo, pub(crate) stats: MemoStats }`; each memo is `HashMap<String /* rel path */, (Key, Value)>` - one entry per path, overwritten on a key change, so memory is bounded by the file count. Keys / values: ConstMemo key (content_hash, lang) -> Option<ConstTable> (None = the scan panicked, replayed as the same PANIC line); NeedleMemo key (content_hash, lang, module_id, services_fp, twirp) -> Option<NeedleHalves> where `NeedleHalves { client, server, proto_rpc }` are NeedleOut's three Results (None = no half passed its text gate or the file had no parse). The memo never stores NeedleOut's `lang` / `slot` / `module_id`: `slot` is the index into parses_by_lang[lang], which shifts whenever a file is added or removed, so a hit re-derives lang and module id from the key's inputs and the slot from this build's parse_index, and a hit whose parse lookup fails is treated as no output, exactly as needle_one returns None today. The halves replay verbatim, panic strings included; NonCodeMemo key content_hash -> `(key: &'static str, fp: Option<FileParse>, tally: SynthTally)`, the parts of Routed::NonCode (Routed itself need not be Clone: its Code arm holds CodeOutcome / ExtractStats), stored only when the branch key is one of PURE_NONCODE = yaml, dockerfile, manifest, dotenv, migration, json, proto, graphql, avro (prisma reads the build-wide `prisma_provider`, the angular template reads the module plan: never memoised). `retain(&self, live: &HashSet<&str>)` drops entries of paths no longer walked. MemoStats { const_hit, const_miss, needle_hit, needle_miss, noncode_hit, noncode_miss } is reset per build.
services_fp = xxh64 over the sorted RpcContext::services' Debug strings (ProtoServiceRef derives Debug, no hash container inside); content hashes = cache::content_hash, computed once per build on the pool in parse_and_graft (only when a cache is held) and passed to parse_repo_files (which then reuses them instead of hashing code files itself: same values), build_const_table and apply_rpc_needles.
Lookups run on pool workers against `&BuildMemo` (read-only, like `cache_ro` in parse_repo_files today); misses are computed as today; inserts happen in the sequential fold after the pool returns, so no lock and no order effect. A memo hit hands back a clone: GrpcNodes, ProtoRpcNodes (extractors grpc.rs), ContractNodes (contracts.rs, inside SynthTally::contracts; ContractSource and FieldStats are already Clone) and SynthTally (route.rs) gain `Clone`. `services_fp` is a pub(crate) helper in memo.rs; the watch session's group key (DC.7b) reuses it. The fold consumes hits and misses identically, so the per-file marker lines a non-code branch emits (`[cli-decl]`, `[migrations]`, `[config]`, ...) still print in walk order on a hit.
cache.rs: ParseCache gets `#[serde(skip)] memo: BuildMemo` (Default), cleared in validate_context together with `entries` when the context changes (the memo's NodeIds carry the RepoId and the needle output depends on the module ids the go context shapes) and retained with the walked path set where retain_paths runs.
Marker, once per repo build that holds a cache: `[graft-memo] const hit=<h>/<n> needles hit=<h>/<n> noncode hit=<h>/<n> repo=<label>`.

packets.title: Split the evidence fill: each language group's intra edges are filled at group build on the pool against its own node locations and cached with the group; the Finalize pass applies those results, re-fills only the edges whose endpoint is first located in another graph, whose endpoint is foreign, or whose evidence a pass changed, and fills the cross edges; byte-identical
packets.rationale: R2-watch section 2 / 9: the evidence fill is global - every update re-fills every edge. At HEAD 22c65ee (engine/graph/parsers sources as at the v0.5.1 release; HEAD differs only in docs) engine/src/passes.rs fill_evidence_sites (the Finalize PassSpec `fill_evidence_sites` in engine/src/profile.rs CODE_PASSES) builds a first-graph-wins `at` map over every node (evidence::locate parses each POSITION JSON) and then parses every edge's EVIDENCE cell. It is the slowest pass on every repo probed: release glia `slowest_pass=fill_evidence_sites:67.4ms` (warm0, default threads), 72 ms at GLIA_THREADS=1 over 80,654 intra and 1,203 cross edges; grpc-go 40 ms; Kina 13 ms (S1 table, DC.7a). 98.5% of the work is intra edges of graphs a watch update did not rebuild. Exactness constraints found at HEAD: (a) one NodeId can sit in several language graphs (graph/src/merged.rs pass_undo doc: 'one id can sit in several per-language graphs' - a client ENDPOINT minted by two languages), and the fill locates an endpoint at its FIRST graph's instance; (b) the SCIP stage (engine/src/external/scip.rs scip_edges, run inside the external_edges Post pass) replaces intra edges' EVIDENCE cells and sets their confidence Strong in place before Finalize (restamp through edge_at_mut on EdgePos::Intra, evidence::attach); no production pass deletes or inserts an intra edge (the `g.edges.retain(.. HANDLED_BY)` in engine/src/external/overlay.rs is inside its #[cfg(test)] module, unlocatable_routes_are_never_mounted), and no pass adds a node to a graph (every `g.nodes.push` in engine/src/external and graph/src/resolvers is test code), so the edge-count check below is a guard, not a path HEAD takes; (c) LineTally's `[evidence-lines]` counts basis Site BEFORE the fill. So the group fill must not mutate edges at group build, and Finalize must detect every edge whose inputs differ.
