packets.implementation:
Model: the fill of an edge e is a pure function F(ev(e), category, At(from), At(to)) where At(id) = (evidence::locate(cells), kind, synthetic_module_file fallback) of the id's FIRST instance in graph order. No pass changes POSITION cells, kinds, qnames or names, so At is fixed at group build; only (a) the first-instance choice, (b) edge deletion and (c) evidence replacement can make a cached local result differ from the global one.
`#[derive(Clone)] pub(crate) struct GroupFill { at: Vec<(NodeId, At)> /* first-wins within the graph, node order */, ev_hash: Vec<u64> /* xxh64 of each edge's EVIDENCE payload at group build, 0 when none */, filled: Vec<(u32, Cell)> /* edges whose local fill changes the cell: index -> new EVIDENCE cell */, contrib: Vec<EdgeContrib> /* per edge: missing?, basis after the local fill, emitter index, module_file? */, emitters: Vec<String>, absent: Vec<u32> /* edges with an endpoint not in this graph */ }`. `fn fill_group_evidence(g: &RepoGraph) -> GroupFill` runs today's loop over g.edges against the graph's own `at`, recording instead of attaching. It runs in build_one on the pool worker, after LineTally (so `[evidence-lines]` is unchanged) and is cached with the LangBuild (DC.7b).
Finalize (`fill_evidence_sites_split(merged, fills)`; `fill_evidence_sites(merged)` keeps its signature as the no-fills case, because engine/src/external/mod.rs apply_external_cells calls it a second time after a cell stage wrote, and that call stays unchanged): build the global `at` from each graph's GroupFill.at when present (no POSITION parse) else by evidence::locate as today, first-wins in graph order, recording each id's owner graph. For graph i with Some(f): if `g.edges.len() != f.ev_hash.len()` (a pass deleted edges) -> fill graph i globally as today. Else per edge j: re-evaluate globally when xxh64(current evidence payload) != f.ev_hash[j] (a pass replaced it), or j in f.absent, or an endpoint's owner graph != i with an At different from graph i's own; otherwise apply f.filled's cell for j if any (a cell swap, no JSON parse) and take f.contrib[j] for the stats. Graphs with None (regions, projects, docs, every graph of a layout merge) and all cross edges take today's path. FillStats is summed per edge from contrib or the global evaluation, so `[evidence] edges=.. missing=.. site=..` and `[evidence-file]` print the same numbers. Marker: `[evidence-split] graphs=<g> group_filled=<n> refilled=<r> fallback_graphs=<f> cross=<c>`.
profile.rs: CodeBuildCtx gains `pub(crate) group_fills: Vec<Option<GroupFill>>`, `pub(crate) fn with_group_fills(self, fills) -> Self`; the PassSpec closure becomes `|m, ctx| passes::fill_evidence_sites_split(m, &ctx.group_fills).report()`. The one CodeBuildCtx struct literal outside profile.rs (engine/src/passes.rs passes_tests, the CJ.4 `[walk] tests` case) gains `group_fills: Vec::new()`. Fills are aligned with merged.graphs from DC.2's LanguageGraphs (one Option per graph, in graph order; None for regions / projects / docs), carried through build_graphs_for_repo / Assembled / finish_build. run_code_passes (merge) passes CodeBuildCtx::empty() -> no fills -> global, unchanged.
Tests (passes.rs mod passes_tests): `split_fill_equals_global_fill` builds a two-graph MergedGraph where (1) both graphs hold one ENDPOINT id with different POSITION cells and graph 1 has an unfilled CALLS edge into it, (2) graph 1 has an edge to an id only graph 0 holds, (3) a 'pass' replaces one graph-0 edge's evidence between group build and Finalize, (4) a 'pass' retains away one graph-1 edge; the split result (every edge's cells and the FillStats) equals running HEAD's global loop on an identical copy. packets.title: Scoped located delta: the delta of two builds restricted to the ids of the rebuilt graphs (every copy) and the keys of their intra edges plus every cross edge, with move detection whenever the walked file set changed; rows and counts equal the full located_delta
packets.rationale: R2-watch section 5 A1 step 8: `located_delta(prev, next)` gives a watch update its rows and 'can be scoped to dirty shards plus cross edges'. At HEAD 22c65ee (engine/graph/parsers sources as at the v0.5.1 release; HEAD differs only in docs) engine/src/delta.rs locate_delta always runs graph::identity::detect_moves_with over both whole graphs, side_parts / side over every node and all_edges(), and activation::algo::delta::graph_delta folds every node's content cells and every edge key - for glia that is every node and all 81,857 edges (`[evidence] edges=81857`) per update when one group changed. Exactness facts verified at HEAD that make scoping sound: graph_delta compares a node by the union of its CONTENT_CELLS (CODE, SCHEMA_FIELDS) over every copy of its id (activation/src/algo/delta.rs content()) and an edge by key with the strongest confidence over every copy (fold_edges); no post-pass writes CODE or SCHEMA_FIELDS (passes write TEST / ORIGIN / DECISION cells and NODE confidence: downgrade_test_paths, demote_unmatched_http_nodes); a clean group's pre-pass graph is a byte-equal clone (DC.7b). So ids outside the rebuilt graphs and intra edges of clean graphs cannot produce a row on a LOW-durability update, provided every copy of an in-scope id or key is included.

`pub(crate) struct DeltaScope { pub(crate) before: BTreeSet<usize>, pub(crate) after: BTreeSet<usize>, pub(crate) moves: bool }` - graph indices on each side that were rebuilt, vanished or added (the session passes the language groups it rebuilt plus the regions, projects and docs graphs, which it rebuilds every update). `pub(crate) struct LocatedRows { pub(crate) delta: GraphDelta, pub(crate) nodes: Vec<DeltaNode>, pub(crate) edges: Vec<DeltaEdge>, pub(crate) counts: DeltaCounts }`. `pub(crate) fn located_delta_counted(before, after, renames) -> LocatedRows` is the full delta with its DeltaCounts (locate_delta plus the counts graph_delta_vs_rev builds inline today, which move into it; graph_delta_vs_rev calls it and keeps its marker and answer): the watch session's full-delta path (DC.7a) needs the counts and cannot get regions_excluded from the public located_delta. `pub(crate) fn located_delta_scoped(before: &MergedGraph, after: &MergedGraph, scope: &DeltaScope) -> LocatedRows`:
1. D = ids of every node in the scoped graphs of both sides; K = EdgeKey of every intra edge of the scoped graphs of both sides plus every cross edge of both sides.
2. Sides: nodes = every node of every graph (graph order) with id in D, REGION ids dropped and SCHEMA_FIELDS JSON swapped for Text exactly as side / side_parts do (side_parts computed over D only; the REGION id set over all graphs - a cheap kind scan - so `regions_excluded` is the full count); edges = every edge of all_edges() with key in K and no REGION endpoint.
3. Moves: `scope.moves` (the session sets it whenever the walked file set changed: any add or remove) -> detect_moves_with(before, after, &[]) over the whole graphs as today; else no pairs. Add-only is not enough to skip it: a same-stem sibling ADD renames an existing file's MODULE qname (LB.9b / LB.13), so detect_moves sees a removed and an added MODULE on one path and pairs them by basename. With the file set unchanged, no MODULE qname moves on a LOW update (a module qname is a function of the path and the plan, and the plan of the file list), so no pair can exist.
4. graph_delta + the same located rows, sort orders and DeltaCounts as locate_delta (shared helper), Locator::new over the whole graphs.

Public API (`glia_engine::watch::*`, a public module slot; never flattened):
`pub struct WatchSession` (private fields: root, label, ident, repo, opts, plan: WalkPlan, table: BTreeMap<String, ReadRecord> (rel -> class, Read, FileStamp), walk: WalkResult, setup (go modules + context key, ts aliases, include roots, RepoInputs, overlay fingerprint), cache: ParseCache (DC.4's memo inside), result: GenerateResult, seq: u64). `pub fn open(root: &str, opts: &BuildOptions) -> Result<Self, String>` (Err: not a directory, or the build's error); `pub fn apply(&mut self, changed: &[PathBuf]) -> Result<WatchUpdate, String>`; `pub fn result(&self) -> &GenerateResult`; `pub fn persist(&self, dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String>` = persist::persist_result(&self.result, dir, "watch") (the caller enforces the overlay=false default-dir rule, as `glia build` and save_to_default do); `pub fn save_cache(&self) -> std::io::Result<()>` = cache.save(root) (LC.11 write-if-changed); `pub fn seq(&self) -> u64`.
`#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct WatchUpdate { seq: u64, files: WatchFiles, groups_rebuilt: Vec<String>, full_rebuild: Option<String>, total_nodes: usize, total_edges: usize, counts: DeltaCounts, nodes: Vec<DeltaNode>, edges: Vec<DeltaEdge>, phase_ms: WatchPhases }` (all pub); `WatchFiles { added, modified, removed: Vec<String> /* repo-relative, sorted */, reparsed: usize, reused: usize /* ParseCache stats */ }`; `WatchPhases { read, walk, parse, const_scan, grafts, language_build, resolve, post, finalize, external_cells, delta, total: f64 }` in ms truncated to 0.1 like timing::ms - parse / const_scan / grafts / language_build from PhaseTimes, resolve / post / finalize from the PassReport stage times, external_cells from DC.2's Finished.times, delta and total timed here (CA.9's timers, stderr only in clean builds; here they also ride the update). DC.7b adds the `fingerprint` and `clone` fields when it fills them. WatchUpdate, WatchFiles, WatchPhases and the Durability enum are all #[non_exhaustive] (engine/tests/api_stability.rs scans every top-level item of a `pub mod` slot).
Durability (`pub enum Durability { Low, High(&'static str) }`, `pub fn durability(rel: &str) -> Durability`): High for `.glia/**` except `.glia/graph/**` ("glia_inputs"), any `.gitignore` ("gitignore"), `go.mod` ("go_mod"), `tsconfig.json` / `tsconfig.base.json` ("tsconfig"), `CMakeLists.txt` / `compile_commands.json` ("include_roots"), a project-root manifest (a basename in glia_code_domain::project_roots::MANIFESTS or an extension in project_roots::MANIFEST_EXTS, the .NET `*.csproj` / `*.sln` family) or packages::is_manifest_path ("manifest": root detection reads manifest content, and a .NET project gates its bin/obj regions), a migration path ("migration": the descent's size cap), `.git/HEAD` / `.git/config` ("identity"); Low otherwise. Salsa's durability: a Low-only update skips re-planning the walk and recomputing every repo-level input.
apply(changed): normalise to repo-relative `/` paths (absolute ones must lie under root; others counted `outside=`); drop `.glia/graph/**`, `.git/**` other than `.git/HEAD` / `.git/config`, and any path two or more levels below a region root (WalkPlan.region_dirs: a collapsed directory's contents never reach the graph, so edits deep in node_modules / target / a nested clone cost nothing). A DIRECT child of a region root (`<region>/<name>`) triggers a replan instead: gate_dir decides the region from exactly those entries (a nested `.git`, a bundle's chunk files), so removing a nested clone's `.git` must un-collapse it. Replan when any path is High, known-and-missing, a directory, unknown-and-existing, or an ancestor of a table entry or a WalkPlan.dirs entry (a deleted directory: it exists no more and is in no table); else re-read only the named table entries (read_one rule of their class, stamp first) and drop the ones whose Read is unchanged. Replan: plan_walk, then read_walk(stamps, reuse = the table's ReadRecord for every rel not named, when its class is unchanged). The noop test runs after either path: when the table's (rel, class, Read) set is unchanged and no High input fingerprint moved -> return an update with empty files and no rows, seq unchanged, print `[watch] noop repo=<label> paths=<n>` (an unknown path that the walk still does not admit, say a gitignored file, costs one replan and a noop). The caller names every changed path; a path apply is not told about is not re-read (poll(), DC.7c, finds them itself). High: recompute repo_identity, go_modules_for (+ cache.validate_context), TsAliasSet::read and, when a `.glia/` path changed, external::repo_inputs. IncludeRoots::read runs on every replan, not only on High: its search dirs are filtered by the dirs that hold a walked C/C++ file (HeldDirs::of over the file list), so adding a .c / .h file in a new directory can change them; the overlay fingerprint is xxh64(opts.overlay, overlay file bytes). The proto service set (RpcContext::add_files) and rust_crates are recomputed every update from the in-memory files (cheap). full_rebuild = Some(reason) when the identity key changed ("identity"), the go module context changed ("go_modules": the cache discards every parse), the overlay fingerprint changed ("overlay") or the service set changed ("proto_services"). Then the DC.2 stages with Some(&mut self.cache): parse_and_graft -> plan_groups -> build_groups(all None in this packet) -> fold_groups -> repo_markers -> aux_graphs -> finish_build(with DC.5 fills), the same calls generate_one_inner makes, so the result is a clean build of the current tree by construction. Delta: delta::located_delta_counted(&prev.merged, &next.merged, &[]) (DC.6: rows sorted by delta.rs, DeltaCounts included); seq += 1; swap result; prev dropped after the delta (peak = cache + prev + next). Every new piece of state (table, plan, repo inputs, result) is built in locals and committed only when the update succeeded, so an Err (or a caught panic in an embedding app) leaves the session at its previous consistent state; the parse cache may hold the new parses, which are content-keyed and stay valid.
Markers: `[watch] open repo=<label> files=<n> groups=<g> nodes=<N> edges=<E> took=<ms>`; per update `[watch] update seq=<s> files +<a> ~<m> -<r> groups_rebuilt=<k>/<g> full_rebuild=<reason|none> nodes +<a> -<d> ~<m> >\<v> edges +<a> -<r> ~<c> took=<ms> repo=<label>`; the build's own `[timing] repo=` / `[timing] build` lines print per update as in a clean build. Declared marker difference (R2 section 8): an update prints the stage markers of what it ran, never gate on marker equality with a clean build.
Unit tests (watch.rs tests, temp repos only): `open_persists_like_a_clean_build` (persist -> bytes == generate_one + persist_result into a sibling dir: relative roots equal); `body_edit_matches_clean` (apply([a.py]) -> files.modified == ["a.py"], a `modified` node row for the edited fn, persisted bytes == clean); `add_delete_replan` (add then delete b.go via apply: added / removed lists, bytes == clean each step); `go_mod_is_a_full_rebuild` (full_rebuild == Some("go_modules")); `noop_keeps_seq` (apply of an untouched path: seq unchanged, no rows); `durability_table` (each High reason and three Low paths).
INTEGRATOR (0.5.2 merge, DE.10 cross-group): right after the previous result drops (after the delta), apply calls glia_engine::memory::release_freed_memory("watch_update") (DE.10, a dependency): the measured fix is a trim after the old graph is freed (208 -> 271 MB over 40 rebuilds; a trim before the swap 207 -> 383). The `[memory] malloc_trim site=watch_update` line prints per update on glibc (GLIA_MALLOC_TRIM=0 turns it off). DF.4a and DD.7 (dependencies) land first: the High setup also computes DF.4a's DartPackages from the walk's ProjectRoots beside rust_crates and passes it to DC.2's stage fns, and the pass context is CodeBuildCtx::new(inputs, opts) as DD.7 leaves it (so the identity pass reads the same SCIP snapshots as a clean build). Release numbers (S1 table, DC.7a): the language build is 457-527 ms of glia's 910-1095 ms warm total and 634-664 ms of grpc-go's; glia's rust group alone is 394 ms at GLIA_THREADS=1 while the other 25 graphs take 36 ms, so a Python edit in glia pays ~400 ms it does not need after DC.7a. A group's graph is a pure function of its ordered post-graft parses plus the inputs its builder reads (engine/src/build/lang_build.rs build_solo: rust_crates for build_rust, the IncludeRoots resolver for build_c_cpp; build_typescript_family: ts_aliases; repo for all) - the cache holds PRE-graft parses (grafts.rs apply_post_cache runs after it), so the fingerprint must be taken after the grafts. packets.implementation:
cache.rs: `pub(crate) fn parse_fingerprint(fp: &FileParse) -> u64` - `struct HashWriter(XxHash64)` implementing io::Write, `bincode::serialize_into(&mut w, &Canonical(fp))` where Canonical's Serialize calls canonical_parse; same bytes CacheEntry::payload writes for the parse, so two parses fingerprint equal iff their canonical bytes are equal.
watch.rs, per update after parse_and_graft + plan_groups: per group, `par_map_ordered(&group.parses, parse_fingerprint)`, then `group_fp = xxh64(key, repo.0, overlay_fp, services_fp, hidden_fp(key), [parse fps in order])` with services_fp = xxh64 over the sorted RpcContext::services' Debug strings, overlay_fp from DC.7a, hidden_fp("rust") = xxh64(Debug(rust_crates)), hidden_fp(TS_GROUP) = xxh64(Debug(ts_aliases)), hidden_fp("c_cpp") = xxh64(Debug(c_includes)), else 0 (Debug of these types holds only Vec / String / Option: deterministic). reuse[i] = a clone of the cached LangBuild whose key and fingerprint match, else None; build_groups builds the None ones on the pool; the cache is then refreshed in plan order (vanished keys dropped): a reused entry stays where it is (it was cloned OUT for the build), a rebuilt group's LangBuild is cloned IN before fold_groups moves its graph into the merged graph. So every group costs exactly one deep clone per update (the passes mutate node confidence, cells and intra-edge evidence, so a cached pre-pass graph can never be handed over by reference); the time is WatchPhases.clone. groups_rebuilt = keys built, plan order. Because overlay_fp and services_fp are in every key, an overlay or service-set change rebuilds every group (consistent with DC.7a's full_rebuild reasons).
Delta: when the update was LOW-only and full_rebuild is None -> delta::located_delta_scoped with scope = graph indices of the rebuilt groups on both sides (a graph index maps to its group through DC.2's LanguageGraphs.keys, kept per side; a new or vanished group is in scope on the side that has it) plus the regions / projects / docs graphs (always rebuilt), moves = the walked file set changed (any add or remove, DC.6); otherwise delta::located_delta_counted. services_fp is DC.4's memo.rs helper. WatchPhases gains `fingerprint` (the per-parse fingerprints and group keys) and `clone` (the cache clones above), both #[non_exhaustive]-safe additions.
Tests (watch.rs tests): `python_body_edit_rebuilds_only_python` (repo with python + go + ts + rust: groups_rebuilt == ["python"], bytes == clean); `tsconfig_paths_edit_rebuilds_typescript` (groups_rebuilt contains "typescript", not "rust", bytes == clean); `cargo_member_add_rebuilds_rust` (new workspace member crate: contains "rust", bytes == clean); `proto_service_change_rebuilds_all` (full_rebuild == Some("proto_services"), every key rebuilt); `scoped_delta_equals_full` (for each of the above, the update's rows == located_delta(prev_clean, next_clean) rows); `cached_error_keeps_clean_order` (inject a cached LangBuild whose graph is Err("x graph: e") for a clean group: result.parse_errors holds it at the fold position a clean build with that error would).

packets.title: WatchSession::poll and changed_paths: stat-poll of the walked file table, directory re-lists on a changed directory mtime, the racy-mtime rule, and explicit watching of the inputs the walk does not read (.gitignore files, .glia/ inputs, CMakeLists.txt, compile_commands.json under build*/, .git/HEAD and .git/config); no notify crate
packets.rationale: Q11 (plan 0.1): 'stat-poll of the walked file table plus directory re-lists; no notify crate' - R2-watch section 11 Q1 option (a): deterministic, no dependency, no event storms (the class of bug behind repo-graph's 1.2 TB read-event loop, 2026-09-19). The session needs it for `glia watch` (DC.8) and pyo3 poll() (DC.9). What a stat-poll must cover, verified at HEAD 22c65ee (engine/graph/parsers sources as at the v0.5.1 release; HEAD differs only in docs): (1) file edits - the table from DC.1 read_walk stamps (len, mtime); (2) adds / deletes / renames - a directory's mtime changes when an entry is added or removed, and DC.1 records every entered directory; (3) inputs read OUTSIDE the walk: engine/src/build/c_includes.rs reads `CMakeLists.txt` beside walked C/C++ files ('the walk admits no CMakeLists.txt') and `compile_commands.json` at each root and in its depth-1 `build*/` dirs (usually gitignored regions), code-domain walk_gating IgnoreStack::push_dir reads every `.gitignore`, glia_config::load reads `.glia/overlay.toml` (`.glia` is a hard skip of the walk), the snapshot readers read `.glia/*-snapshot/`, repo_identity reads `.git`; (4) coarse timestamps - Linux file times tick at the kernel's coarse clock, so a same-length rewrite inside one tick keeps (len, mtime); git's racy-index rule is the standard answer.
entry_points: engine/src/watch.rs - WatchSession::changed_paths(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> (new, pub) - the stat scan, no rebuild (for a caller that debounces)
engine/src/watch.rs - WatchSession::poll(&mut self) -> Result<Option<WatchUpdate>, String> (new, pub) - changed_paths then apply when non-empty
engine/src/watch.rs - WatchSession - `watched: Vec<(String, Option<FileStamp>)>` (inputs outside the table) and `scanned_at: SystemTime`, refreshed at open and after every replan
packets.implementation:
changed_paths: (a) stat every table entry (std::fs::metadata; missing -> the path); differs in len or mtime -> the path; (b) racy rule: an entry whose recorded mtime is not older than the session's previous `scanned_at` minus 2 s is re-hashed (content_hash of a fresh read) and reported when the hash moved, until its mtime ages past that window - so a same-length, same-tick rewrite is still seen; (c) stat every WalkPlan.dirs entry and every WalkPlan.region_dirs root (DC.1): a moved mtime or a vanished dir reports the dir path (apply replans on a directory); a region root's mtime moves when its direct entries change, which is what gate_dir reads (a nested clone losing its `.git` un-collapses); (d) stat every `watched` input: plan.gitignores, every file under `<root>/.glia/` except `graph/` (read_dir recursion, sorted), `CMakeLists.txt` in each dir holding a walked C/C++ file, `compile_commands.json` at each project root and in its depth-1 `build*` dirs, `.git/HEAD` and `.git/config` when present; a changed, new or vanished one is reported. Output sorted and deduplicated (BTreeSet): deterministic. poll() = changed_paths, then `apply(&paths)` when non-empty (apply re-checks content, so a touch with unchanged bytes gives the noop update and poll returns None). apply refreshes table stamps, `watched` and `scanned_at`.
Marker, only when a scan found something: `[watch] poll files=<n> dirs=<d> watched=<w> changed=<c> racy=<k> took=<ms> repo=<label>`.
Tests (watch.rs tests; mtimes set explicitly with std::fs::File::set_modified so no test sleeps on clock ticks): `poll_sees_edit_add_delete` (each -> Some(update) with the right files lists; then None when quiet); `poll_relists_a_changed_dir` (new file in a subdir -> the dir reported -> added; then delete the `.git` dir of a nested clone the walk collapsed to a region -> the region root reported -> its files are added and the region anchor removed, bytes == clean); `racy_same_length_rewrite_is_seen` (rewrite with equal length, set_modified back to the recorded mtime inside the window -> Some(update)); `poll_watches_inputs_outside_the_walk` (edit `.glia/overlay.toml` -> full_rebuild == Some("overlay"); edit a `.gitignore` to drop a file -> removed; edit CMakeLists.txt beside a .cpp -> rebuilt c_cpp); `touch_without_change_is_none` (set_modified only -> poll() == None, seq unchanged).

packets.implementation:
Args: `repo: String` (positional); `--persist-every ` u64 default 60 (0 = only on exit); `--poll-ms ` u64 default 500, clamped to >= 10; `--debounce-ms ` u64 default 200. Global `--no-overlay` -> `error: --no-overlay: watch persists into the default gmap dir, which holds the overlay-applied graph` and exit 2 (the rule `glia build` applies without --out). run: `WatchSession::open(repo, &build_options())` (Err -> `error: ..`, exit 2); print the ready line `{"ready":true,"seq":0,"repo":,"total_nodes":N,"total_edges":E}`; install the flags: unix `signal(SIGINT=2)` and `signal(SIGTERM=15)` with an `extern "C" fn(i32)` handler that only stores `true` into a static AtomicBool (async-signal-safe); non-unix: none (Ctrl-C then ends the process without the exit persist; stdin EOF still persists - stated in the doc comment); a detached thread reads stdin to EOF and sets a second AtomicBool. Loop: sleep poll_ms in 10 ms slices checking the flags; `session.changed_paths()`; merge the result into a pending `BTreeMap>` (the CLI stats each pending path itself); ACTIVITY on a tick = the pending set grew or a pending path's (len, mtime) moved since the previous tick (changed_paths keeps reporting an edited path until it is applied, so 'non-empty' alone is never quiet); pending non-empty and no activity for debounce_ms -> `session.apply(&pending paths)`, clear it; an update whose seq moved -> `serde_json::to_string(&update)` + `\n` on a locked stdout, flushed (one object per update, nodes / edges in delta.rs order); mark dirty. When persist_every > 0, dirty and the interval elapsed -> persist, right after that tick's poll / apply (CD.7c writes a CODE cell as a span only when the file on disk still matches, so persisting a graph that is behind the disk would write text cells). On a flag: apply any pending set, then persist (always on exit: the store skips unchanged shards) and exit 0. Persist = `session.persist(&default_layout_dir(repo))` + `session.save_cache()`; an Err -> `error: ..` exit 5 (glia build's code). Markers: `[watch] listening repo= poll_ms=

debounce_ms= persist_every=`, `[watch] persisted seq= reason=interval|exit`, `[watch] exit reason=sigint|sigterm|stdin_eof`. packets.implementation:
`#[pyclass(name = "WatchSession")] pub(crate) struct PyWatchSession { session: glia_engine::watch::WatchSession, repo: String, overlay: bool }`.
`#[new] #[pyo3(signature = (repo, overlay=true))] fn new(py, repo: &str, overlay: bool) -> PyResult<Self>`: `py.detach(|| WatchSession::open(repo, &BuildOptions::default().with_overlay(overlay)))`, Err -> ValueError (the generate convention for a build error).
`fn apply(&mut self, py, paths: Vec<String>) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>>`: py.detach(apply(paths as PathBuf)), Err -> RuntimeError; returns `convert::to_py(py, update_json(&update))`: a dict with keys seq, files {added, modified, removed, reparsed, reused}, groups_rebuilt, full_rebuild, total_nodes, total_edges, counts, nodes, edges, phase_ms.
`fn poll(&mut self, py) -> PyResult<Option<Py<PyAny>>>`: py.detach(poll), None when nothing changed.
`fn snapshot(&self) -> PyGraph`: `PyGraph::from_result(self.session.result().clone()).with_overlay_applied(self.overlay)` - an independent graph, so later updates never mutate a snapshot the caller still serves.
`fn persist(&self, py) -> PyResult<()>`: `graph::default_dir_refusal(self.overlay)` -> ValueError (an overlay=False session never writes the default dir, as save_to_default); else py.detach(persist(default_layout_dir(repo)) then save_cache()), Err -> OSError. packets.implementation:
`struct SplitMix64(u64)` with `next() -> u64` (x += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; z = (x ^ (x >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9; z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB; z ^ (z >> 31)). Operations (weighted pick from next() % total): body edit of a random python / go / ts / rust file (append a statement inside the last function); declaration add (a new function plus a call to it from a sibling file); file add (a new python or go file with one function); file delete (of a file the sequence added); rename (move a file the sequence added to a new name); same-stem add / remove (`api/user.ts`); markdown edit; no-op touch (File::set_modified only); go.mod module toggle; tsconfig paths toggle; .proto rpc toggle; overlay `[constants]` toggle. Each op is applied through `apply(&[touched paths])` when next() is even, else through `poll()` after setting a strictly increasing mtime with File::set_modified (no sleeps). Seeds: `[1, 2, 3, 4]` x 15 steps by default; `GLIA_WATCH_PARITY_SEEDS=` / `GLIA_WATCH_PARITY_STEPS=` widen it for a soak run. After every step the DC.10a assertions run (persisted bytes, parse_errors, pass_undo, rows == full delta); a failure message names `seed= step= op= path=

` so the sequence replays exactly. Every op sequence also keeps a mirror of the expected file set so `files.added / removed` are asserted against it.

packets.title: activation::algo::classes: a union-find over NodeIds (min-id representative, path compression) and a Quotient<G: GraphSource> adapter that maps every node to its class representative and drops the edges a class swallows
packets.rationale: Cross-repo identity (plan section 2 DD, R2-identity section 5) needs equivalence classes over node ids and a view of a graph in which each class is ONE node, so a walk (reach::bfs, PPR) crosses a class at zero hops instead of needing a carry edge between copies (the carry-edge interplay R2 section 11 warns about: SHARES_SCHEMA is a carry edge, so a pair joined by it AND by identity double-walks unless every walk runs over one quotient). MEASURED at HEAD 84e2e71: `ls activation/src/algo` = community.rs cut.rs cycles.rs delta.rs hubs.rs linkpred.rs minhash.rs mod.rs reach.rs timeline.rs; `grep -rniE "union.?find|UnionFind|Quotient" activation/src graph/src engine/src` finds only community.rs's `WeightedGraph::quotient`, an UNDIRECTED, WEIGHTED, dense-index view for Leiden aggregation that drops edge categories and is no GraphSource, so Adjacency::carry / reach::bfs / ActivationPlan::rank cannot run on it. Generic graph algorithms live in activation::algo over GraphSource (CLAUDE.md design rule), so the union-find and the quotient go here, domain-free: the caller names the categories and an edge filter (the engine passes SAME_AS and the rule tiers it collapses). R2 section 4 rejects egg / egglog (a new dependency that moves PARSER_STAMP, unstable e-class ids, and no rewriting to do): a hand-rolled union-find by minimum id is deterministic and small.

packets.rationale: Every identity rule needs a KEY, and three of them must agree with code that already exists. (a) Contract ops: the plan says the contract-op class shares CC.8's op-key normaliser. At HEAD that normaliser is private: engine/src/contract_breaks.rs `fn key_of(h: &Holder)` builds `METHOD path` / `action channel` / `channel` from the op's ORIGIN, and the graph crate (where the resolver lives) cannot call the engine; code-domain is the one crate both see (and it already depends on serde_json). (b) Packages vs projects, spike S1 MEASURED at HEAD with `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia merge /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec052/probe/DD/s1/lib /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec052/probe/DD/s1/app --out m.json` (a lib repo with five manifests, an app repo depending on each): npm PROJECT label `@org/lib` == PACKAGE_DEP `package:npm:@org/lib`; go PROJECT label `github.com/org/lib` (ecosystem `go`) == `package:gomod:github.com/org/lib` (ecosystem `gomod`); composer label `org/lib` (ecosystem `php`) == `package:composer:org/lib`; python label `My_Lib` vs `package:pypi:my-lib` (needs PEP 503: lowercase, runs of `-_.` -> `-`); cargo label `my-lib` vs `package:cargo:my_lib` (the scanner records the dependency KEY of `my_lib = { path = .., package = "my-lib" }`; crates.io treats `-` and `_` as one name, so folding `-` -> `_` matches). Ruby (Gemfile has no package label), maven / gradle / dart / elixir / dotnet (no PACKAGE_DEP extraction: parsers/code/extractors/src/packages.rs 'Out of scope') have no pair. (c) SCIP: a symbol is `scheme manager package version descriptor...` (code-domain/src/snapshots.rs ScipSymbolRecord, e.g. the committed fixture scip-python-dict-dispatch: "scip-python python svc 0.1 `svc.repos`/UserRepo#save()."); cross-repo navigation treats package + descriptor as the identity (R2 section 8), and CE.1d binds by position, never by parsing the string, so the parse is a new, declared use. (d) `diverged` (R2 section 5, Q18): two copies with one key whose content differs. SCHEMA_FIELDS payloads say it for messages and contract ops; for code, graph/src/identity.rs hashes whitespace-collapsed CODE text with FNV, which cannot be recomputed when a layout loads a CODE cell as an unresolved CodeSpan (CD.7c: `{"code_span":{..,"xxh64":..}}` when the source moved). xxh64 of the CODE bytes equals the span's own xxh64 (code-domain/src/code_span.rs CodeSpan::of hashes the verbatim slice, seed 0), so a digest that reads either form gives one answer with or without sources - what merge == joint build needs.

Three consumers read the same rows: the resolver (graph crate, which reads CODE_TABLES directly) for the kinds each rule pairs and the edge confidence, why::tier_of for the tier of a SAME_AS edge (otherwise every `resolver:` edge tiers DERIVED, engine/src/why.rs stage_tier, and a manifest-declared package class is FACT, R2 section 3), and the engine's collapse (Q17: FACT and DERIVED classes collapse, HEURISTIC never, Q18). A fourth column, `walk`, says whether a class is contracted in WALKS (blast, trace, tests_for, liveness): a class of one external package (`package:npm:react` in two repos) must collapse in rows but not merge in walks, or every module depending on react in every repo joins every blast radius (the hub fan-out SHARES_DATA_SOURCE is kept out of carry_edges for, code-domain/src/lib.rs). packets.implementation:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum IdentityTier { Fact, Derived, Heuristic }   // Ord: Fact < Derived < Heuristic (weakest = max)
impl IdentityTier { pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str /* fact|derived|heuristic */; pub fn collapses(self) -> bool /* != Heuristic */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IdentityRule {
  pub name: &'static str,          // the SAME_AS EVIDENCE rule; never contains '/' (the `<rule>/diverged` qualifier)
  pub from: &'static [NodeKindId], // member kinds on one side
  pub to: &'static [NodeKindId],   // ... and the other (equal lists for a same-kind rule)
  pub key: &'static str,           // what the members share, one line for `glia identity` and the docs
  pub tier: IdentityTier,
  pub walk: bool,                  // contracted in walks; a Heuristic rule never walks
}
```
CODE_TABLES.identity_rules, in this order: package_name (PACKAGE_DEP, PACKAGE_DEP; key "package:<eco>:<name>, ecosystem-normalised"; Fact; walk false) | manifest_name (PACKAGE_DEP, PROJECT; key "dependency name == manifest label (per ecosystem)"; Fact; walk true - a PROJECT has no edges, so contracting it with its dependents fans out only to the library's real consumers) | message_fqname (MESSAGE_TYPE, MESSAGE_TYPE; key "message:<flavor>:<fq name>"; Fact; walk true) | contract_op (DOC_SECTION, DOC_SECTION; key "METHOD + normalised path, or action + channel, under one project"; Derived; walk true) | contract_route (DOC_SECTION, DOC_SECTION; key "the one ROUTE the op's path matches"; Derived; walk true) | scip_symbol (FUNCTION METHOD CLASS STRUCT INTERFACE ENUM ATTRIBUTE STATE_VAR - the SCIP stage's DEF_KINDS - both sides; key "SCIP scheme manager package descriptor"; Fact; walk true) | body_hash (MODULE FUNCTION METHOD CLASS STRUCT INTERFACE ENUM, both; key "path-suffix files, name chain, byte-identical body"; Heuristic; walk false) | path_suffix (same kinds; key "path-suffix files under a confirmed vendoring offset, body differs"; Heuristic; walk false). validate() adds, each error naming `identity_rules[i]`: a name empty, containing '/', or repeated; an empty or unregistered kind list; a Heuristic rule with walk == true. Nothing else reads the field yet, so no behaviour changes in this packet. TOY_TABLES and the two activation test literals take `identity_rules: &[]` (the `..TABLES` update literals follow). packets.title: PROJECT ORIGIN records where its label came from (label_source: manifest | dir | root | declared), so a dependency is matched only against a label the manifest itself declared
packets.rationale: The package <-> project rule (R2 section 3: 'PACKAGE_DEP name == PROJECT ORIGIN (ecosystem, label)', FACT because both sides are declared) is only FACT when the label is the manifest's name. At HEAD a PROJECT's label falls back silently: code-domain/src/project_roots.rs ProjectRoot::new takes `label.or_else(|| basename of rel_path).unwrap_or("root")`, and engine/src/walk.rs build_project_graph writes ORIGIN {provenance, ecosystem, manifest, label, path} with no trace of which. So a package.json with no `name` in `packages/utils` is labelled `utils` and would wrongly be 'the same thing' as `package:npm:utils` from the registry. MEASURED in the S1 probe (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec052/probe/DD/s1): every manifest that names its package gives the right label (5/5), and the app repo's three PROJECTs are all labelled `app` - from their manifests, indistinguishable at HEAD from a basename fallback. Recording the source is one ORIGIN key; every reader parses ORIGIN as JSON by key (engine/src/answers.rs project_roots, the eventbus resolver test, glia projects), and the one fixture pin is a `contains` substring (walk-project-roots key.json `\"provenance\":\"project_root\"`). A NodeId in several per-language graphs is counted once (first graph). False identity: contract_route inherits the HTTP matcher's tiers - an op declared by a service that does not serve it anchors to the service that does, the same pairing link_contract_routes already draws as DOCUMENTS (contract-per-file-identity: billing's GET /orders anchors to orders' route); the `any` tier and ambiguous lookups never anchor. contract_op refuses ops with no owning PROJECT. Pairing is CROSS-REPO only (two directories of one repo are its own business): per repo, an index BTreeMap<(kind, local, basename), BTreeMap<path, Vec<(NodeId, Option<u64>)>>>. For every repo pair (A, B) in first-graph order and every key both hold, each A path is looked up in B's path map for that key under itself and every proper `/`-suffix of itself (and B's paths against A's the same way), so a pair is found in O(path depth), never by an all-pairs scan of a big bucket (a thousand `constructor`s in `index.ts`). A found pair has an offset: (the prefix stripped on A's side, on B's side) - one of them is "", both for identical paths. offset_groups: BTreeMap<(repo A, repo B, offset), Vec<pair>>; a group is CONFIRMED when one of its pairs has two equal Some digests. The rules are HEURISTIC and never collapse or walk (DD.3's table), so a false class costs a report row, not a wrong answer. Cost: per-repo-pair lookups are O(candidates x path depth); quokka's ~3,000 declarations pair in well under a second. Determinism: BTreeMaps, first-graph repo order, NodeId-sorted members. UTF-8: suffixes are taken at `/` byte boundaries of valid UTF-8 paths (`/` is ASCII), never inside a char. A MODULE whose CODE is truncated by a cap would digest its prefix only; equal prefixes then confirm - acceptable for a HEURISTIC candidate. Coverage limit by design: a copy kept under node_modules/ or vendor/ (or any always_region / gitignored dir) is a REGION anchor with no parsed nodes, so it forms no candidate; the detector covers subtree / copied-directory vendoring (quokka-stack/quokka_web/, Kina backend/internal/config). graph/src/resolvers/identity.rs is also edited by DD.5 and DD.7: DD.7 now depends on this packet.

1. EDGES. `edges.sort_by(|a, b| (a.from.as_str(), a.kind, a.to.as_str(), a.weight.map(f32::to_bits)).cmp(&(b.from.as_str(), b.kind, b.to.as_str(), b.weight.map(f32::to_bits))))` - engram_core::EdgeKind derives Ord (declaration order; diff.rs's EdgeId already sorts by it), so the order is engram-core's own and no engram-core edit is needed. Alternative weighed: sort glia's cross edges by qname in the engine - rejected, the engine's canonical order is NodeId by design and the layout bytes are RepoId-specific anyway.
2. HINTS. In build_identity_hints carry the node's qname (`g.nav.qname_by_id`) and end row into `positioned`; group as today by (token, kind); sort each group by (start_line, end_line, qname, id.0). Ordinals change only inside a row-tie (the measured 0 / 5 / 12 nodes); count those whose rank the qname decided into stats.hint_row_ties. Alternative weighed: the byte column of the name in the start row (source order) - rejected: POSITION has no column and a name search in the row is a heuristic; alphabetical inside one row shifts nothing a row insert does not already shift.
3. KEY RANK. `type KeyRank = (bool, bool, bool, Reverse<u32>)` with `Reverse(kind.map_or(u32::MAX, |k| k.0))`; within one repo a qname and kind name one NodeId, so this is total there; a cross-repo tie keeps the Reverse((gi, ni)) (argument order). stats.key_kind_ties counts winners whose rank differed from the runner-up only in the kind.
4. INHERITDOC. via_heritage: `targets.iter().filter_map(qname_of).filter(|q| last segment == base).min()` (BTreeSet semantics, no order dependence).

diff_gmaps stays a pure function of the two gmaps (CK.2's rule): the words come from Symbol.name / the key, the parent from the key, the slot from the hint.
1. name_words: iterate chars; a boundary at a non-alphanumeric, at lower/digit -> upper, and before the last upper of an upper run followed by a lower (`SMRWith` -> smr, with); lower-case; empty words dropped; BTreeSet<String>.
2. words_fit(b, t): both Symbols (or both Propositions); words non-empty on both sides; jaccard >= 1/3 (integer test 3*|A∩B| >= |A∪B|) or A ⊆ B or B ⊆ A. same_parent(b, t): parent(b.key) == parent(t.key), parent stripping the last `::` segment (owner-suffixed route-like keys never reach here). The words pass needs both; the hint guard needs words_fit only.
3. pair_words: groups BTreeMap<(token, kind), (Vec<b>, Vec<t>)> over unmatched hinted non-route-like nodes (as pair_names). For each b: among the t with same_parent and words_fit, the one with the highest Jaccard (integer-compared as cross products), unique (a tie -> none); symmetric for t; pair when mutual. Snapshot once per group (pairs inside a group are mutual-best, so iteration order cannot change them). Count stats.by_words.
4. Hint pass guard: `route_pair_ok(b, t) && (is_route_like(b) || words_fit(b, t))`; a refusal counts hint_refused as today. A hint pair whose names are equal still passes (A ⊆ B), whatever the parents: the members of a moved file or of a renamed class whose names the name pass found ambiguous keep pairing by hint, as at HEAD. packets.implementation:
1. activation::algo::ppr::push_ppr: Andersen, Chung and Lang's push over the undirected view of `adj` (each node's outgoing and incoming incidences, the private Adjacency::outgoing / incoming the algo modules already use; a self-loop counted once). Weighted degree d(u) = sum of weight(category) over incidences; a node with d(u) = 0 keeps its residual as score. State: p, r as Vec<f64> over the dense index; a FIFO VecDeque of dense indices seeded with the seed; push u while r[u] >= epsilon * d(u): p[u] += alpha * r[u]; for each incidence (v, c): r[v] += (1 - alpha) * r[u] * weight(c) / d(u); enqueue v when it crosses its threshold and is not queued; r[u] = 0. Incidences in edge order (Adjacency parity rule 2), the queue FIFO, so the result is a pure function of the index. Returns every (NodeId, p) with p > 0, sorted by p descending then dense index. alpha is the restart probability (glia's damping 0.5 -> alpha 0.5). Doc: the guarantee |p - ppr| <= epsilon * d(v) per node, and work <= 1 / (epsilon * alpha) pushes.
2. Oracle tests (ppr.rs): on a 6-node weighted toy graph (ToyGraph helpers) push_ppr with epsilon 1e-9 matches a dense power iteration of the same undirected, weighted, restart-0.5 walk to 1e-6 per node; epsilon 1e-3 keeps the top-3 order; a dangling seed returns itself with p = 1 - accumulated; the same input twice gives bit-identical output.
3. engram-export ppr_side: build a GraphSource whose node_ids are NodeId(i) for gmap.nodes[i] and edges are glia_core::Edge { from, to (by key lookup; an edge to a key not exported is skipped), category: EdgeCategoryId(kind_index), confidence Strong, cells: [] }; weight(c) = the exported weight of that EdgeKind (the exporter's CATEGORY_MAP weights are per glia category; on the gmap the edge's own `weight.unwrap_or(1.0)` is what Engram multiplies, so the GraphSource carries one category per distinct (EdgeKind, weight bits) pair, mapped back to that weight). For every Symbol and Proposition fact in gmap order: push_ppr(seed, alpha 0.5, epsilon 1e-3), drop the seed, take the top K by (score desc, key asc), scores rounded to 6 decimals. Rows written as JSONL: line 1 `{"ppr_side":1,"gmap_digest":"<16 hex>","alpha":0.5,"epsilon":0.001,"k":<K>,"walk":"undirected","weights":"gmap edge weight, 1.0 when none"}`, then one `{"key":"...","candidates":[["key",score],...]}` per fact (a fact with no neighbour gets `[]`), BTreeMap-ordered JSON keys, tmp-then-rename (write_atomic).
4. bin: `--ppr-candidates <K>` (1..=200, clap range); the line `[engram-export] ppr side: <facts> facts, k=<K>, <pushes> pushes, <ms> ms -> <path>` after the meta line. It is never written implicitly, never read by any glia code, and its absence changes nothing in the gmap, diff or meta bytes.
5. Tests (tests/ppr_side_v6.rs, bin-driven): export a fixture with `--ppr-candidates 5` twice -> identical side bytes; header digest equals the meta's gmap_digest; every candidate key is a key of the gmap; a fact two Calls hops away ranks below a one-hop neighbour; without the flag no `.ppr.jsonl` exists and a stale one is removed.

MEASURED in the spec probe (the spec probe (scratch dir spec052/probe/DE, git-archive / git-clone copies only; nothing written under /home/ivy/Code); the 0.5.1 wheel in ~/.venvs/glia-leap; a harness mimicking repo-graph's _build_graph: generate(copy, incremental=True), save_to_default, swap, optional malloc_trim(0); git-archive copies of glia 84e2e71 and grpc-go 6f50403; VmRSS after each rebuild, MB): glia 15 rebuilds - glibc 406 -> 852 (+446), glibc + malloc_trim after the swap 207 -> 257 (+50), MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 338 -> 551 (+213), arena 2 + trim 204 -> 211 (+7, but 2.09 s / rebuild vs 1.44), mimalloc 2.2.3 (LD_PRELOAD) 404 -> 1051 (+647), mimalloc MIMALLOC_PURGE_DELAY=0 405 -> 999 (+594), jemalloc 5.3.0 (LD_PRELOAD) 384 -> 537 (+153), jemalloc dirty/muzzy_decay_ms 0 + background_thread 201 -> 219 (+18, 1.72 s / rebuild); glia 40 rebuilds - glibc 413 -> 1335 still climbing, trim after the swap 208 -> 271 (levels at 268-287 from rebuild 10), trim at the end of generate before the swap 207 -> 383 (creeping); GLIA_THREADS=1: glibc 300 -> 412 (levels by rebuild 5), + trim 181 -> 168. grpc-go 15: glibc 211 -> 487, trim 107 -> 158, jemalloc tuned 111 -> 121, mimalloc tuned 218 -> 420, trim before swap 109 -> 177. Mean seconds per rebuild (glia): glibc 1.44, trim 1.52, jemalloc tuned 1.72. So: the creep is freed graph memory held in rayon workers' glibc arenas (one thread: no creep), the measured fix is a trim right after the old graph is freed, and no allocator crate beats it (mimalloc is worse than glibc; jemalloc needs non-default tuning to match and is slower on glia). packets.title: PHP: a group `use` behind a leading backslash (`use \App\Models\{User, Order};`) parses: the file is parsed from a byte-for-byte copy whose one leading `\` of such a statement is a space, so the rest of the file is no longer swallowed by an ERROR node and the group's clauses bind
packets.area: DF PHP group use behind a leading backslash
packets.rationale: 0.5.1 plan 7.4 deferred `use \App\{X}` here. MEASURED at HEAD 84e2e71 (leap wheel, fixture php-group-use-leading-backslash): a file whose namespace statement is followed by `use \App\Models\{User, Order};` emits its MODULE src::Orders::Checkout and NOTHING else - no CLASS Checkout, no METHOD run, 0 IMPORTS, 0 CALLS - because tree-sitter-php 0.24 has no rule for a group behind a leading `\` and its error recovery wraps the following class declaration in the ERROR node. The same file with `use App\Models\{User, Order};` (probe php2) emits CLASS / METHOD, 2 IMPORTS and 2 CALLS. CB.7 already knew the grammar gap and made parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs use_clauses return nothing for a declaration with has_error() (the `leading_backslash_is_stripped` test accepts `group.is_empty()`), which stops a wrong import but not the loss of the rest of the file. `\App\X\{..}` is valid PHP (legacy_namespace_name accepts T_NAME_FULLY_QUALIFIED) and means exactly `App\X\{..}`: a `use` path is always absolute.
entry_points: parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs - parse_file - parse `mask_group_use_backslash(source)` when it returns Some (the tree only); every text read (`src`, CODE / POSITION cells, names) stays on the ORIGINAL source bytes

parsers/code/php/src/lib.rs - mod tests - leading_backslash_is_stripped tightened; new tests group_use_behind_backslash_keeps_the_file, mask_is_byte_preserving, mask_leaves_trait_and_closure_use_alone

packets.implementation:
1. `fn mask_group_use_backslash(source: &str) -> Option<String>`: scan line starts (after ASCII spaces / tabs) for the keyword `use` followed by whitespace, an optional `function` / `const` keyword and whitespace, then a `\\` that begins a name path (`[A-Za-z_\\][A-Za-z0-9_\\]*`) which reaches `\\{` before any `;` / `(` / newline-free `}`; for each such statement record the byte offset of that ONE leading backslash. None when there is none (the common case: no allocation). Otherwise copy the source and overwrite each recorded byte with b' ' (ASCII for ASCII: lengths, byte offsets, rows and columns are unchanged, so every tree position is valid against the original text). A trait `use T { .. }` inside a class (no `\\{`), a closure `use ($x)` (`(` first) and an already-unanchored `use App\\{` are left alone. Byte scanning only on ASCII anchors (CLAUDE.md UTF-8 rule).
2. parse_file: `let masked = mask_group_use_backslash(source); let tree = parser.parse(masked.as_deref().unwrap_or(source), None)`; `src` stays `source.as_bytes()`. Every node range is identical in both texts, so `text_of(node, src)` reads the original bytes (the masked declaration's namespace_name starts one byte after the original backslash, which use_clauses already strips). CODE / POSITION cells and CD.7c code spans keep slicing the file on disk byte for byte.
3. When masked: `eprintln!("[php-use] group use behind a leading backslash masked={n} file={file_rel_path}")` once per file.
4. TESTS (mod tests): leading_backslash_is_stripped's group arm now asserts `group == vec![sym("App::Billing", "Ledger", None)]` (was `is_empty() || ==`); group_use_behind_backslash_keeps_the_file parses the fixture's Checkout.php and asserts CLASS src::Orders::Checkout and METHOD ..::run exist, the two Symbol imports (App::Models User / Order) and the two `Attribute` calls; mask_is_byte_preserving asserts len equality and that only the recorded bytes differ (`use \\A\\{B};` -> `use  A\\{B};`), also for `use function \\A\\{f};`; mask_leaves_trait_and_closure_use_alone (`use T { a as b; }`, `function () use ($x) {}`, `use \\A\\B;` -> None).

AFTER: (1) `cargo test -p glia-parser-php` green; the four tests above fail on HEAD (no mask fn; the tightened assertion fails). (2) grade.py php-group-use-leading-backslash: nodes 2/2, edges 4/4 (verified at the wave close-out wheel; during the wave: `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 cargo run -q -p glia-cli -- analyze <copy> --format json` shows the CLASS, the 2 IMPORTS and the 2 CALLS). packets.implementation:
1. Parser (tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 node-types, checked: `parameter` has fields `external_name` (simple_identifier), `name` (the internal name, a simple_identifier) and `type`; `inout` / attributes are a `parameter_modifiers` child): `fn record_local_types(decl: TsNode, body: Option<TsNode>, scope: NodeId, src: &[u8], acc: &mut Acc)`. Parameters: each `parameter` of the declaration (tree-sitter-swift: `parameter` with optional `external_name`, `name`, `type`); the local is `name`; its type is `simple_type_name` of the type after peeling `optional_type` / implicitly-unwrapped `!`, `inout`, attributes; a generic / function / tuple type records `""`. Body locals: a pre-order walk of the body that does NOT descend into nested `function_declaration` / `lambda_literal` (their locals are not this scope's): each `property_declaration` binding one `pattern` name -> annotation (`type_annotation`) through simple_type_name, else its value through constructor_name (`T(..)`, `T.init(..)` -> T; anything else `""`). acc.nav.record_local_type keeps the first type and blanks a name bound to two types (existing CodeNav rule). Also the closure-capture shape `guard let x = y` records `""` for x (unknown).
2. Graph: SwiftModuleTypes::resolve(g, site) gains, AFTER the static / construction / implicit-self arms (so their bindings never change), the local-receiver lookup. NOTE (verifier): the HEAD Attribute arm is `let group = self.group(self.caller_dir(g, site.from)?, base)?;` - the `?` returns from resolve when `base` is a local name (no type of that name), so the new lookup cannot be a later match arm; restructure the Attribute arm as `match self.group(dir, base) { Some(group) => same_module_static as today, None => the local_receiver lookup below }` (a base that IS a type of the caller's dir keeps same_module_static, unchanged). The lookup: `if let CallQualifier::Attribute { base, name } = &site.qualifier && let Some(ty) = g.nav.local_types.get(&site.from).and_then(|l| l.get(base)).filter(|t| !t.is_empty()) { let dir = self.caller_dir(g, site.from)?; let group = self.group(dir, ty)?; let m = Self::member(g, group, name)?; self.local_receiver.set(+1); return Some((m, Evidence::emitter("graph:swift_scope").rule("local_receiver"))) }`. It is reached only after the generic pass found nothing (extra_hook contract), so a unique-name binding the generic receiver pass already made (A6.2a through resolve_type_name) is left as is; the hook adds the ambiguous-across-targets case and the optional-chain `o?.save()` shape. Never across modules: a type declared only in another target binds nothing (an `import`ed module's types stay unresolved, the CB.26 rule).
3. Marker: SwiftModuleTypes::marker appends ` local_receiver=<n>` to the existing `[swift-scope]` line (graph/src/build.rs prints it; the format string lives in swift_scope.rs).
4. TESTS. Parser (mod tests): param_and_local_types_are_recorded (the fixture's Service.swift: local_types[run][store]=Store, [local][s]=Store, [t]=Store, [u]=Store, [o]=Store, [freeRun][store]=Store); nested_closure_locals_are_not_recorded; tuple_pattern_is_unknown. swift_scope.rs mod tests: local_receiver_binds_in_own_module (two dirs both declaring Store: binds the caller dir's), local_of_unknown_type_binds_nothing, other_module_only_type_binds_nothing. engine/tests/swift_calls.rs: params_and_locals_bind_through_the_target (generate_one over the fixture shape; 4 CALLS with EVIDENCE rule local_receiver or receiver_type, none into Sources::Admin).

packets.implementation:
1. `fn unwrap_genex(arg: &str) -> Genex`: not starting `$<` -> Plain. Parse one balanced `$<...>` (depth-counted on ASCII `$<` / `>`; an unbalanced one -> Skip). Head before the first top-level `:`: `BUILD_INTERFACE` -> the tail; `INSTALL_INTERFACE` / `INSTALL_PREFIX` -> Skip; a head that is itself a nested condition (`$<CONFIG:Debug>`, `$<BOOL:..>`, `$<PLATFORM_ID:..>`, `$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>`, `$<NOT:..>`, `$<AND:..>`, `$<OR:..>`, a literal `0` / `1`): `0` -> Skip, otherwise the tail (a root that only exists under some configuration is still a place the build looks; roots only ever ADD candidates); any other head (`TARGET_PROPERTY`, `TARGET_FILE_DIR`, `JOIN`, ...) -> Skip. The tail is split on top-level `;` into dirs (a list), each recursively unwrapped (a nested BUILD_INTERFACE). Dirs(...) with every non-Skip piece; Skip when none is left.
2. cmake_dir(arg, list_dir, forms): `match unwrap_genex(arg) { Plain => today's body, Dirs(ds) => the first... ` - cmake_dir returns Option<String> for ONE dir today, so its caller (the loop over a call's arguments) is changed to iterate `cmake_dirs(arg, ..) -> Vec<String>`, which is today's cmake_dir for a Plain arg and the per-piece cmake_dir for Dirs; `contains("$<")` remains a refusal for any piece still holding one after unwrapping. The counter genex += each dir read through a generator expression.
3. Marker: IncludeRoots::marker appends ` genex=<n>` to the `[c-includes] search roots=...` line (one per repo, existing).
4. TESTS (c_includes.rs mod tests): build_interface_dir_is_a_root (`$<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/inc>` in `lib/CMakeLists.txt` -> `lib/inc`); install_interface_is_skipped; config_conditional_dir_is_a_root (`"$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/debug>"`); false_condition_is_skipped (`$<0:x>`); list_inside_genex (`$<BUILD_INTERFACE:a;b>` -> a, b); unknown_genex_is_skipped (`$<TARGET_PROPERTY:t,INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>`); IN-REPO TESTS THAT MOVE (verifier): cmake_target_include_directories already feeds `INTERFACE $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/gen>` with lib/gen/g.h walked, so its `got.dirs` assertion gains `lib/gen` (expected ["lib/include", "lib/api", "lib/gen", "common"], cmake 3 -> 4; re-measured on the landed code) while its cmake_include_args / `cmake_dir("$<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>", ..) == None` assertions stay; order_and_dedup's literal marker gains ` genex=0`.

packets.title: Python signals, the scanner: blinker named signals (`x = signal("order-placed")`, `Namespace().signal(..)`, `signal("x").send / .connect`) and Django signals (`x = Signal()` / `django.dispatch.Signal()`) are read as declarations, and `x.send(..)` / `x.send_robust(..)` / `x.connect(fn)` / `@x.connect` / `@receiver(x)` as emit / handle sites of a signal the caller binds; a literal blinker site mints its event per file
packets.rationale: Matrix cell python/eventbus is `none` at HEAD (notes/matrix.json: extract 2/6, MIN over matrix/python/eventbus (blinker), eventbus_django, eventbus_pyee; only pyee is full). parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs reads one Python bus, pyee (`from pyee` / `import pyee` gate, `@ee.on` / `ee.emit`), and has no row for blinker or Django (the CF.1 notes predicted it). MEASURED at HEAD 84e2e71 (leap wheel, grade.py on copies): matrix/python/eventbus nodes 0/2, edges 0/1; eventbus_django nodes 0/2, edges 0/1. The identity of a signal is not at its sites: blinker names it once at its declaration (`order_placed = signal("order-placed")` in signals.py) and the sites (`order_placed.send(..)`, `@order_placed.connect`) sit in another file that imports the variable; a Django Signal() has no name at all - the variable IS the identity. So a site can only be named with the declaration in hand: this packet gives the eventbus crate the two pure scanners (declarations; sites of a given set of bound names) and the one per-file shape that needs no binding (a literal `signal("x")` site); DF.13 joins them across files after the parse cache. 0.5.1 left the cell over the per-fix cap (report deferred_052: 'a cross-file signal-variable binding, 400-520 LOC').

packets.implementation:
1. Gates (lower-cased source, VerbCtx-style caching): blinker = a line starting `from blinker` / `import blinker`; django = `from django.dispatch` / `import django.dispatch` / `from django import dispatch`. Both scanners return nothing for a non-`.py` path, and every occurrence goes through the CJ.1a LazyGuard (a needle starting inside a Python string literal or comment is no site), so glia's own sources and test literals mint nothing.
2. python_signal_decls: line-anchored (column 0, a module-level assignment): `<ident> = <call>` where <call> is `signal(` / `blinker.signal(` / `<ident>.signal(` with a first literal argument (literal_after, single line) [blinker gate] -> PySignalDecl { name, identity: lit, kind Blinker }; or `Signal(` / `dispatch.Signal(` / `django.dispatch.Signal(` [django gate] -> PySignalDecl { name, identity: name, kind Django } (the caller qualifies the identity with the declaring module's dotted path, so two apps' `order_placed` signals stay two events). Class-attribute and function-local signals are not declarations (out of the item; counted as skipped in DF.13's marker).
3. python_signal_sites(source, path, bound) takes NO import gate (verifier: matrix/python/eventbus/orders.py and eventbus_django/receivers.py import neither blinker nor django.dispatch - only `from signals import order_placed`; the bound set from DF.13 IS the gate): byte search per bound name for the site shapes, each requiring an identifier boundary before the name (is_ident_byte) and, for `@receiver(`, a list or single argument whose element equals the name exactly (whitespace tolerated); returns (bound name, side, byte offset, 0-based line via line_of). Sorted by offset. Pure text, no tree-sitter (the eventbus crate's existing model).
4. Literal blinker sites (per file, cacheable): two new string-keyed rows on each side, gated on the blinker import: emitter `signal(` followed by literal then `).send(` / `).send_robust(`; handler `signal(` literal `).connect` - implemented as a small dedicated pass in emit_event_nodes for `.py` paths (the generic needle table cannot express `signal("x").send(`), adding to the same EventNodes with the same `seen` set.
5. python_signal_nodes: for each (side, identity, at) in offset order, push_event_node(.., if Emit {EVENT_EMITTER, "event_emit:"} else {EVENT_HANDLER, "event_handle:"}, Confidence::Medium, module_id, repo), anchors as the string-keyed needles anchor (the one site that minted the node, plus every later site of the same identity), mark_transport(.., "blinker" | "django").
6. TESTS: blinker_decls_read_the_literal (fixture matrix/python/eventbus signals.py -> [order_placed -> order-placed]); django_decls_read_the_variable (eventbus_django signals.py); decls_need_the_import (no blinker import -> none); sites_need_the_binding (orders.py with bound {order_placed} -> Emit at `order_placed.send(`, Handle at `@order_placed.connect`; with bound {} -> none; `my_order_placed.send(` never matches order_placed); receiver_list_form (`@receiver([a, order_placed])`); literal_blinker_site_mints_per_file (`signal("x").send()` -> event_emit:x); rust_and_python_literals_mint_nothing (the needles inside a Python string / comment, CJ.1a); no_event_emit_send (the matrix fixture's forbid: no `event_emit:send` from any of these).
7. Marker: emit_event_nodes prints `[event-py-literal] blinker literal sites=<n> file=<path>` for a .py file where the literal pass minted >= 1 node (the CJ.1a `[code-guard]` precedent of a per-file line).

packets.title: Python signals, the binding: a post-cache graft builds the repo's signal table (declaring module, variable -> identity), finds each Python file's bound signal names (declared in the file, `from <mod> import <name> [as a]`, `import <mod>` + `<mod>.<name>`), and swaps the file's event nodes for ones that include its signal sites, so blinker and Django signals pair as EVENT_FLOWS across files
packets.rationale: A signal's identity is declared in one file and used in another (matrix/python/eventbus: signals.py declares, orders.py `from signals import order_placed` and sends / connects; eventbus_django: receivers.py the same), and the per-file extractors (cached) cannot see another file. The engine already runs exactly this kind of post-cache, text-only, whole-repo fold for events (CB.3b apply_event_const_names in engine/src/build/grafts.rs: re-run the event scan with a resolver, swap the file's event nodes through eventbus::replace_event_nodes). packets.implementation:
1. Order inside apply_post_cache: after apply_event_const_names (CB.3b), before the wrappers' queue half and the owner pass - so the swapped nodes are owner-qualified and IMPORTS-filtered like every event node (the same seam CB.3b documents).
2. Module resolution: the declaring module of a decl is the file's MODULE qname (ModuleQnames::plan, the same plan every graft uses); an import's target qname: `module.replace('.', "::")` for level 0, else the importer's qname with `level` trailing segments dropped then the module appended (Python relative import semantics: level 1 = the importer's package); `from pkg import signals` naming a MODULE `pkg::signals` binds `signals.<name>` (Module-form sites `signals.order_placed.send(`).
3. Django identity = the declaring module's dotted path (`::` -> `.`) + `.` + name (`signals.order_placed`, `myapp.signals.order_placed`); blinker identity = its literal. A name declared twice in one module with different identities -> dropped (counted).
4. Per file with sites: `let mut fold = eventbus::extract_event_nodes_with_consts(source, path, module_id, repo, &resolve)` with the per-file resolver apply_event_const_names builds (factored into one private helper both grafts call, so the two cannot drift) (exactly CB.3b's call, so the file's pyee / literal / constant-keyed nodes are re-emitted identically) then append `eventbus::python_signal_nodes(..)` to fold.emitters / fold.handlers (nodes, nav, anchors merged; a name already in the fold keeps one node) and `eventbus::replace_event_nodes(fp, module_id, "python", fold)`. Panics: the per-file call is wrapped in catch_unwind with parse_errors `<path>: PANIC (python signals)`, as CB.3b does.
5. Determinism: decls collected into a BTreeMap in walk order; files processed in walk order; the swap is per parse (parses_by_lang is a HashMap: nothing may depend on its iteration order - the per-language Vec is walked in its own order).
6. Normal form: a template text where each (a) is `${path}`, each (e) is `${path.replace('a', 'b')}` (single quotes, escapes kept), literals inline. Anything else -> not a config expression (no guess, no value data-flow: only declarations of constants / readonly members / one-return getters are read, as CH.3a).
2. TS parser classify_template: for each `template_substitution` child whose expression is `this.<m>` and indirect reads are allowed (depth one, CH.3a's rule f) -> `class_member_value(member, src)` -> config_expr_text -> Some(t): push `t` into `source` (the template text) and keep `${…}` in `out` (the path stays template-shaped until the fold); record alias. Alternatives (per-deployment values, A11.4) apply the same transform to each alternative.

DESIGN: a value typed Sub finds `m` on Sub's prototype chain, so the member a typed-receiver call names is the nearest class at or above Sub that defines `m` - CH.1b's lookup (nearest_definer, the runtime's own) started at the receiver's declared class instead of the caller's. That member is the one the call binds; a subclass of Sub that overrides it is reached by dispatch, which is DF.22c's method-level IMPLEMENTS hop, never a second call edge (A6.6's rule, resolve_via_receiver_type doc: "the implementation is one method-level IMPLEMENTS hop further, never guessed here"). Alternatives weighed: (a) bind inside resolve_calls: INHERITS_FROM is drawn by resolve_refs, which runs after it (build_ts_like). (b) Let type_method walk superclasses in every builder: moves Java / C# / Kotlin / Python receiver binds unmeasured (their builders also run resolve_calls before resolve_refs); the TS-family post-refs pass keeps the item's scope, as CH.1b did, and the walk is language-free should another builder adopt it with its own measurement. (c) Re-run resolve_calls after resolve_refs: binds every site twice and doubles every tally. 1. receiver_class(g, site, gate) -> Option<(NodeId, bool)>: from_module = enclosing_home_module(g, site.from)?; if let Some(ty) = constructed_type(site) { return constructed_type_id(g, from_module, ty).filter(is CLASS).map(|t| (t, true)); } type_name = receiver_type(g, site)?; type_id = resolve_type_name(g, from_module, type_name)?; if let CallQualifier::Attribute { base, .. } = &site.qualifier && local_type(g, site.from, base).is_none() && !gate.admits(g, site.from) { return None; } (A6.2a's gate: in TS / JS a bare name outside the constructor is a parameter, local or global, never the field); kind CLASS -> Some((type_id, false)). The gate is a fresh BareFieldGate owned by resolve_inherited_calls; its skipped tally is dropped (resolve_calls already printed this build's `[recv] bare field receivers skipped` line, which counts own-method binds the gate stopped). The receiver typing helpers are the ones resolve_via_receiver_type uses, called, not copied (DF.17 changes only what that function does after type_method misses on the own class). 2. resolve_inherited_calls, the qualifier match gains: `CallQualifier::Attribute { name, .. } | CallQualifier::ComplexReceiver { name, .. }` -> an empty name, no receiver_class, or g.symbols.class_methods[class] containing `name` (an own method that did not bind is no inherited call) -> kept; else match nearest_definer(g, &supers, class, name): One(to) -> push_edge(g, site.from, to, edge_category::CALLS, graph_evidence("graph:calls", "inherited_receiver").line(site.line)); stats.receiver_bound += 1; when not constructed, recv_stats::record() (the A6.2a per-language `[recv] receiver-typed calls bound` count, as resolve_via_receiver_type does; a constructed bind stays out of it, as CL.5a's do); Ambiguous -> stats.ambiguous += 1, kept; Nothing -> kept. Kept sites stay in their original order (byte_identical). 3. InheritStats gains receiver_bound; the marker becomes `[ts-inherit] calls bound through superclasses: (self= super=

receiver= ambiguous=) abstract implements=`, printed when any count > 0. The struct doc says CL.5a's `[recv] constructed receivers: bound=B unbound=U` still counts what resolve_calls bound, so a constructed receiver bound here counts unbound there and receiver= here. 4. Scope: only build_typescript_family reaches resolve_inherited_calls (build_ts_like's inherit flag); build_typescript (Dart / Solidity / Terraform through lang_build's `_` arm) and every other builder are unchanged. No new Branch: like CH.1b's binds, these edges are pushed by the pass with graph_evidence, outside resolve_calls' EvidenceTally (the `[evidence-graph]` line is unchanged). 5. TESTS graph/src/calls.rs mod tests (Shape / heritage_ref helpers, through build_typescript_family): (a) receiver_call_binds_through_superclasses - module src::h: CLASS A { load }, CLASS B { find } with heritage_ref(B -> A, INHERITS_FROM), CLASS C { go } with s.nav.record_field_type(C, "b", "B"), FUNCTION f with s.nav.record_local_type(f, "p", "B"); CallSites: go ComplexReceiver{receiver: "this.b", name: "load"} line 4, go ComplexReceiver{"this.b", "find"} line 5, go ComplexReceiver{"this.b", "nope"} line 6, f Attribute{base: "p", name: "load"} line 8, f ComplexReceiver{receiver: "new B()", name: "load"} line 9, f Attribute{base: "q", name: "load"} line 10 -> CALLS go -> A::load (graph:calls / inherited_receiver, line 4), go -> B::find (receiver_type, line 5), f -> A::load (inherited_receiver, lines 8 and 9); g.unresolved_calls == [nope@6, q@10] in that order; a second shape with CLASS K extending two classes P and Q that both define m and a field `k: K` -> `this.k.m()` stays unresolved, ambiguous=1; marker `[ts-inherit] calls bound through superclasses: 3 (self=0 super=0 receiver=3 ambiguous=0) abstract implements=0`. packets.risks: Liveness generosity: IMPLEMENTS is a forward carry edge, so a reached override makes the member it overrides live and, through A7.8's implementer step, every sibling override - as an interface (A6.6) or abstract (CH.1b) pair already does; a base member live only through a live override's `super.m()` does the same (A7.8's step is node-level); dead_symbol's own claim is made exact (super_method), liveness stays conservative as documented. Pairing is by name, as CH.1b's: a static member and a same-named instance member would pair (the parser records no static-ness; 0 of the 11 measured concrete pairs mix them); getter / setter pairs share one METHOD node (one qname). An overridden concrete member is never a dead_symbol row (its incoming IMPLEMENTS is a carry edge), the same as an abstract member since CH.1b: an overridden default whose body never runs is not reported (shell's System::run). Two definers at one level pair nothing (nearest_definer Ambiguous). The dispatch rule is node-level, as CH.1c's: a call on an exactly typed receiver (`new T().m()`, a local initialised by `new T()`) vouches for T's overrides although none can run there (mem0: openai-llm.test.ts's `new OpenAILLM(..)` local vouches for the DeepSeekLLM / LMStudioLLM overrides, moot there since their own tests call them); telling exact-type receivers apart would need their own EVIDENCE rule and is not taken. The rule string super_method is written in graph and read in engine: dead_dispatch's (g) test fails if either side drifts. Determinism: pairs sorted by (from, to) with the rule riding along, deduped, existing edges filtered; gaps' calls_into is looked up, never iterated into output, so rows keep view.nodes order. Cost: Evidence::of runs only for edges into METHODs that are an IMPLEMENTS target. 1. ROWS, as listed in entry_points. Gates are the crates' Rust path spellings, lowercase (rows read the lowercased file): `lapin`, `azservicebus`, `async_nats`, `google_cloud_pubsub`, `aws_sdk_sqs`, `aws_sdk_sns`, `apalis`. Every new row sits above the A2.9 block, so the Redis / MQTT generic `.publish(` / `.subscribe(` rows yield to a site one of these already claimed; is_generic_verb_row stays keyed to RedisPubSub / Mqtt, so the NATS `.publish(` / `.subscribe(` rows read their arg #0 normally (receiver-agnostic, the CL.3 NATS.Net `.PublishAsync` precedent). The new gates join broker_signals() automatically (derived from the rows), so eventbus.rs suppresses its `publish(` / `.subscribe(` twins in those files (the google-cloud-pubsub fixture's `publisher.publish(Default::default())`).
1b. lapin consume reuses the pika `basic_consume(` row (gate gains "lapin"), so it also inherits that needle's HANDLER_RULES entry KeyedOrArg(["on_message_callback"], 1): lapin's arg #1 is the consumer TAG, a quoted literal, which handler_expr reads as no handler (reference() accepts only a name / member) - so the lapin consumer carries no HANDLED_BY ref and no `[queue-callbacks]` line; the rust_lapin_rows test pins it (fp.refs holds no HANDLED_BY from the consumer).
2. lapin publish is ArgIndexOr(1, 0): the routing key names the queue on the default / direct exchange; a fanout publish passes an empty key and the exchange is the identity (CL.1's amqplib rule). A one-line `channel.basic_publish("", "orders", ..)` also hits the ungated HEAD `channel.basic_publish` ArgLiteral row, which reads the empty arg #0 and records a deferred tag; CL.1 rule (i) drops that tag beside the named node (unit test pins exactly one producer node).
3. aws-sdk: Chain keys `queue_url` / `topic_arn` - keyed_literal already reads a builder METHOD key (`.queue_url("..")`: a `.` before, `(` after) and folds the URL / ARN to `orders` (queue_topic::fold_topic). chain_region stops at the depth-0 `;`, so `.send().await` after it is inside the chain and harmless.
4. TopicRule::StorageJobType (`.push(`, apalis). R = the identifier before the needle (receiver_before). R must be DECLARED in the file: a fn parameter `R: <ty>` or a `let [mut] R[: <ty>] = <init>`. Accepted only when <ty> or the initializer's path names a segment ending in `Storage` (`&mut apalis_redis::RedisStorage<Job>`, `MemoryStorage::new()`, `PostgresStorage::new(pool)`). Identity: the generic argument of that `...Storage<T>` (last path segment of T, `&` / `&mut` stripped); else the type path leading positional argument #0 (`T { .. }`, `T(..)`, `path::T { .. }`, `T::new(..)` / `T::default()`), uppercase-initial. A receiver that is not a storage, or no readable type, is NO SITE and records no tag (the NoIdentity rule's effect): `reports.push(Report { .. })` beside a real storage mints nothing.
5. TopicRule::WorkerJobType (`.build_fn(` / `.build(`, apalis). The needle's statement (back to the previous depth-0 `;` / `{` / `}`) must contain `WorkerBuilder` before the needle, else no site (`.build(` is every builder's). Handler H = positional arg #0, an identifier path; `fn H(<pat>: <T>, ..)` (async or not) declared in the file gives T (last segment). Else the statement's `.backend(<S>)` argument S, declared in the file as a `...Storage<T>`, gives T. Else no site. HANDLER_RULES makes H the consumer's callback, so `queue_consumer:WelcomeEmail -HANDLED_BY-> send_welcome` binds through LA.33's bind_consumer_callbacks.
6. NO SITE vs NO TOPIC: for StorageJobType / WorkerJobType a disqualified occurrence (receiver not a storage, no WorkerBuilder in the statement, no readable type) is filtered in scan_guarded before it becomes a TopicHit - the same place bare_word_ok drops an occurrence - so CL.1 records no deferred `unresolved:apalis` tag for it. Both identity rules return TopicForm::Literal and no expr (a symbol is never a URL and never const-folds). The CJ.1a guard already drops a needle whose first byte sits in a Rust string or comment (scan_guarded), so glia's own new test literals mint nothing when glia indexes itself; the declaration lookups read the raw file, which is safe because they only qualify an already-admitted site.
7. MARKER: no new line - the existing GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG=1 `[queues] needle '<needle>' framework=<F> gate=ok topic=<t> file=<path>` line fires per new row, and `[queue-callbacks] consumers=.. bound=..` per file for apalis.
Alternatives weighed: an apalis row keyed on `WorkerBuilder::new("name")` - rejected, the worker name is not the job and never pairs with the push side; a receiver-name heuristic (`storage.push`) - rejected, the README names it `storage` but real code names it anything.

An exchange-only writer (`.withExchange("logs")`, fanout) mints nothing - recorded in the row comment.

1. PER-FILE (cron.rs extract_akka_quartz, gated on extension + `QuartzSchedulerExtension`). Receivers R = the literal `QuartzSchedulerExtension(<x>)` and every identifier bound to it in the file (`val scheduler = QuartzSchedulerExtension(system)`). (a) `R.createSchedule(` : name = arg #0 literal, expression = arg #2 literal or the named `cronExpression = ".."` -> normalise_schedule -> CronJob { schedule, target: name, source: "akka_quartz", handler: None } (the job's receiver is an ActorRef, never a code symbol). (b) `R.schedule(` / `R.scheduleJob(` / `R.rescheduleJob(` : name = arg #0 literal; when (a) created that name in this file the call adds nothing; else CronJob { schedule: format!("{AKKA_QUARTZ_REF}{name}"), target: name, source: "akka_quartz" } - a REF the per-file pass cannot name, qname `cron:@quartz-conf:<name>:<name>`. `.schedule(` on any other receiver is ignored.
2. HOCON (cron.rs hocon_quartz_schedules).
