packets.area: DT T10 contracts: TypeScript hardhat / TypeChain / artifact readers (evm/ts.rs)
packets.rationale: Kina's largest in-repo caller set is hardhat. contracts/test/EscrowManager.test.js does `const EscrowManager = await ethers.getContractFactory("EscrowManager"); escrow = await EscrowManager.deploy(..)` after a `let escrow;` at describe level, and `token = await MockToken.deploy(..)` from `getContractFactory("MockERC20")`. It then calls 22 distinct EscrowManager functions through `escrow.connect(seller).fn(..)` chains (the verifier checked every call's argument count against EscrowManager.sol: 0 mismatches), plus `token.mint` / `approve` / `balanceOf`. The scripts deploy-mock.js / deploy-usdt-local.js call `token.mint` / `usdt.mint`. provision_demo_wallets.js calls `hre.ethers.getContractAt([...inline 3-entry ABI...], deploy.stablecoin, deployer)`. At HEAD none of these mint anything, and DT.10c / DT.10i alone still do not, because no `new Contract` is involved. The contract name read at the site (factory, TypeChain type, artifact path) is the strongest identity, so the rule is `contract` (DERIVED). The viem / wagmi / web3.js readers in the first DT.10d moved to DT.10j (see notes).

packets.implementation:
1. Every new binding feeds the DT.10c / DT.10i site reader: hardhat and TypeChain bindings are ethers Contract instances, so member calls, element access, `.connect(..)` chains and ETHERS_MEMBERS (waitForDeployment, getAddress, deploymentTransaction among them) apply.
2. A Scope::Contract binding has no ABI entries, so every non-stop-listed member mints. The resolver pairs it by contract name and counts a member the contract does not declare as `not_declared`; Kina's hardhat `token.approve` / `token.balanceOf` on MockERC20 inherit from OpenZeppelin.
3. NOT read (DT.10h caveat): chai `await expect(tx).to.emit(escrow, 'Released')` (an assertion, not a subscription); `hre.artifacts.readArtifact('C')`; TypeChain type annotations alone (`const e: Escrow = ..`).
4. hardhat test sites sit in mocha arrow / function-expression callbacks, which carry no FUNCTION node, so the A5.8 pass ties them to the test MODULE (CONTAINS).

packets.title: TypeScript viem / wagmi / web3.js clients and the remaining ABI forms: viem / wagmi option-object calls (`readContract` / `writeContract` / `simulateContract` / `useReadContract` .. with `functionName`, `watchContractEvent` / `getContractEvents` / `parseEventLogs` with `eventName`, `multicall` contracts), `getContract(..).read.fn` instances and hardhat-viem, web3.js `new web3.eth.Contract(abi, addr).methods.fn` / `.events.E` / `getPastEvents`; TS object-literal ABIs, `parseAbi([...])` and `as const`
packets.area: DT T10 contracts: TypeScript viem / wagmi / web3.js readers + object-literal ABIs (evm/ts.rs, evm/abi.rs)
packets.rationale: The T10 scope names 'viem readContract / writeContract with functionName'. viem / wagmi carry `abi:` plus `functionName:` in an options object instead of a member call, and their ABIs are usually `parseAbi([...])` or a `const x = [...] as const` object literal with bare keys. web3.js puts the ABI first (`new web3.eth.Contract(abi, addr)`) and calls through `.methods.fn(..)`. None of the three test beds uses viem, wagmi, web3.js or TypeChain (the verifier grepped all three), so this packet is measured on its fixture with Kina / examples-glia / quokka as unchanged controls. Split from the first DT.10d (see notes).
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/evm/ts.rs - the gate extends to `viem` (and `viem/..`), `wagmi`, `@wagmi/` and `web3` import paths

parsers/code/extractors/src/evm/ts.rs - (new) fn viem_sites over the call names:
- READ_WRITE: readContract, writeContract, writeContractAsync, simulateContract, estimateContractGas, prepareWriteContract, useReadContract, useWriteContract, useSimulateContract, useContractRead, useContractWrite, useEstimateContractGas
- EVENTS: watchContractEvent, getContractEvents, createContractEventFilter, useWatchContractEvent, parseEventLogs
Each is called bare `f({..})`, as `f(client, {..})` or as `client.f({..})`. The object argument's depth-1 keys are read:
- `abi`: an identifier, an inline literal or the shorthand `abi`
- `functionName` / `eventName`: a string literal, or an array of them for parseEventLogs
- `args`: an array literal -> its element count
- `address`: an identifier, used for the hint when the abi is unbound
`multicall({ contracts: [..] })` and `useReadContracts({ contracts: [..] })` read each element. lib `viem`.

parsers/code/extractors/src/evm/ts.rs - (new) viem instances:
- `<x> = getContract({ address, abi, client })`, `<x> = (await )?hre.viem.deployContract("<C>")` and `hre.viem.getContractAt("<C>", ..)` (the last two -> Scope::Contract(C)) bind x
- call sites `x.read.<m>(`, `x.write.<m>(`, `x.simulate.<m>(`, `x.estimateGas.<m>(`, with args = the first argument's array length
- event sites `x.watchEvent.<E>(`, `x.getEvents.<E>(`, `x.createEventFilter.<E>(`

parsers/code/extractors/src/evm/ts.rs - (new) fn web3_bindings: `new <w>.eth.Contract(<abi>(, <addr>)?)` binds x; the ABI is the FIRST argument. Sites `x.methods.<m>(` and `x.methods['<m>'](`; events `x.events.<E>(`, `x.getPastEvents('<E>'`, `x.once('<E>'`. lib `web3`.

parsers/code/extractors/src/evm/abi.rs - read_abi reads three more forms:
- a TS object-literal array (bare or quoted keys, single or double quotes, trailing commas), normalised to JSON and handed to read_json_abi
- `parseAbi([...])` / `parseAbiItem(..)` read through to the array inside
- a trailing `as const` / `satisfies Abi` skipped
packets.implementation:
1. The ABI from `abi:` resolves like DT.10c's abi argument: a same-file binding with entries, an imported identifier without entries (DT.10g joins it), or an inline literal. A shorthand `abi` bound to nothing in the file falls back to the hint from the `address` identifier: `ESCROW_ADDRESS` -> Scope::Abi(ESCROW_ADDRESS), name_key escrow.
2. A site whose `functionName` / `eventName` is not a literal (a variable) is counted `dynamic`.
3. The viem instance members `read` / `write` / `simulate` / `estimateGas` / `watchEvent` / `getEvents` / `createEventFilter` / `address` / `abi` are never members themselves.
4. web3.js: `x.methods.release(id).send({ from })` -> member release, args 1; `.call()` / `.send()` / `.estimateGas()` after `methods.m(..)` are not members.
5. The marker's viem= / web3= counts (already in DT.10c's line) now move.
6. TESTS.

packets.rationale:
examples-glia-expected row: 'Contract | Settler.Release: s.escrow.Transact(opts, "release", ..) | Escrow.release'. api/internal/chain/escrow.go holds `escrow *bind.BoundContract`, handed in through `Dial(.., contract *bind.BoundContract)` and `&Settler{client: client, escrow: contract, address: address}`. The api project holds no ABI, only a receiver named like the contract, so this pair is HEURISTIC (name_hint). Kina's backend/internal/signer/signer.go parses a raw-string JSON const (escrowManagerABI, 8 functions; the verifier parsed it) but packs a non-literal name, `parsedABI.Pack(method, args...)` (signer.go:201). That is counted dynamic here, and DT.10f reads it through the wrappers.

1. PRECISION: only a direct hand-over of a parameter makes a wrapper, either into a geth name position or into another inferred wrapper. No value is tracked through assignments (the CA.4 rule).

- a wrapper whose scope is Scope::Recv keeps it, so the resolver's name_hint applies to its sites (HEURISTIC)
- a call of a wrapper whose argument at the index is a parameter of the caller is a FORWARD: it may make the caller a wrapper, and is never counted dynamic
- a call whose argument at the index is anything else non-literal (a local, a concatenation, a call) is no site and is counted `dynamic`

packets.area: DT T10 contracts: cross-file ABI join (post-cache graft engine/src/build/evm_abi.rs)
packets.rationale:
DT.10c-k read an ABI only when its declaration sits in the calling file. Common layouts put it elsewhere: a TS `abi.ts` exporting `ESCROW_ABI` that every service imports, or a Go `abi.go` holding the package const that `client.go` parses (`abi.JSON(strings.NewReader(escrowABI))`, legal across the files of one package). Without the join such a client carries Scope::Abi(<name>) with no entries. It pairs only by name_hint (HEURISTIC) when the binding is named like the contract, and not at all otherwise (`SHOP_ABI` for contract Escrow). Kina and examples-glia keep their ABIs in the calling file, so this packet is measured on its fixture, with both test beds as controls.
The join must be post-cache and repo-level: an extractor sees one file, and merge_nav drops an extractor's own nav facts (the engine/src/extract.rs CB.24 ClientHost note). The TS declaration is therefore recorded on fp.nav, as ClientHost is, and spread by a graft, as stamp_client_hosts does.
For Go, the verifier found the facts already exist. The Go parser's FileConsts::scan (DF.7, parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs) records EVERY package-level string const of every Go file as `NavFact::GoStringConst { name, value }`: a raw string's text verbatim, an interpreted string's text with its escapes kept. That includes Kina's escrowABI / escrowManagerABI JSON. The Go half reads those facts, with no new Go-side declaration.

packets.implementation:
1. INDEX (pass one, over every parse of the repo, order-independent):
- TS: each MODULE's EvmAbi facts, keyed (declaring file, name);
- Go: each `.go` parse's ABI-shaped GoStringConsts, keyed (declaring file, name). A `_test.go` file's consts serve only `_test.go` callers.
A key declared twice is dropped. BTreeMap only.
2. JOIN (pass two): for each RPC_CALL / EVENT_HANDLER with an evm_call: / evm_event: qname, and each of its evm ENDPOINT_HIT cells that has abi_ref and no abi.
- TS (`from` starts with `./` or `../`): resolve against the calling file's directory, normalising `..`, then try in order the path as written, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `/index.ts`, `/index.js`. The first candidate whose (path, name) is indexed wins. A bare package or tsconfig-alias specifier stays unjoined (counted `unresolved`; TsAliasSet maps specifiers inside the TS graph build, not in this graft).
- Go (`from == "."`): every `.go` file of the calling file's directory. Exactly one (file, name) -> join; two or more -> `ambiguous`; none -> `unresolved`.
A join rewrites the cell in place: `abi` = the entries, `abi_from` = the declaring file. The node, its qname and its edges are unchanged. The resolver then identifies by ABI and drops the members the joined ABI does not list (DT.10b's not_in_abi). A cell's result depends only on the index, so the HashMap iteration over parses_by_lang reaches no output.
3. MARKER: `[evm-abi-join] joined=<j> unresolved=<u> ambiguous=<a> declarations=<d> repo=<label>` when d + j + u + a > 0. j / u / a count cells, d the indexed declarations.
4. CACHE / WATCH: the facts are cached with the parse and the graft runs post-cache on every build, so an ABI edit in abi.ts re-joins a cache-served pay.ts. watch re-runs post-cache grafts (the DC.7b note), and the post-graft fingerprint covers the rewritten cell.
5. TESTS.

packets.title: Contract-model wire vocabulary: code-domain/src/wire.rs (model SCHEMA_FIELDS, wire Shape, server MESSAGE_TYPE payload; sorted-key writers + readers; JSON kinds) and NavFact::SliceResult
packets.rationale: T1 needs one JSON vocabulary that the TS, Go, Dart and GraphQL extractors, the Go build and the consumers (the models pass, contract_fields) all agree on. Defining it once lets the TS-shape packet (DT.1d) and the Go-wire packet (DT.1e) run in parallel. Writers emit SORTED keys at every level. The endpoint fold re-serialises ENDPOINT_HIT payloads through `Fields` (engine/src/endpoint_fold.rs:1416, verified: the top-level order is kept, nested objects become serde_json::Value, and the workspace builds without preserve_order, so nested keys come back sorted). A sorted writer is therefore byte-stable through that round trip. Go slice results ([]models.Order) are deliberately absent from CodeNav::return_types (go_type_ref returns None for slices, parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1828), so the Go wire resolution needs its own fact.
entry_points: code-domain/src/wire.rs (new) - ModelField / ModelSchema { format, fields, extends, open }: to_payload(), parse(&str), cell() (SCHEMA_FIELDS)

code-domain/src/wire.rs - enum Shape { Named{ty,array,model}, Call{chain,array,model}, Chain{chain,array,model}, Object{fields: Vec<ShapeField>, open}, Union(Vec<Shape>), Open{raw} }, ShapeField { name, field, required, bind_required, shape }: to_json(), from_value(&serde_json::Value)
code-domain/src/wire.rs - ServerWire { ty, raw, form, line, status: Option<u16>, document: Option<String>, shape }: to_payload(), parse(), cell() (MESSAGE_TYPE)
code-domain/src/wire.rs - append_hit_fields(payload, response: Option<&Shape>, request: Option<&Shape>) -> String; hit_shapes(payload) -> (Option<Shape>, Option<Shape>)
code-domain/src/wire.rs - JsonKind + json_kind(format, ty); element_type(ty) -> (base, array)
code-domain/src/lib.rs - `pub mod wire;` beside `pub mod same_as;` (line 56); NavFact::SliceResult { elem: String } appended LAST, after GoPackageName (DF.15)
packets.implementation: 1. Model SCHEMA_FIELDS goes on an INTERFACE / CLASS / STRUCT / graphql MESSAGE_TYPE: {"extends":[..]?,"fields":[F..],"format":"ts|go|dart|graphql","open":true?}. F = {"array":true?,"bind":"required"?,"field":"<source member, only when != name>"?,"model":"<qname, written by a builder>"?,"name":"<json name>","required":bool,"type":"<type text>"}. Optional keys appear only when set. contract_fields' Field::parse (name/type/required) stays compatible. 2. Shape forms: Named {"array"?,"model"?,"type":"Order"}; Call {"array"?,"call":"self.store.Orders()","model"?}; Chain {"array"?,"chain":"self.cfg.X","model"?}; Object {"fields":[SF..],"open":true?}; Union {"union":[S..]}; Open {"open":true,"raw":"<=120 chars"}. SF = {"bind":"required"?,"field":"<schema field when name is an alias (GraphQL)>"?,"name":"<response key>","required":bool,"shape":S}. 3. ServerWire is a MESSAGE_TYPE cell and keeps A12.1's leading keys: {"type":"<simple name or empty>","raw":"<arg text <=120>","form":"json_response|json_bind|graphql_returns|graphql_selection|graphql_result","window":"site","line":<1-based>,"status":<int>?,"document":"<ident>"?,"shape":S}. Only this writer ever writes one, so its order is fixed by hand. `status` present means a known code: explicit, or the implicit 200 of forms with no status argument. `status` absent means unknown (a variable or a call), and such a site is never judged (DT.1g). 4. append_hit_fields splices `,"response":S` and then `,"request":S` before the payload's last `}`. The old bytes stay a prefix, and a hit with no shape is unchanged. 5. json_kind by format. ts: string, string-literal unions and templates -> String; number|bigint -> Number; boolean -> Boolean; X[] / Array<X> / ReadonlyArray<X> -> Array; inline object -> Object; any|unknown|object|Date -> Any; null|undefined -> Null; other identifiers -> Unknown(name), where the pass decides (a model is Object, anything else is never judged). go: string|time.Time|uuid.UUID|[]byte -> String; int*/uint*/float*/json.Number -> Number; bool -> Boolean; []T/[N]T -> Array; map -> Object; any|interface{}|json.RawMessage -> Any; *T -> T; any other named or external type -> Unknown. dart: String -> String; int|double|num -> Number; bool -> Boolean; List/Iterable -> Array; Map -> Object; dynamic|Object|DateTime -> Any; T? -> T. graphql: ID|String -> String; Int|Float -> Number; Boolean -> Boolean; [X] -> Array; X! -> X. 6. element_type repeatedly strips `*`, `?`, `!`, `| null` and `| undefined`, plus one array layer ([]X, X[], Array<X>, ReadonlyArray<X>, List<X>, [X]). Qualifiers are kept (models.Order). 7. NavFact::SliceResult { elem }: a Go callable whose first result is []T / []*T / [N]T with T named (go_type_ref text). DT.1f reads it. 8. Strings are escaped through serde_json::to_string. 9. Tests (wire mod): a round trip per payload; for every writer output, `serde_json::to_string(&serde_json::from_str::<Value>(p)) == p` (the sorted-key property); escapes; the append_hit_fields prefix property; json_kind per format; element_type cases ([]*models.Order, Order[], Array<Order>, List<Member>?, [Item!]!, Ticket | null); a ShapeField with `field` (alias) round trip.

packets.rationale: Measured on a Kina 8ac238c copy: 81 frontend files hold 82 import statements of `../models`, `../../core/models` or `../../../core/models` (core/models/index.ts, where every model interface lives, e.g. `frontend::src::app::core::models::index::Offer` at index.ts:81), and 0 IMPORTS edges reach frontend::src::app::core::models::index. resolve_ts_source maps `../models` to `...::core::models`, which is no MODULE, so ts_target (graph/src/imports.rs:1000) returns None at SameStem's NotAStem. Without the binding, `Offer` in offer.service.ts resolves to nothing, and T1's client-model resolution (DT.1g reads module_import_bindings) sees no Kina model. tsc / Node directory resolution (dir.ts first, then dir/index.ts) is a FACT. The TsAliases doc in engine/src/build/lang_build.rs:736 records the gap (`an alias naming a directory gets no implicit index.ts (the relative resolver has none either)`) and becomes false here.
entry_points: graph/src/imports.rs - ts_target - when module_by_qname misses, SameStem::pick returns NotAStem and explicit_ext is None: look up `<target_qname>::index` (module_by_qname, then the same SameStem pick for an index.ts + index.js pair) -> Some((id, "dir_index"))
graph/src/imports.rs - resolve_imports_ts - tally relative (specifier starts with `.`) vs alias dir-index binds; marker after the loop
engine/src/build/lang_build.rs - TsAliases doc comment (line ~736): the `no implicit index.ts` limitation sentence replaced by the dir_index rule
packets.implementation: 1. ts_target tries, in order: module_by_qname[q] (a file, tsc's first choice), the SameStem pick of q, and then, only when explicit_ext is None, module_by_qname[q::index] and the SameStem pick of q::index. explicit_ext None is required because an extension names a file, and Dart's `.dart`, Solidity's `.sol` and Terraform module dirs never reach the new arm. Both ImportTarget::Module and ::Symbol go through ts_target. So named bindings (`import { Account } from '../models'` -> module_symbols[index][Account]) and namespace aliases follow, and CALLS / INJECTS / heritage refs bound through module_import_bindings follow with no further change. 2. Evidence rule is `dir_index` (graph:imports, site line). 3. Re-export barrels (`export * from './x'`) are NOT followed: they emit no ImportStmt at HEAD (quokka's core/index.ts `export * from './chat'` etc. makes no IMPORTS edge, measured), and index.ts must declare the name itself (Kina's does). 4. The lang_build.rs doc sentence is updated in the same commit. 5. Tests (imports mod tests): dir_import_binds_index; file_beats_directory (format.ts + format/index.ts); alias_target_dir_binds_index (tsconfig paths target `src/app/core` -> `src::app::core::index`); explicit_extension_never_falls_back; dart_import_unchanged; named_binding_through_index drives a CALLS edge.

packets.title: Declared model fields: one SCHEMA_FIELDS cell (format ts / go) on every TypeScript interface and field-only class and every Go struct, with Go names by encoding/json's tag rules
packets.area: DT.1 models: model schemas (TS + Go parsers)
packets.rationale: T1 compares models by JSON field names, and no model declaration records its fields. At HEAD, examples-glia and Kina carry no SCHEMA_FIELDS outside DOC_SECTIONs. quokka carries them only on its 4 proto MESSAGE_TYPEs and its swagger contract ops (verified: `glia query <copy> -e 'm(N, K) :- cell(N, "SCHEMA_FIELDS", T), node(N, K), K != "DOC_SECTION".'` -> eg 0, Kina 0, quokka 4 proto messages). On the Go side the JSON name is the json tag, not the Go name: examples-glia `CustomerName string json:"customer_name"` is the real drift, and `json:"-"` (InternalNote) is never on the wire. Parsers extract; the pass compares (DT.1g / DT.1m).
entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - visit_interface (line 1428) - push ts_interface_schema(n, src) (wire::ModelSchema, format ts) onto the INTERFACE node's cells. property_signature name: property_identifier; string unquoted; number text; computed -> skipped + open. `?` -> required false; a top-level `| undefined` -> optional. type = the annotation text, whitespace-collapsed; array = element_type. index_signature -> open. Method / call / construct signatures are skipped. extends = the names collect_interface_heritage (line 1473) reads; a generic or utility base (Pick / Omit / Partial / Required / Readonly / Record, any `X<..>`) -> open

parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - visit_class (line 668) - a class whose body holds only fields (public_field_definition without private / protected / static / #name) and at most a constructor gets the same cell. Constructor parameter properties with public / readonly count as fields

parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs - collect_field_types (line 713) - per struct_type, go_struct_schema(list, src) is pushed onto the STRUCT node (found in acc.nodes by id). Exported names only. json tag via reflect.StructTag rules. An untagged embed -> extends (pointer stripped, qualifier kept). A tagged embed -> a named field (`json:"-"` -> skipped). binding:"required" / validate:"required..." -> bind
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs - (new) parse_json_tag(raw) -> JsonTag { name, skip, omitempty, as_string }
both parsers - a per-file marker
packets.implementation: 1. Go tag rules (encoding/json): `json:"-"` skips the field; `json:"-,"` names it "-"; an empty name -> the Go field name; omitempty -> required false; `,string` -> type "string" (the value is encoded as a JSON string); no tag -> the Go name, required true. Unexported fields are skipped and counted. A struct with no exported field and no embed gets no cell (examples-glia Orders, Products, Memory, Hub, Publisher and Settler get none). The struct's own type name may be unexported (billing's planBody is serialised). `field` is written only when it differs from `name`. 2. TS type text is kept as written (normalised whitespace), so the pass resolves names itself. No node is minted for `type X = {...}` aliases (documented limit). 3. Several cells on one node (TS declaration merging) are unioned by the pass. 4. Unit tests: a TS interface (optional, quoted, readonly, method skipped, index -> open, extends, `extends Pick<..>` -> open); a field-only class vs a service class (no cell); the Go tag table (rename, omitempty, -, -, (dash-comma), string, untagged, unexported, embed, tagged embed, binding/validate required); a struct with only unexported fields -> no cell.

Files: web/package.json (`@angular/core` dep). web/src/models/account.ts: `export interface Audited { createdAt: string; updatedAt?: string; }`; `export interface Account extends Audited { readonly id: string; 'display-name': string; email?: string; roles: string[]; owner: Person; isActive(): boolean; }`; `export interface Settings { theme: 'light' | 'dark'; [flag: string]: unknown; }`; `export class Person { name = ''; age?: number; constructor(public nickname: string) {} }`; `export class AccountStore { private cache = new Map<string, Account>(); get(id: string): Account | undefined { return this.cache.get(id); } }`. api/go.mod: `module example.com/fields/api` go 1.22. api/models/account.go (imports time): `type Audit struct { CreatedAt time.Time json:"createdAt"; UpdatedAt *time.Time json:"updatedAt,omitempty" }`; `type Account struct { Audit; ID string json:"id"; DisplayName string json:"display_name" binding:"required"; Email *string json:"email,omitempty"; Roles []string json:"roles"; Owner Person json:"owner"; Password string json:"-"; Dash string json:"-,"; Balance int64 json:"balance,string"; Region string; secret string }`; `type Person struct { Name string json:"name"; Age int json:"age,omitempty" }`; `type cache struct { rows map[string]*Account }` (gofmt, backtick tags). key.json: framework models-declared-fields, language go, dirs [web, api]. expect_cells (all cell SCHEMA_FIELDS): INTERFACE src::models::account::Account contains `"name":"display-name"` and `"extends":["Audited"]`; INTERFACE src::models::account::Settings `"open":true`; CLASS src::models::account::Person `"name":"age"`; STRUCT models::account::Account `"name":"display_name"`, `"name":"Region"`, `"extends":["Audit"]`, `"field":"Balance","name":"balance","required":true,"type":"string"`, `"field":"Dash","name":"-"`, `"bind":"required"`; STRUCT models::account::Person `"format":"go"`. forbid {kind INTERFACE, name src::models::account::Person, max_nodes 0}. The examples-glia and Kina copies have 0 SCHEMA_FIELDS rows on INTERFACE / CLASS / STRUCT; quokka has only its 4 proto MESSAGE_TYPEs. packets.title: TypeScript client wire shapes: each HTTP call site's response and request shape on its ENDPOINT_HIT (HttpClient / axios type arguments, the body argument's declared type or literal keys for libraries whose body position is known, fetch's JSON.stringify body and `.json() as T`), and an awaited generic call mints its ENDPOINT
packets.rationale: This is the client side of T1: which model a call site expects back and which it sends. At HEAD no ENDPOINT_HIT carries a shape (examples-glia hits are method/path/file/line/col/confidence/template/alias/folded_from/host only, verified). Kina has 90 typed `http.<verb><..>` calls (50 with inline envelopes `get<{ offers: Offer[]; page: number; limit: number }>`) and 41 untyped. Measured gap, verified by the verifier's probe at HEAD: `await axios.get<Foo>(..)`, `await axios.post<Foo>(..)`, `await axios.get<Array<Foo>>(..)`, `(await axios.get<Foo>(..)).data`, `await this.http.get<Foo>(..).toPromise()` and `const x = await this.http.get<Foo>(..)` mint NO ENDPOINT. `axios.get<Foo>(..)` without await, `await axios.get(..)` without a type argument and `await lastValueFrom(this.http.get<Foo>(..))` do. tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2's define-grammar.js:77 lists [call_expression, instantiation_expression, binary_expression, await_expression] as a conflict and builds the awaited generic call as call(function: await_expression(instantiation_expression(member, type_arguments)), arguments), so try_detect_endpoint returns at `func.kind() != "member_expression"`.
entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - try_detect_endpoint (line 2870) - (new) awaited_generic_callee(call) -> Option<(member TsNode, type_arguments TsNode)>: unwrap an await_expression / instantiation_expression function. Used for shapes 1 and 2 and for their type arguments; the parse shape is pinned in a unit test first
parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - push_endpoint (line 2974) / EndpointCandidate (line 463) - gains response: Option<Shape> and request: Option<Shape>, computed from `call`

parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - (new) ts_type_shape(type_node, src) -> Shape: type_identifier / nested_type_identifier -> Named; array_type, Array<X>, ReadonlyArray<X> -> Named{array}; object_type -> Object (property_signature name / ? / type; index_signature -> open); union_type minus null / undefined literal types -> the one left, else Union; any / unknown / object -> Open; other predefined and literal types -> Named{ty} (json_kind reads them); other generics (Pick, Partial, ApiResponse<T>, Observable<T>) -> Open

parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - (new) body_shape(arg, call, src). An object literal -> Object (pair / shorthand keys; spread -> open). An identifier -> the declared type of that name in the enclosing callable: a required/optional_parameter annotation, else a `const`/`let` declarator before the call with an annotation, `x as T`, `x satisfies T`, `new T()` or an object literal. `x as T` / `satisfies` -> T

parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - (new) request_arg(cand, call): which argument is the body. Shape 1 with a receiver field typed HttpClient (the CH.3c field type, `private http: HttpClient` or `inject(HttpClient)`): the second argument of post/put/patch. Shape 2 with an alias imported from `axios`: the second argument of post/put/patch. Aliases from `ky` / `got`: the `json:` property of the second argument's object literal. Any other receiver or library: none (counted request_unknown_client)

parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - fetch arm - request from the init object's `body: JSON.stringify(<expr>)`. Response from `(await fetch(..)).json() as T`, or, for `const r = await fetch(..)` in the same callable, `(await r.json()) as T`, `r.json() as Promise<T>` or `const d: T = await r.json()`
parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs - endpoint_hit_cell (line 3905) - wire::append_hit_fields after `alias`
packets.implementation: 1. Response: the call's type_arguments (first argument) for get / post / put / patch / delete on shape 1 (this.<x>.<verb>) and shape 2 (an import alias); fetch per the entry point. No type argument -> no response key. ky's `.json<T>()` and other post-call typings are not read (documented). 2. Request: per request_arg. HttpClient options objects (the second argument of get / delete) are never bodies. FormData / Blob / string bodies -> none. 3. Type names stay unresolved text (`Order`): the pass resolves them in the hit file's module (DT.1g); the parser never guesses a module. 4. The awaited-generic unwrap applies to endpoint detection only. extract_call_qualifier (CallSites) keeps HEAD behaviour; the verifier's probe shows `await this.repo.find<Foo>(1)` loses its CALLS edge while `this.repo.find<Foo>(2)` keeps it (notes Q4). 5. Tests: get_typed_array; post_body_param_annotation (examples-glia place(order: NewOrder)); patch_object_literal_keys (`{ status: 'cancelled' }`); inline_envelope_type; union_with_null; any_response_is_open; awaited_generic_axios_mints_endpoint plus the parse-shape pin plus the `.toPromise()` chain form; fetch_stringify_body_and_json_as; ky_json_option_is_the_body; custom_wrapper_receiver_records_no_request; untyped_call_writes_no_shape (payload byte-identical to HEAD).

packets.title: Go server wire cells: every known-2xx / unknown-status JSON write and every JSON bind in a handler (gin, echo, fiber, net/http encoding/json, chi render) becomes one MESSAGE_TYPE cell on the handler, its value classified as written (type, call chain, field chain, envelope keys, inline struct), a local replaced by its declaration; plus NavFact::SliceResult
packets.rationale: This is the server side of T1: which model a handler serialises or binds. Measured at HEAD: no node carries a MESSAGE_TYPE cell in examples-glia, Kina or quokka (verified, 0 rows each). Kina (non-test .go files): 278 `c.JSON(` sites, of which 88 have http.StatusOK/Created/Accepted, 175 have another http.Status*, and 15 have a non-literal status (`c.JSON(errorStatus(err), gin.H{"error": ..})`, `c.JSON(status, ..)`: every one an error body). packets.implementation: 1. Status. http.Status<Name> maps to its code through a 2xx-name table (OK 200, Created 201, Accepted 202, NonAuthoritativeInfo 203, NoContent 204, ResetContent 205, PartialContent 206, MultiStatus 207, AlreadyReported 208, IMUsed 226). Any other http.Status* or a non-2xx int literal -> the site is skipped (counted). A 2xx literal -> its code. Implicit forms (fiber JSON(v) without a Status chain, render.JSON, Encode) -> 200, unless an earlier `w.WriteHeader(<x>)` in the same function body names a non-2xx code (skipped), a 2xx code (that code) or a non-literal (status absent). Anything else (a variable, errorStatus(err)) -> status absent (unknown: recorded, never judged by DT.1g). 2. wire_value: a composite literal T{..} / &T{..} / []T{..} / []*T{..} -> Named{ty, array}. gin.H / echo.Map / fiber.Map / map[string]any|interface{} literal -> Object of string-literal keys -> wire_value(value); a non-literal key -> open; depth <= 3. An anonymous struct literal -> Object from its field tags (DT.1c's parse_json_tag). make([]T, ..) -> Named{T, array}. new(T) -> Named{T}. An identifier -> acc.wire_locals[(from, name)], else Open. Any other call -> Call{chain_text(call)} (chain_text at line 2389; None -> Open). A selector -> Chain{chain_text}. Parentheses, & and * are unwrapped. 3. wire_locals cover a short_var_declaration (paired values: `x, err := f()` gives x Call{chain} and err nothing) and a var_spec with a type (slice kept: `var xs []T` -> Named{T, array}; `var req struct{..}` -> Object from tags) or with a value. A name declared twice with different shapes -> Open. Declarations only, in body order (record_body_locals' walk); a later `x = ..` assignment never changes the shape. 4. One ServerWire cell per site on `from` when `from` is a FUNCTION / METHOD (package scope skipped). ty = the simple name of a Named shape (after the last `.`), "" otherwise. raw = the argument text (<= 120 chars). line is 1-based. Identical payloads on one node are kept once. 5. Func-literal route handlers (bodies collect_closure_calls skips) and helper-wrapped writes (`respondJSON(c, v)`) are not read (documented). 6. The original single packet (~580 LOC) grew past ~600 with the verifier's precision rules, so it is split: this half collects and resolves both sides; DT.1m compares them. Reading HTTP_CALLS (resolver edges) is merge-safe because a layout merge drops every `resolver:*` cross edge and re-runs CODE_PASSES (engine/src/merge.rs:237, 334). Client names resolve through g.symbols.module_symbols / module_import_bindings, which the store persists (store/src/code_section.rs SymbolTableStore), so no TS / Dart builder change is needed. examples-glia shows why names alone are wrong: TS `Product` is the Go `CatalogueItem` (GET /api/products), while the Go `models.Product` of the same name is never serialised. packets.implementation: 1. Matching uses exact JSON names, ASCII case-insensitive for a request into a Go server (encoding/json's decode folding, exact match preferred). 2. Response rules (producer server, consumer client): client-only required -> json_field_missing (breaking); client-only optional -> json_field_optional_absent; server-only -> json_field_unread; server omitempty with client required -> json_field_may_be_absent; JSON kinds that differ while both are known (an Unknown name counts as Object only when it resolves to a model, else it is never judged), or array vs scalar -> json_type_mismatch (breaking). Request rules (producer client, consumer server): client-only -> json_field_dropped; server-only with bind required -> json_required_missing (breaking), else json_field_unset; kinds that differ -> json_type_mismatch (breaking). An open side, or a union with an open member, makes no *_only claim (note open). Paths are flattened as `items[].sku`. 3. A model pair needs both sides to be named models with schemas and `confirms` to hold. diverged = any change at that model's level. Recursion goes into same-named fields with models on both sides (depth <= 4), also under inline Object roots (`{ offers: Offer[] }` vs gin.H{"offers": ..}). 4. Types are #[non_exhaustive]. Every list is sorted (route qname, direction, hit file, line, handler qname). 5. Unit tests: the rules table per direction, case folding, open sides, may_be_absent, type mismatch incl. array vs scalar, confirmation threshold (1-field sides, half), recursion, ambiguous server, determinism. 6. engine/tests/model_wire_pairs.rs is extended over models-http-shop: exactly 11 pairs (9 responses plus the POST /api/invoices and PATCH /api/invoices/:id/status requests). The Invoice responses (GET :id, POST, PATCH) each carry customerName json_field_missing (breaking), customer_name json_field_unread and couponCode json_field_optional_absent, with no change naming Note. invoice-pages has the same three under `invoices[]`, and `page` is not judged (strconv.Atoi is unresolved). The POST request has couponCode json_field_dropped. The PATCH request is identical; so are Article/CatalogEntry and the /listings envelope (Listing vs ListingWithSeller flattened). GET /api/listings/:id has sellerName json_field_optional_absent; daily has day json_field_unread; weekly has week json_field_unread. Producer = the op for a response and the client for a request. Ops without SCHEMA_FIELDS (swaggo annotations, feature.yaml) are skipped. 3. packets.rationale: examples-glia's admin selects `sku` on products, and `type Product` lacks it (the query fails at run time). At HEAD the SDL scan mints GRAPHQL_RESOLVER nodes for root types and fields only (`[graphql-sdl] files=1 resolvers=4`, verified). No node or cell holds an object type's fields, and operations record no selection. No new kind: a schema object type is a message type (A10.5 / A10.6 / jsonschema mint MESSAGE_TYPE the same way). The original packet (~590) is split; this half extracts, and DT.1n pairs and reports. Two precision guards the verifier added. (a) A GraphQL type name has no namespace, so `type User` in two services is a name coincidence. In one repo, the type gets the owner segment the LB.8 owner pass already gives its GRAPHQL_RESOLVER siblings (`graphql_resolver:products @api` at HEAD), so two services stay two nodes. Across repos, the identity resolver's message_fqname rule (keyed by qname alone, graph/src/resolvers/identity.rs message_classes) must skip `message:graphql:`, or it would mint FACT SAME_AS on a bare name. (b) contract_fields' collect_holders (shared with contract_breaks) treats every MESSAGE_TYPE as a contract holder. Without a skip, queue topic types would resolve to GraphQL types by simple name (message_types_by_name), and every schema edit would surface as an `unknown unsupported_format` row in contract-breaks / review.

packets.title: glia-export-engram writes `<out>.hints.jsonl` on every run: a header binding it to the gmap by `gmap_digest` (as `<out>.ppr.jsonl` does), then one `{"hint","key"}` row per exported fact, sorted by key. `hint` is that fact's glia node's `graph::identity::Identity::hint()` v1 string, or null when the node has no v1 identity. Backed by a new bulk `glia_graph::identity::identities`
packets.area: DT 0.5.2 tweaks - T12 one hint format (1/2: the export's hints side file)
packets.rationale: T12 (dev-notes/tweaks-0.5.2.md; James 2026-10-16: "yeah sure lets get everyone aligned"). Engram's first real correction row (Kina `entryGuard`) cannot be matched to its fact. The gmap's identity_hint uses the export's own `<file token>:<kind>:<ordinal>` form. The cell store keys a row by LB.6's `Identity::hint` v1 form. Re-measured by the verifier at HEAD 7661c035 with `glia 0.5.1 (build 0.5.1+pd2c8c82058d631f0)`; both binaries were built 22:55 / 22:57, after 4c0b0d6d, the last commit that touched code. The runs used `git archive 8ac238c` copies of Kina. The gmap (decoded from its bincode) holds `frontend/src/app/app.routes.ts:3:0` for `frontend::src::app::app.routes::entryGuard`. `glia build` + `glia cell set .. entryGuard CONV --text ..` stores `v1|3|app.routes.ts|9bdbdf56d843b8d0|entryGuard` (`glia cell ls --json`). That is the same string Engram's own DECISION row in ~/Code/Kina/.glia/cells.jsonl carries; the file is untracked, dated 2026-10-16 23:55, and was only read. Today the export writes only the gmap, `.files.json`, `.meta.json` and `.glia/`, so Engram cannot get the v1 form of a fact. The tweak doc fixes the transport: a digest-bound side file of `{key, hint}` rows, with a `gmap_digest` header as `.ppr.jsonl` has, and no GMAP contract change. Computing the hints needs every exported node's Identity. `identity_of` does one linear node scan per call, which is O(N^2) over an export, so the graph crate gets one bulk derivation that equals it exactly.

packets.implementation:
No Gmap, contract or GMAP_FORMAT_VERSION change. The gmap, `.files.json` and `--since` diff bytes stay the same. `.meta.json` changes only through the moved build and parser stamps.
1. graph/src/identity.rs. Make `HINT_VERSION` pub. Add `pub fn identities(merged: &MergedGraph) -> HashMap<NodeId, Identity>`:
- Walk `merged.graphs` in order with `seen: HashSet<NodeId>`.
- Per graph, build `node_map(g)` once (first occurrence wins, which is identity_of's `g.nodes.iter().find`).
- For every id in `g.nav.kind_by_id.keys()` that `seen.insert`s, run `derive(g, |x| by_id.get(&x).copied(), id)` and insert the Identity when it is Some.
An id's result is identity_of's own: the first graph in graph order whose nav names the id, then its first node instance. Iterating the nav HashMap's keys decides nothing, because each id is visited once and depends on no other id. Doc the map as lookup-only, never iterated into output, plus one sentence: "one derivation per node; `identity_of` scans one graph's nodes per call".
graph/tests/identity_moves.rs adds `identities_match_identity_of_for_every_node`. Over `prior()` and `current()`, for every node of every graph: `identities(&g).get(&n.id) == identity_of(&g, n.id).as_ref()`. And every key in the map has `identity_of(&g, k).is_some()`.
2. engram-export/src/lib.rs. Move build_gmap's body into `pub fn build_gmap_with_nodes(..)`. In pass 2:
- Beside each `nodes.push(GmapNode { key: qname.clone(), .. })` (the key winner), push `Some(n.id)` to `fact_nodes`.
- Beside each NatSpec tag fact push (inside the `for f in m.facts` loop, after the duplicate guard), push `None`.
So `fact_nodes.len() == gmap.nodes.len()`, and index i is gmap.nodes[i]'s glia node.
`build_gmap` becomes `let (g, f, s, _) = build_gmap_with_nodes(..); (g, f, s)`. Its 34 other call sites stay unchanged: 25 in lib.rs including export_engram_gmap and its tests, 9 across tests/contract_v6, documents_v6, identity_v6, natspec_v6 and spans_v6. Only the bin's call moves to the new function.
Add `pub fn hints_side_path(out) -> PathBuf` (`<out>.hints.jsonl`, the `ppr_side_path` shape). Add a crate doc section `## The hints side file (T12)`: one hint format, the v1 form is the cell store's key, data that glia never reads. write_atomic's doc names hints_side too.
3. engram-export/src/hints_side.rs (new, ~150 LOC with tests).
- `pub const HINTS_SIDE_VERSION: u32 = 1`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct HintRow { pub key: String, pub hint: Option<String> }`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct HintsSideStats { pub facts: usize, pub hinted: usize }`.
- `pub fn hint_rows(merged: &MergedGraph, gmap: &Gmap, fact_nodes: &[Option<NodeId>]) -> Vec<HintRow>`: `let ids = glia_graph::identity::identities(merged)`. For each (i, node) in gmap.nodes, `hint = fact_nodes.get(i).copied().flatten().and_then(|id| ids.get(&id)).map(Identity::hint)`. Then sort by key in String byte order; keys are unique in an export.
A row is written for every fact, null when the fact has no v1 identity:
- ENDPOINTs, ROUTEs, config / data_entity nodes, doc sections (DOC_SPACE parents, no MODULE) and non-code files;
- NatSpec tag facts, which have no glia node of their own. A `<sym>#natspec:..` key with the symbol's hint would rekey onto the symbol in `cell set`, so null is right.
So `facts == gmap.nodes.len()`, and Engram can check the file is complete.
- `side_bytes(rows, digest)`: line 1 is the header, a BTreeMap `{"facts":<n>,"gmap_digest":"<digest:016x>","hint_version":HINT_VERSION,"hinted":<h>,"hints_side":1}`, the same `{digest:016x}` the PPR header and meta.json's `gmap_digest` use. Then one line per row, `{"hint":"v1|.."|null,"key":"<key>"}` (BTreeMap, serde_json compact, non-ASCII literal), each `\n`-terminated.
- `pub fn write_hints_side(merged, gmap, fact_nodes, digest: u64, out: &Path) -> io::Result<HintsSideStats>` writes through crate::write_atomic.
The bytes are a pure function of the graph and the gmap. Identity holds no RepoId: it is the kind id, the file basename, the nav local chain, and FNV-1a of the whitespace-collapsed CODE. The rows are sorted by key and no map is iterated into them.
Unit tests:
- the header literal for digest 0xabc: `{"facts":3,"gmap_digest":"0000000000000abc","hint_version":"v1","hinted":1,"hints_side":1}`;
- rows are sorted by key whatever the gmap order;
- a None or out-of-range fact_nodes entry gives `"hint":null`;
- two calls give equal bytes.
4. bin.
(a) Before the gmap write, next to the stale diff and PPR side file removals, remove `hints_side_path(&out_path)`. NotFound is fine; any other error is exit 5 (`error removing the stale hints side file ..`). A crash after the gmap write then never leaves a hints file naming another digest.
(b) Call `build_gmap_with_nodes`.
(c) After the diff and before the PPR side file, time `write_hints_side(&result.merged, &gmap, &fact_nodes, stats.digest, &hints_out)`. On Err, print `error writing the hints side file <path>: <e>` and set code 9 if code == 0 (the gmap, its sidecars and the diff are already complete). Exit 9 is free: the bin uses 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
(d) Written on EVERY run, with no flag. Engram wants it on every export, and it costs one identity derivation per node, unlike the per-fact PPR pushes behind `--ppr-candidates`.
(e) The marker, printed right after the `glia build=` line and before `ppr side:`: `[engram-export] hints side: <facts> facts, <hinted> v1 hints, <ms> ms -> <out>.hints.jsonl`.
(f) Doc:
- the write order: `<out>.diff`, `<out>.ppr.jsonl` and `<out>.hints.jsonl` are deleted first, then gmap, files.json, meta.json, diff, hints side file, PPR side file, `<out>.glia/`;
- exit 9;
- one paragraph on the file.
`--since` does not touch it: the v1 form is basename-based and carries no LB.6 file tokens.
5. engram-export/tests/hints_side_v6.rs (new, ~170 LOC). Scratch lives outside git, as in ppr_side_v6.rs. Fixture:
- `fx/svc/chain.py`: ppr_side_v6's CHAIN_PY, plus a class with a method whose body is at least 40 collapsed characters, so a body hash is non-zero;
- `fx/svc/cart.py`: the verifier's measured twin, exactly `class Cart:\n    def total(self): return sum(item.price * item.quantity for item in self.items)\n    def summary(self): handler = self.total; return handler()\n`. Its METHOD and the ATTRIBUTE the `self.total` read mints share `svc::cart::Cart::total`: two NodeIds, kind 4 and 35. Measured on the one-file copy: `glia cell set .. app::Cart::total CONV` gives `target=ambiguous`; `--kind METHOD` stores `v1|4|app.py|8285f8265b86a93e|Cart::total`; the ATTRIBUTE's hint is `v1|35|app.py|0000000000000000|Cart::total`;
- `fx/web/api.ts`: `export async function load() { return fetch('/api/orders'); }` (a positionless ENDPOINT);
- `fx/docs/README.md`: one section.
Tests:
(a) side_file_binds_to_its_gmap_and_lists_every_fact. Export with `--no-persist`. The header equals {facts: gmap.nodes.len(), gmap_digest: meta.json's gmap_digest == format!("{:016x}", content_digest(gmap bytes)), hint_version "v1", hinted: the non-null rows, hints_side 1}. Row keys are strictly ascending and, as a set, equal the gmap keys. Every non-null hint satisfies `Identity::parse_hint(h).map(|i| i.hint()) == Some(h)`. The `endpoint:` row and the doc-section row are null.
(b) hints_bind_their_fact_on_the_layout_a_cell_write_reads, the one-format test. In process, `generate_one(fx)` then `build_gmap_with_nodes`. For every Some(id), the row equals `identity_of(&merged, id).map(|i| i.hint())`. Then write a rooted layout with `persist_graph(&r.merged, &r.repo_labels, &r.repo_roots, &r.parse_errors, dir, "test")`; its CODE is stored as spans (CD.7c). Then `load_layout(dir)`, which uses the same read_merged_sharded_meta as `glia_store::write_cell`'s fresh-layout read. On the loaded graph, every Some(id) gives the same hint. And for every hinted row, `QnameIndex::build(&loaded.merged, None).resolve(key, None, Some(hint))` is `CellTarget::Bound(id)` of the row's fact. For the Cart key, `resolve(key, None, None)` is `Ambiguous`, and the row's hint has kind 4 (the METHOD, the export's key winner by `key_rank`). The hint alone, with no `--kind`, singles out the fact's node.
(c) rerun_and_flags_change_nothing. Two runs give identical hints bytes, and a run with `--ppr-candidates 3` gives the same hints bytes. A garbage `<out>.hints.jsonl` placed before a run is replaced. The gmap, files.json and meta.json bytes are the same whatever the flags.
(d) The marker: exactly one `[engram-export] hints side: <facts> facts, <hinted> v1 hints, ` line, ending `-> <path>`.

packets.rationale:
T12 second half (dev-notes/tweaks-0.5.2.md). The gap is "`glia cell set` takes no hint". The ask: "`glia cell set --hint` / pyo3 `write_cell` / `PyGraph.set_cell` `hint=` take that form, validated, with a reported target when a fresh layout's binding disagrees". The store already accepts a caller's hint (`CellWrite::with_hint`; write_cell binds with `w.hint.clone().or_else(hint_of)`), but no surface lets a caller pass one. Re-measured by the verifier at HEAD 7661c035 with target/debug/glia, `0.5.1+pd2c8c82058d631f0`:
- `glia cell set .. --hint 'v1|3|app.routes.ts|9bdbdf56d843b8d0|entryGuard'` gives `error: unexpected argument '--hint' found`, exit 2.
- The committed pyo3 surface py/api_surface/cells.txt has no hint on set_cell / write_cell; a `hint=` keyword is a TypeError.
- The binding is silent when a hint disagrees. On a Kina 8ac238c copy, a CONV row written on entryGuard stores hint `v1|3|app.routes.ts|9bdbdf56d843b8d0|entryGuard`. After `'/home'` -> `'/dashboard'` in its body and `glia build`, the node's own hint (captured by a DECISION write) is `v1|3|app.routes.ts|2623b9a9f0ebe171|entryGuard`. `glia cell ls --check --json` still reports both rows `bound` and says nothing about the hint.
- A hint is also the only thing that picks between nodes sharing a qname without `--kind`. On the one-file fixture below, a Python METHOD and the ATTRIBUTE that `self.total` mints share `app::Cart::total`. `glia cell set .. app::Cart::total CONV --text ..` gives `target=ambiguous` with hint null. With `--kind METHOD` it gives `target=bound` with hint `v1|4|app.py|8285f8265b86a93e|Cart::total`. `--kind ATTRIBUTE` binds the ATTRIBUTE, hint `v1|35|app.py|0000000000000000|Cart::total`.
Engram's corrections writer is to switch to `--hint` with the v1 hints from DT.12a's `<out>.hints.jsonl` (the tweak doc's plan, step 4).

packets.implementation:
The binding rule does not change. The exact qname (and kind) wins; the hint narrows several qname matches or re-binds a moved node (graph::cells::QnameIndex::resolve). The next build binds the row the same way (engine external::cells), so the write still lands on the qname's node. What changes is that a disagreement is REPORTED instead of hidden.
1. store/src/cells.rs, validation. In `prepare(w)`, after the kind-name check, when `w.hint` is Some(h):
- `Identity::parse_hint(h)` must be Some, else `invalid(format!("hint {h:?} is not a v1 identity hint (v1|<kind id>|<file>|<body:016x>|<local>, the form `glia cell ls --json` and glia-export-engram's <out>.hints.jsonl carry)"))`;
- its kind id must be in `node_kind::ALL`, else `hint {h:?} names node kind id <k>, which is not registered`;
- when `w.kind` is Some(k), the hint's kind name must equal k, else `hint {h:?} names a <NAME> but kind is <k>`. Today `IdentityIndex::rebind` silently ignores such a hint, and an exact `--kind` match binds the other twin with no word.
Each is a StoreError::Invalid (`invalid cell write: ..`), raised before the lock and before any write, so nothing is written.
No existing in-repo caller passes a non-v1 hint: rekey_rows and set_cell_in pass `identity_of` hints of a node bound with the same kind; grep finds no test that sets one. Hand-edited `.glia/cells.jsonl` rows are NOT validated: the build and `ls --check` keep ignoring an unparseable hint, as `IdentityIndex::rebind` does today.
2. store/src/cells.rs, the report.
- Add `const HINT_DIFFERS: &str = "hint_differs";`.
- Add `fn hint_report(merged, t: &CellTarget, caller: Option<&str>) -> (Option<String>, Vec<String>)`. `node_hint` is `identity_of(merged, id).map(|i| i.hint())` for Bound(id) / Rekeyed{id}, else None.
- `differs` is computed only when `t` is Bound and the caller gave a hint. Parse both and list the fields that differ, in the order kind, file, body, local. When the node has no v1 identity (an ENDPOINT, a ROUTE) the list is `["no_identity"]`. Rekeyed keeps its own target and tier, because the hint did the binding there. Ambiguous / Orphaned / Rejected have no node.
- `pub fn set_binding(&mut self, merged, t, caller_hint)`: `set_target(t)`, then `(node_hint, hint_differs) = hint_report(..)`; when hint_differs is non-empty, `target = HINT_DIFFERS`.
- In write_cell's `LayoutState::Fresh` arm, compute `hint_report(merged, &target, w.hint.as_deref())` right after apply_cell_write, while `merged` is still held. `w.hint` is the caller's; the `hint_of` fill is not compared. Apply it to `out` after `set_target`. With no fresh layout the target stays `pending` and node_hint None, since there is nothing to compare against.
- remove_cell_entry keeps set_target; its struct literal initialises `node_hint: None, hint_differs: Vec::new()`.
- The stored row keeps the CALLER's hint verbatim, which is today's rule (see notes, open question).
- Docs: CellWriteOutcome's `target` doc lists `hint_differs` (bound by the qname and applied, as the next build applies it; the bound node's own hint differs from the caller's; see `node_hint` / `hint_differs`). Update the module doc's "Where the write lands" paragraph too.
3. engine/tests/cell_write_api.rs (~80 LOC).
(a) caller_hint_is_validated. Each of these gives Err(Invalid) naming the reason: `a.py:1:0` (the gmap identity_hint form), `v1|999|a.py|0000000000000000|f`, and a FUNCTION hint with `with_kind(Some("CLASS"))`. No `.glia/cells.jsonl` is created, and a fresh layout stays byte-identical (shards()).
(b) an_agreeing_hint_binds. Persist, then write with the node's own hint (identity_of). That gives target `bound`, node_hint == the hint, hint_differs empty, and the row stores it.
(c) a_differing_hint_is_reported_and_applied. The own hint with its body field replaced by `0123456789abcdef` gives target `hint_differs`, hint_differs ["body"], write_through Applied. SOURCE's bodies are under 40 chars, so the own body field is 0000000000000000 and still differs. The entry lands on the qname's node and equals a fresh generate_one's payload (write-through == rebuild), and the row stores the caller's hint. The local replaced by `other` gives ["local"]. A write with no gmap dir gives target `pending`, node_hint None.
(d) a_hint_singles_out_one_of_two_twins. Fixture: the measured Cart text, exactly `class Cart:\n    def total(self): return sum(item.price * item.quantity for item in self.items)\n    def summary(self): handler = self.total; return handler()\n`. With no hint and no kind the write is `ambiguous`. The METHOD's own hint with no kind gives `bound` on the METHOD's id. The same hint with `with_kind(Some("ATTRIBUTE"))` is Err(Invalid).
4. cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs (~25 LOC).
- SetArgs: `/// The node's move-stable v1 identity hint (`v1|<kind id>|<file>|<body:016x>|<local>`, as `cell ls --json` and glia-export-engram's <out>.hints.jsonl carry it): picks between nodes sharing <qname>, re-binds a moved node, and is stored with the row; the target reads `hint_differs` when the qname's node has another hint.` `#[arg(long, value_name = "HINT")] hint: Option<String>`.

- marker(): after the ` redacted=` suffix rule, append ` differs=<f1,f2>` when `!o.hint_differs.is_empty()`.

- The rekey path is unchanged; identity_of hints are always valid v1.

The diff is one line, `  arg hint pos=- long=hint short=- required=false num_args=1 action=Set default=- value_names=HINT global=false hidden=false`, between `arg help` and `arg json` under `cmd glia cell set`.

Docstrings name the v1 form and the hint_differs target.

The store's own comparison sees the live fill as `w.hint` and may differ, so this override is what returns the live binding's report, as the target is today.

Body-only differences will be common in the Engram flow: any edit to a function since its export gives `hint_differs differs=body`. That is honest, but it is noisy if the caller treats it as an error (open question).
Two marker formatters (cli/src/cmd/store/cell.rs and py/src/cells.rs) both have to gain the ` differs=` suffix, and a test pins each.
set_cell_in must override the store's report with the live one (set_binding with the caller's hint), or a pyo3 write without hint= could read hint_differs whenever the live PyGraph and the layout disagree.
identity_of in write_cell is one linear node scan per write, which is fine for single writes; a bulk import still writes the sidecar and rebuilds (store doc).
store is a hashed root, so PARSER_STAMP moves: one parse-cache invalidation.
The validation refuses only through write_cell: a non-v1 hint already in a hand-edited cells.jsonl keeps loading, and is ignored on rebind as today.
The README edit is limited to one usage line. It departs from the T12 spec rule "never README.md" (see notes), and the closing docs packet still owns the prose below it.
No unwrap or panic in non-test code, and no new dependency (store already imports glia_graph::identity).

packets.title: Inferred-model breaks against a git rev (engine): every http_model / graphql_selection exchange judged base -> working tree, the SERVER side's change against what its CLIENT reads or sends and the client's change against what is served (json_name_changed, response_field_removed, new_required_request_field, json_field_missing, schema_field_removed, ...), one row per client <-> server model pair with located read / write sites and field lines, the pairing's tier, and the advisory gate (check::is_blocking under min_tier, default fact)
packets.area: DT.1 models: inferred-model evolution (engine contract_breaks/models.rs + graph resolvers/models.rs)
packets.rationale:
James's ruling 4 (tweaks-0.5.2.md, 2026-10-17, *"yes ?"*): a change to an INFERRED client <-> server contract model is judged at PR time and is ADVISORY by default. It blocks only for a FACT pairing or on opt-in. This packet is the engine answer; DT.1p wires it into contract-breaks / review / CLI / pyo3, the CC.8a -> CC.8b and CC.6a -> CC.6b split.

MEASURED BASELINE (spec run: HEAD 9819503c plus wave 15's tree; re-measured by the verifier with target/debug/glia built 02:10 from wave 15's in-progress tree, on copies under ~/.cache/glia-spec-t1o/, since removed).
(a) examples-glia fbfb6c0 as two commits, v1 Order.CustomerName `json:"customerName"`, v2 `json:"customer_name"` (the examples-glia bug). `glia contract-breaks <copy> --base HEAD~1` printed `[contract-breaks] base=HEAD~1 pairs=0 breaking=0 compatible=0 unknown=0 removed=0 added=0 orphaned_clients=0`, exit 0, absence 'no contract (OpenAPI / AsyncAPI op or message type) in either graph and no client edge removed vs HEAD~1'. `glia review` exited 0 with `[review] ... violations new=0 resolved=0 blocking=false`, listing only `modified api::internal::models::order::Order STRUCT api/internal/models/order.go:20` and its MODULE, impact 0.
(b) The trimmed fixture this packet commits (rebuilt by the verifier from the description below: 13 files, 265 lines) gave the same numbers. HTTP_CALLS 3/3 (endpoint:GET:/api/orders/${…} @web -> GET /api/orders/:id @api at order.service.ts:14, POST :18, PATCH :22, all derived). HANDLED_BY fact: Orders::Get / Place / ChangeStatus at orders.go:22-24. GRAPHQL_CALLS 2/2 in wave 15's tree (Restock and StockList, both derived; StockList pairs because DT.11a is in that tree). No SCHEMA_FIELDS or MESSAGE_TYPE cells yet (DT.1c / DT.1e are unlanded). CODE / POSITION verified: `Order struct {` opens the STRUCT's CODE at order.go:20 (CustomerName :22), `interface Order {` at order.ts:9 (customerName :11), and the StockList op's CODE (DT.11a's document) opens on queries.ts:3 with `stock` on :9 (Restock's `stock` on :19).
So the bug that examples-glia was built to show (the client never receives the name) cannot be seen at PR time.

WHY AN EVOLUTION JUDGE, NOT A DIFF OF DT.1i's DRIFT. contract_fields (DT.1i) compares the two sides at one moment. A diff of its rows would show the rename as two unrelated drifts (customerName json_field_missing + customer_name json_field_unread). It would also miss server changes that DT.1m's static verdicts call non-breaking: an optional client read that the server stops sending, omitempty added to a field the client requires, and a renamed request field whose value the server now silently drops. The server-side rules here are the OpenAPI RESPONSE / REQUEST evolution rules contract_breaks.rs already applies, under their names (response_field_removed, response_field_added, response_type_changed, response_field_now_optional, request_field_removed, request_field_added, new_required_request_field, request_type_changed), restricted to the fields the paired client actually reads or sends: each change's `breaking` says whether that client is hit. Two rules are new because OpenAPI has no rename: json_name_changed / request_json_name_changed. The client-side rules keep DT.1m / DT.1n's names and verdicts (json_field_missing, json_field_optional_absent, json_type_mismatch, json_field_may_be_absent, json_required_missing, json_field_unset, json_field_dropped, graphql_field_undefined). So one command speaks one rule language.

THE GATE uses check's own machinery. The tier is why::tier_of over the edges that join the client site to the server model (the tiering check and review use). Blocking is check::is_blocking(tier, min_tier), with check's values (fact | derived). HEURISTIC never blocks. The default min tier is fact (check's per-rule default, DEFAULT_MIN_TIER, is derived) because the ruling makes inferred pairings advisory. In 0.5.2 every HTTP / GraphQL pairing is resolver-paired (HTTP_CALLS and GRAPHQL_CALLS measured derived), so no model row blocks unless the opt-in is set. The FACT branch is real code, reached by a FACT channel edge (a future SCIP or generated-client pairing), and is unit-tested.

ROWS COLLAPSE per (client model, server model) pair, per James's ruling 3 ('contract-model classes collapse in answers'). Each row lists every exchange that joins the pair, located.
entry_points: engine/src/contract_breaks/models.rs (new child module of the public slot; engine/src/contract_breaks.rs gains `mod models;` and `pub use models::{model_breaks, ModelBreak, ModelBreakArgs, ModelBreaks, ModelChange, ModelExchange, ModelSite, MODEL_MIN_TIERS};`, no facade edit; api_stability follows a slot file's `mod` + `pub use` into contract_breaks/models.rs) - pub fn model_breaks(rev: &RevDelta, args: &ModelBreakArgs) -> ModelBreaks over rev.before.merged / rev.after / rev.delta / rev.answer.base: model_breaks_of plus the absence when no row is listed

models.rs - pub(crate) fn model_breaks_of(base: &str, before: &MergedGraph, after: &GenerateResult, delta: &GraphDelta, args: &ModelBreakArgs) -> ModelBreaks: the body, with `absence` always None (the standalone model_breaks adds it, so the contract-breaks / review wiring of DT.1p prints no extra `[absence]` line). pub(crate) from the start so DT.1p only adds a `pub(crate) use` in contract_breaks.rs and never edits this file; it is used by model_breaks here, so no dead_code / unused warning

models.rs - pub const MODEL_MIN_TIERS: &[&str] = &[check::FACT, check::DERIVED] (default first); #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct ModelBreakArgs { pub min_tier: &'static str } with Default = fact. Any spelling other than `derived` is judged as fact (the advisory default, as check::min_tier_of reads a hand-edited spelling as its default); the surfaces validate (DT.1p)

models.rs - #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] types in this field order: ModelBreaks { base, min_tier, rows: Vec<ModelBreak>, exchanges, breaking, blocking, advisory, compatible, absence: Option<Absence> }; ModelBreak { pairing (`http_model` | `graphql_selection`, the contract_fields pairing names of DT.1i / DT.1n whose pairs it judges), direction (`response` | `request` | `selection`), client: contract_fields::FieldSide, server: FieldSide, exchanges: Vec<ModelExchange>, status (`breaking` | `compatible`), change (`modified` | `added`), changed (`server` | `client` | `both` | `pairing`), tier, blocking: bool, note: Option<&'static str>, changes: Vec<ModelChange> }; ModelExchange { key, tier, client_site: ModelSite, server_site: ModelSite }; ModelChange { field, change (`removed` | `renamed` | `added` | `type` | `required`), side (`server` | `client` | `both`), rule, breaking, before: Option<String>, after: Option<String>, client: Option<ModelSite>, server: Option<ModelSite> }; ModelSite { file: Option<String>, line: Option<i64> (1-based), at_base: bool }

models.rs - fn judge(direction, c0: Option<&WireFields>, c1: &WireFields, s0: Option<&WireFields>, s1: &WireFields, fold: bool) -> Vec<ModelChange>: the rules table (implementation step 4), a pure function unit-tested without a graph

models.rs - fn exchange_tier(m: &MergedGraph, ex: &Exchange) -> &'static str: per joining category the strongest why::tier_of of the edges between the exchange's two ends (Evidence::of(edge), as review_edges reads it), then the weakest across categories. HTTP: the HTTP_CALLS endpoint -> route cross edge, the HANDLED_BY route -> handler edge, and DT.1f's handler -USES-> server model edge of the exchange's form (rule json_response / json_bind) when the server root is a model. GraphQL: the GRAPHQL_CALLS op -> resolver edge

models.rs - fn member_site(m: &MergedGraph, loc: &Locator, node: NodeId, path_segment: &str, member: &str, format: WireFormat) -> Option<ModelSite>: the node's located line plus the index of the first line of its in-memory CODE cell (line 0 = the POSITION line) that declares or reads the member; fn selection_site(m, loc, op: NodeId, path: &[&str]) -> Option<ModelSite>: the line of a selected field in the op's CODE cell (DT.11a's document), brace depth tracked

graph/src/resolvers/models.rs - #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct WireFields { pub fields: BTreeMap<String, WireField>, pub open: BTreeSet<String> } and pub struct WireField { name, member, required, bind_required, kind: Option<&'static str>, array, ty, model: Option<NodeId>, declared_by: Option<NodeId> }; pub fn wire_fields(merged: &MergedGraph, side: &ResolvedShape, direction: WireDirection) -> WireFields; pub fn graphql_fields(merged: &MergedGraph, pair: &GraphqlPair) -> (WireFields, WireFields) returns (selection, served); model_fields records each entry's declaring node

graph/src/resolvers/mod.rs - pub use additions: `graphql_fields, wire_fields, WireField, WireFields` (flat through the resolvers glob, as DT.1g / DT.1m / DT.1n export client_wires / wire_pairs / graphql_pairs; Wire-prefixed beside DT.1m's WirePair / WireChange, no ambiguous_glob_reexports; grep finds no existing wire_fields / WireField / graphql_fields)
packets.implementation:
1. GRAPH: ONE-SIDED FLATTENING (graph/src/resolvers/models.rs).
- wire_fields(merged, side, direction) flattens one ResolvedShape (DT.1g).
- The root is the path `""`. Its kind is `array` / `object` / `any`. A root array's element fields take their JSON names unprefixed. Nested paths follow DT.1m's flattening: `lines[].productId`, an envelope's `invoices[].customerName`.
- It recurses into a field whose element type resolves to a model, to depth <= 4. A model already on the current path is never re-entered.
  - TS / Dart: resolve_client_type in the declaring model's own module.
  - Go: the field's `model` qname that DT.1f's nested_models wrote.
  - Each model is read through model_fields. model_fields now also records, per entry, the node whose SCHEMA_FIELDS declares it (the model itself, or the `extends` base it was flattened from). That node is `declared_by`. Its other outputs, and so wire_pairs / graphql_pairs / the models resolver / contract_fields, are unchanged.
- kind maps wire::json_kind(schema format, ty) (code-domain/src/wire.rs: WireFormat, JsonKind) onto `string` | `number` | `boolean` | `array` | `object` | `any` | `null`. A JsonKind::Unknown becomes `object` when it resolves to a model, else None (never judged).
- member = ModelField::member() (the cell's `field`, else its `name`). required = ModelField.required. bind_required = ModelField.bind_required.
- `open` gets:
  - the path of an object / any field that has no model;
  - the path of an open model or union, or an Open shape;
  - `""` when the whole side is open (an open root, or a custom MarshalJSON / UnmarshalJSON in that direction, as model_fields decides).
- graphql_fields(merged, pair) (DT.1n's GraphqlPair) returns two WireFields.
  - The selection: the op's root entry for the pair's root field, keyed by schema-field path. A key is a ShapeField's `field` when aliased, else its name. `name` is the response key, `member` the schema field, required true. A spread or inline fragment adds an open path, as DT.1j marks it.
  - The served side: the schema MESSAGE_TYPE's SCHEMA_FIELDS (format graphql, required = non-null), recursing into MESSAGE_TYPE-typed fields of the same owner as DT.1n does. declared_by is that MESSAGE_TYPE.
- No HashMap iteration reaches output.
- Unit tests: nested model, root array unprefixed, envelope prefix, declared_by through an extends base, cycle stop, open paths (inline object, index signature, MarshalJSON per direction), member from `field`, GraphQL alias mapping.

2. EXCHANGES PER SIDE (engine models.rs).
- From glia_graph::wire_pairs(m).pairs (pairing http_model; only directions with sides on both ends) and glia_graph::graphql_pairs(m).pairs (pairing graphql_selection), on each side's MergedGraph.
- Each exchange records:
  - its ident (pairing, direction, route-or-op id, handler-or-resolver id, endpoint id, hit file);
  - its client root: the client model, else the ENDPOINT / op;
  - its server root: the server model, else the handler / schema MESSAGE_TYPE;
  - its WireFields (wire_fields / graphql_fields);
  - the static breaking changes of DT.1m / DT.1n;
  - its sites. client_site is the ENDPOINT_HIT `file` / `line` (stored 1-based, measured), or the op's location. server_site is the ServerWire cell's `line` in the handler's file (the JSON write for a response, the bind for a request), or the GRAPHQL_RESOLVER's location.
- Several hits that share an ident (one file) keep the first by line.
- An exchange is unjudged (counted, never listed) when its WirePair notes ambiguous_server, when its GraphqlPair is refused or noted open (a conflicting payload, an interface / union return), or when either side's `open` holds `""`.

3. PAIRING ACROSS THE REV.
- Before-side ids are mapped through delta.moved_nodes. The rev is built under the working tree's identity, so an unchanged qname is the same NodeId.
- First match on the ident plus the client root.
- Then, within one (pairing, direction, route-or-op key), take the one unmatched candidate left on each side. This covers a renamed client model, a renamed handler and a moved hit file, which change the ident or the root but not the route; with several candidates on a side nothing is matched.
- An after-only exchange is a new pairing. A before-only one is `lost` (counted only: a lost HTTP / GraphQL pairing whose channel edge went away is already an orphaned client in contract_breaks).

4. THE RULES TABLE.
Let C0 / C1 be the client's field at path p at the rev / in the working tree, and S0 / S1 the server's. A kind is known when it is Some and not `any`. `reads` / `sends` / `selects` mean C1 has p.

RESPONSE (the server produces, the client reads; names exact).
Server-side changes, judged against C1:
- S0 only, and S1 has a path q under the same parent with the same member, which S0 lacks: renamed, rule json_name_changed (before p, after q). Breaking iff C1 has p and not q. q is consumed.
- S0 only otherwise (the member was removed or tagged `json:"-"`): removed, rule response_field_removed. Breaking iff C1 has p.
- S1 only and not consumed: added, rule response_field_added, compatible.
- Both known, kinds differ: type, rule response_type_changed. Listed only when C1 has p. Breaking iff C1's kind is known and differs from S1's.
- Required to not required (omitempty / pointer): required, rule response_field_now_optional. Listed only when C1 has p. Breaking iff C1 is required.
- Not required to required: not listed.
Client-side changes, when S0 == S1 =: S:
- C1 only, no S: added, rule json_field_missing (breaking) when C1 is required, else json_field_optional_absent (compatible).
- Kinds differ and C1's known kind differs from S's: type, rule json_type_mismatch, breaking.
- Optional to required with S not required: required, rule json_field_may_be_absent, compatible (DT.1m's verdict).
- C0 only, or C1 only with S present: not listed.

REQUEST (the client produces, the server binds; fold = a Go server, names ASCII case-folded with exact first, as DT.1m).
Server-side changes, judged against C1:
- Rename (same member): rule request_json_name_changed. Breaking iff C1 sends p and not q (the client's value no longer reaches the member).
- S0 only otherwise: rule request_field_removed, compatible.
- S1 only: when bind-required and C1 lacks p, rule new_required_request_field, breaking. Otherwise rule request_field_added, compatible. Not listed when bind-required and C1 sends p.
- Both, bind optional to required, and C1 lacks p: required, rule new_required_request_field, breaking.
- Kinds differ and C1's known kind differs from S1's: rule request_type_changed, breaking.
Client-side changes:
- C0 only and S bind-required: removed, rule json_required_missing, breaking.
- C0 only and S optional: rule json_field_unset, compatible.
- C1 only, no S: rule json_field_dropped, compatible.
- Kinds differ: rule json_type_mismatch, breaking.

SELECTION (GraphQL; a schema field nobody selects is never a change).
Server-side changes:
- S0 only and C1 selects p: rule schema_field_removed, breaking.
- Selected, kinds differ: rule schema_field_type_changed, breaking.
- Selected, non-null to nullable: rule schema_field_now_nullable, breaking.
- S1 only: not listed.
Client-side changes:
- C1 only, no S: rule graphql_field_undefined, breaking.

COMMON.
- side = `both` when both S and C moved at p; the server rule then applies, judged against C1.
- Only the topmost of a removed or added subtree is listed.
- No claim that needs an absence is made under a path in the relevant side's `open` (row note `open`).
- The root path `""` is displayed `(root)`.
- before / after are the moved side's declaration: the type text, the JSON name for a rename, `required` / `optional` (`non-null` / `nullable` in GraphQL).
- A new pairing lists only its static breaking changes (the same rule names), with change `added`, side `client`, note `new_pairing`, row changed `pairing`.

5. TIER AND GATE.
- An exchange's tier is exchange_tier (entry points). A category with no joining edge counts as derived, as tier_of treats a missing evidence. The client type is read at its call site and adds no edge.
- A row's tier is its strongest exchange's (review's reduced-violation rule: the strongest kept row).
- blocking = status breaking && check::is_blocking(row.tier, min_tier).

6. ROWS.
- Exchanges are grouped by (pairing, direction, client root, server root), using working-tree ids.
- Exchanges within a row are sorted by (key, client_site).
- changes = the union over the row's exchanges, deduplicated by (field, rule, before, after), sorted by (field, rule).
- status = breaking when any change breaks, else compatible. A row with no change is not listed. change = `added` when every exchange is new.
- client / server are FieldSides from one Locator per side (an op's format `graphql`; an inline root's the ENDPOINT / handler).
- Keys: HTTP is the route qname with its owner dropped (glia_code_domain::endpoint::split_owner, as DT.1i keys: `GET /api/orders/:id`); GraphQL is `<op type> <op name> <root field>` (DT.1n's key).
- Rows are sorted by (breaking < compatible, pairing, direction, client qname, server qname).

7. FIELD LINES (ModelChange.client / server).
- member_site scans the declaring node's in-memory CODE cell (rev builds are in-memory GenerateResults: CODE is Text, never a CodeSpan). CODE line i is source line POSITION + i, verified: `Order struct {` at order.go:20, `interface Order {` at order.ts:9.
- Patterns:
  - Go (the member): `^\s*<Member>(\s|,)`;
  - TS (the JSON name): `^\s*(readonly\s+)?['"]?<name>['"]?\??\s*:`;
  - Dart (DT.1l's models): the first line holding the fromJson subscript `['<name>']` / `["<name>"]`, else a field declaration `^\s*(late\s+)?(final\s+)?\S.*\s<member>\s*[;=]`.
- Fallback: the declaring node's own line. An inline root (an ENDPOINT's literal body, a handler's gin.H) is located at the exchange's client_site / server_site.
- A removed field is located, in order: at the working tree's declaring node when its CODE still declares the member (a `json:"-"` tag); at the base's declaring node's member line (at_base true); at the working tree root's own line.
- GraphQL: the client side is selection_site in the op's CODE cell (DT.11a's document; verified: the StockList op's CODE opens on queries.ts:3, `stock` on :9; Restock's on :19). Each path segment is the first line, after its parent's line and at brace depth 1 below the parent's selection set, matching `^\s*(<key>\s*:\s*)?<member>\b`; fallback the op's line. The server side is the MESSAGE_TYPE's own line: DT.1j specifies no CODE cell on it (today's GRAPHQL_RESOLVER nodes carry only POSITION, measured), so no per-field schema line exists.

8. ABSENCE (model_breaks only).
When there are no rows: absence::empty(&after.merged, "model_breaks", &format!("rev {base}"), "no_match", note, &["HTTP_CALLS", "GRAPHQL_CALLS"], None), with unparsed_files from after.parse_errors. The note is:
- with no exchange: 'no client <-> server model exchange (an HTTP call or GraphQL operation typed on both sides) in either graph vs <base>';
- otherwise: '<J> client <-> server model <exchange|exchanges> judged vs <base>, none changed what a client reads or sends' (J = exchanges - unjudged, absence::plural), plus '; <U> unjudged (an open or ambiguous side)' when U > 0.

9. MARKER once per model_breaks_of call. `exchanges` counts every working-tree exchange (http + graphql); `unjudged` is the part of it never judged; breaking = blocking + advisory. The module doc of contract_breaks.rs gains an INFERRED MODELS paragraph pointing here.

10. TESTS.
- Unit tests in models.rs, at least 26: every table row above in each direction; case folding; open paths; the topmost rule; the coordinated server + client rename (compatible, side both); new_pairing; the route-key fallback (a renamed handler is matched, not a new pairing); tiering (fact under fact blocks, derived under fact is advisory, derived under derived blocks, heuristic never blocks, the row takes the strongest exchange's tier, a category's strongest edge counts); member_site per format with its fallback chain; selection_site depth tracking; determinism.
- engine/tests/model_shop/mod.rs (shared like git_fixture; it uses `crate::git_fixture::GitRepo`, so every test crate that declares `mod model_shop;` also declares `mod git_fixture;`): renamed() -> GitRepo (copy engine/tests/data/model-breaks-shop sorted, commit v1, replace the first `json:"customerName"` in api/internal/models/order.go with `json:"customer_name"`, commit v2) and edit(repo, rel, from, to) (one exact replacement; panics when `from` is absent).
- engine/tests/model_breaks.rs: cases (a)-(g) of the acceptance through delta::graph_delta_vs_rev + model_breaks, printing the marker.

It is shared by DT.1o's engine test and DT.1p's engine / CLI / py tests. It is a data dir, not a substrate-gap fixture, so run.py's legacy-latest.json does not move.
