packets.rationale: The surface half of James's ruling 4 (tweaks-0.5.2.md, 2026-10-17): 'an inferred client <-> server model break shows in review / contract-breaks but blocks only for a FACT pairing or on opt-in'. DT.1o built the judge (contract_breaks::model_breaks). This packet makes both PR-time gates show it without letting an inferred row fail CI by default. Measured baseline (DT.1o's rationale, re-run by the verifier): on the two-commit examples-glia copy and on the fixture, `glia contract-breaks --base HEAD~1` printed pairs=0 and exit 0 (`--json` keys [absence, base, breaking, orphaned_clients, schemas]), and `glia review` exit 0 showed only the modified STRUCT. The opt-in uses check's vocabulary (engine/src/check.rs min_tier_of / is_blocking: fact | derived; heuristic never blocks; review.rs DB.3c's blocking vs advisory split), as `--models-min-tier`. It is not a separate boolean: one gate rule, and the same values a [[constraint]] min_tier takes. The default is fact, not check's DEFAULT_MIN_TIER derived, because the ruling makes inferred pairings advisory, and in 0.5.2 every HTTP / GraphQL pairing is DERIVED. The exit rules stay those of today's surfaces: contract-breaks exits 1 when `breaking` > 0 and review when `blocking`; an advisory model row reaches neither. Review lists only breaking model rows (a PR report). contract-breaks lists compatible ones too, unless --breaking-only, as it does for schema rows. The --with merge (CC.8c) is judged as well, so a typed client in another repo is covered (measured: with the fixture's api/ and web/ as two repos, HTTP_CALLS 3/3 pair across the merge).

1. ENGINE: contract_breaks.rs.
- breaks_of runs model_breaks_of(base, before, after_build, delta, &ModelBreakArgs { min_tier: args.models_min_tier }) after its unchanged `[contract-breaks] base=` eprintln, so the `[model-breaks]` line prints after it (and, with --with, before `[contract-breaks] clients=`).
- models = its rows; breaking_only drops the compatible ones (counted into `listed` for the absence's breaking_only note).
- breaking = breaking schema rows + orphaned clients + BLOCKING model rows. advisory = breaking model rows that do not block.
- absence is Some only when schemas, models and orphaned_clients are all empty. Its note is byte-identical to today's when no model exchange was judged; otherwise it gains '; <J> client <-> server model <exchange|exchanges> judged, none changed what a client reads or sends'. The CC.8a / b / c pins therefore hold.
- The `[contract-breaks] base=` line is unchanged: its status counts stay schema rows.
- The module doc gains INFERRED MODELS (the gate, the default, the flag), its ORDER section names `models`, and `breaking`'s doc says 'plus blocking model rows'.

2. ENGINE: review.rs.
- After the rule comparison, crate::contract_breaks::model_breaks_of over (rev.answer.base, rev.before.merged, rev.after, rev.delta). model_breaks = its breaking rows; compatible rows are contract-breaks' business. counts.model_breaks = their number.
- blocking = any new blocking violation || any blocking model row.
- render_markdown:
  - the headline gains ` | <M> model break(s)`, then ` (<A> advisory)` when A > 0, only when M > 0, so GOLDEN_NEW and every existing pin is unchanged;

A site is code(qname) followed by file:line of the change's field site, else the row side's; ` (at <base>)` marks an at_base site; `—` marks none. The table is cut by max_rows with `_(<shown> of <total>)_`, through push_table / code / text;
  - `unchanged` also requires no model break.
- The module doc's 'blocking' and Markers sections say the `[review] base=` line is unchanged: its `blocking=` is the combined gate, and the `[model-breaks]` line carries the model counts.

3. CLI contract-breaks.
- The flag doc: 'the weakest pairing tier at which an inferred client <-> server model break fails the gate: fact (the default; every pairing glia 0.5.2 infers is derived, so its rows are advisory) or derived; a heuristic pairing never fails it'.

Under the heading, an italic line: '_Inferred client <-> server models, judged against what the client reads or sends; a breaking row fails the gate only at or above `--models-min-tier` (<t>)._'. Then `| pairing | via | status | gate | tier | changed | rule | field | before | after | client | server |`, one line per change:
  - via = code(first exchange key) plus ` +<n>`;
  - gate = `blocking` / `advisory` on a breaking row, `—` on a compatible one;
  - a breaking rule is in bold (as contract_rows does);
  - sites as in review.
- `_(no contract change vs <rev>)_` only when models is empty too.
- The module doc's JSON key list and exit rule: 1 when `breaking` > 0; an advisory model row never fails it.

4. CLI review: the flag. The module doc: exit 1 also for a blocking model break; the JSON key list gains model_breaks.

5. pyo3: the kwarg is last in both functions. engine_args validates it against MODEL_MIN_TIERS (ValueError with the engine's message, before any build). The docstrings and module docs list `models` / `advisory` / `model_breaks`.

accept refuses a rule that fails rules::validate or defines no `violation` (verifier addition), while try still judges it (error -> drop). The alternative was to refuse it at parse_candidate, which would make try reject the whole candidate over one bad rule

DF.22c reverses CH.1b's stance that 'a concrete override is not IMPLEMENTS'. That stance was the CH.1b author's design note, not a recorded ruling by James (no ruling found in next-leap-0.5.1.md, leap-051-corrections.json or the 0.5.2 plan). The spec models dispatch as the method-level IMPLEMENTS hop (A6.6 / CA.3b / CH.1b); every consumer already follows it, and CE.1e's SCIP import maps METHOD -> METHOD is_implementation to IMPLEMENTS. The alternative is a method-level INHERITS_FROM plus a new hop in live_walk, gaps and tests_for. James decides before DF.22c's wave (W11)

Liveness stays node-level generous. IMPLEMENTS is a forward carry edge, so a reached override makes the member it overrides live, and the implementer step then makes every sibling override live, as interface and abstract pairs already do. A base reached only through an override's `super.m()` does the same. DF.22c makes only dead_symbol's dispatch rule exact for super calls; an edge-aware liveness is not specced

dead_symbol's dispatch rule stays node-level, as CH.1c's is. A call on an exactly typed receiver (`new T().m()`, a `new` local) vouches for T's overrides, although none can run there. Example: mem0's openai-llm.test.ts `new OpenAILLM(..)` local vouches for the DeepSeekLLM / LMStudioLLM overrides. That is moot on mem0, since their own tests call them, but it is a general imprecision. Separating exact-type receivers would need their own EVIDENCE rule
